Create `app/lib/credentialRules.ts` (`:653–731`, `:961–1063`, `:503–543`, `:614–640` verbatim with `export`; then the two new functions):

```ts
/**
 * Credential-family rules (architecture-07): the rule-set predicates, the
 * catalog date defaults, the confirmed-carryover window and the rule-review
 * words, moved verbatim from app/ITrackApp.tsx so the client, the packet and
 * every screen branch on one definition. `credentialFamily()` is the one
 * discriminator the screens switch on instead of re-branching the predicates.
 *
 * Pure: no React, DOM or D1 import; `today` is always a parameter. Imports
 * carry the `.js` suffix for `npm run build:lib-test` (`tsc --module
 * nodenext`); the instruments import is type-only, so no runtime edge points
 * from here at app/lib/instruments.ts.
 */
import type { CatalogRule, Credential } from "./workspaceTypes.js";
import type { InstrumentState } from "./instruments.js";
import { portalCarryoverLookbackMonths } from "./carryover.js";
import { addMonthsIso, addYearsIso } from "./dates.js";
import { isExpandedCertificationRuleSetId } from "./expandedCertifications.js";

export function isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("isc2-") ?? false;
}

export function isNremtCredential(credential: Credential | null | undefined) {
  return credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("nremt-") ?? false;
}

export function isCrcCredential(credential: Credential | null | undefined) {
  return credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("crcc-") ?? false;
}

export function isAbveCredential(credential: Credential | null | undefined) {
  return credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("abve-") ?? false;
}

export function isNremtCatalogRule(rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined) {
  return rule?.id.startsWith("nremt-") ?? false;
}

export function isFloridaMentalHealthCatalogRule(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
) {
  return rule?.id.startsWith("fl-lcsw-lmft-lmhc-") ?? false;
}

export function isCrccCatalogRule(rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined) {
  return rule?.id.startsWith("crcc-") ?? false;
}

export function isAbveCatalogRule(rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined) {
  return rule?.id.startsWith("abve-") ?? false;
}

export function isRehabilitationCertificationCatalogRule(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
) {
  return isCrccCatalogRule(rule) || isAbveCatalogRule(rule);
}

export function isExpandedCertificationCatalogRule(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
) {
  return isExpandedCertificationRuleSetId(rule?.id);
}

export function isExpandedCertificationCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return isExpandedCertificationRuleSetId(credential?.ruleSetId);
}

export function requiresOfficialCatalogDates(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    isNremtCatalogRule(rule) ||
    isFloridaMentalHealthCatalogRule(rule) ||
    isRehabilitationCertificationCatalogRule(rule) ||
    isExpandedCertificationCatalogRule(rule)
  );
}

export function nremtLevelKey(ruleSetId: string | null | undefined) {
  return /^nremt-(emr|emt|aemt|paramedic)-/.exec(ruleSetId ?? "")?.[1] ?? null;
}

export function currentNremtCatalogRule(
  catalog: CatalogRule[],
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  const level = nremtLevelKey(credential?.ruleSetId);
  if (!level) return null;
  return (
    catalog.find((rule) => rule.id.startsWith(`nremt-${level}-`)) ?? null
  );
}

export function isManagedPharmacistCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    credential?.profession === "Pharmacy" && credential.ruleSetId,
  );
}

export function isManagedNursingCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    credential?.profession === "Nursing" && credential.ruleSetId,
  );
}

export function isManagedDentalCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    credential?.profession === "Dental" && credential.ruleSetId,
  );
}

export function isManagedRehabilitationCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    credential?.profession === "Vocational Rehabilitation" &&
      (credential.ruleSetId?.startsWith("crcc-") ||
        credential.ruleSetId?.startsWith("abve-")),
  );
}

export function isCompliancePeriodCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  const ruleSetId = credential?.ruleSetId;
  return Boolean(
    ruleSetId &&
      (ruleSetId.startsWith("fl-insurance-producer-") ||
        ruleSetId.startsWith("ny-professional-classroom-teacher-") ||
        ruleSetId.startsWith("ny-professional-esol-bilingual-") ||
        ruleSetId.startsWith("nj-employed-teacher-annual-pd-") ||
        ruleSetId.startsWith("pa-professional-educator-act-48-")),
  );
}

export function isFloridaInsuranceComplianceCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("fl-insurance-producer-") ?? false
  );
}

export function isFloridaMentalHealthPhaseCredential(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    credential?.ruleSetId?.startsWith("fl-lcsw-lmft-lmhc-") ?? false
  );
}

export function requiresCurrentNextTemplate(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    isFloridaInsuranceComplianceCredential(credential) ||
    isFloridaMentalHealthPhaseCredential(credential)
  );
}

export function requiresOfficialNextPeriodAttestation(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential) ||
    isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential) ||
    isFloridaMentalHealthPhaseCredential(credential) ||
    isNremtCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedPharmacistCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedNursingCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedDentalCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedRehabilitationCredential(credential) ||
    isExpandedCertificationCredential(credential)
  );
}

export function requiresNonOverlappingNextPeriod(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return (
    isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential) ||
    isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential) ||
    isFloridaMentalHealthPhaseCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedPharmacistCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedNursingCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedDentalCredential(credential) ||
    isManagedRehabilitationCredential(credential) ||
    isExpandedCertificationCredential(credential)
  );
}

// Default cycle window for a new credential, anchored on the caller's local
// `today` (app/lib/dates.ts) rather than the UTC date. ABVE's fixed cycle is
// the one template with hard-coded dates.
export function defaultCatalogCycleStart(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
  today: string,
) {
  if (isAbveCatalogRule(rule)) return "2025-01-01";
  return rule
    ? addMonthsIso(addYearsIso(today, 1), -rule.cycleMonths)
    : addYearsIso(today, -1);
}

export function defaultCatalogDeadline(
  rule: CatalogRule | null | undefined,
  today: string,
) {
  return isAbveCatalogRule(rule) ? "2027-12-31" : addYearsIso(today, 1);
}

export function confirmedCarryoverWindowStart(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  if (!credential) return null;
  const lookbacks = credential.requirements.flatMap((requirement) => {
    if (
      requirement.isActive === false ||
      requirement.applicabilityStatus !== "applies" ||
      !requirement.ruleCategoryId
    ) {
      return [];
    }
    const months = portalCarryoverLookbackMonths(
      requirement.ruleCategoryId,
    );
    return months === null ? [] : [months];
  });
  return lookbacks.length
    ? addMonthsIso(credential.cycleStart, -Math.max(...lookbacks))
    : null;
}

export function ruleReviewLabel(reviewStatus?: string | null) {
  switch (reviewStatus) {
    case "verified":
      return "Official source verified";
    case "transition_rule_check_assigned_cycle":
      return "Transition rule · check assigned cycle";
    case "needs_review":
      return "Needs official review";
    case "source_linked_check_conditions":
      return "Source-linked · confirm conditions";
    default:
      return "Source-linked · review details";
  }
}

export function ruleReviewClass(reviewStatus?: string | null) {
  switch (reviewStatus) {
    case "verified":
      return "verified";
    case "transition_rule_check_assigned_cycle":
      return "transition";
    case "needs_review":
      return "needs-review";
    default:
      return "conditional";
  }
}

/**
 * The one family a credential belongs to, tested in this order (the first
 * predicate that matches wins — a Vocational Rehabilitation CRCC credential
 * is "crc", never "managed-rehab"). Screens switch on this instead of calling
 * the predicates one after another (architecture-07).
 */
export type CredentialFamily =
  | "isc2"
  | "nremt"
  | "crc"
  | "abve"
  | "fl-mental-health"
  | "compliance-period"
  | "managed-pharmacist"
  | "managed-nursing"
  | "managed-dental"
  | "managed-rehab"
  | "expanded"
  | "generic";

export function credentialFamily(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
): CredentialFamily {
  if (isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential)) return "isc2";
  if (isNremtCredential(credential)) return "nremt";
  if (isCrcCredential(credential)) return "crc";
  if (isAbveCredential(credential)) return "abve";
  if (isFloridaMentalHealthPhaseCredential(credential)) {
    return "fl-mental-health";
  }
  if (isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential)) return "compliance-period";
  if (isManagedPharmacistCredential(credential)) return "managed-pharmacist";
  if (isManagedNursingCredential(credential)) return "managed-nursing";
  if (isManagedDentalCredential(credential)) return "managed-dental";
  if (isManagedRehabilitationCredential(credential)) return "managed-rehab";
  if (isExpandedCertificationCredential(credential)) return "expanded";
  return "generic";
}

/**
 * The instrument state a rule-review status colours by, for the StatusPill
 * that replaces the legacy `.verified-chip` (ruleReviewClass stays for the
 * legacy markup until the last screen leaves ITrackApp.tsx).
 */
export function ruleReviewState(
  reviewStatus?: string | null,
): InstrumentState {
  switch (reviewStatus) {
    case "verified":
    case "transition_rule_check_assigned_cycle":
      return "on-track";
    case "needs_review":
      return "overdue";
    case "custom":
      return "none";
    default:
      return "due-soon";
  }
}
```

Create `app/lib/activityRules.ts` (`:545–593` and `:936–959`; `activityIsMutable`'s `credentials: Credential[]` → `readonly Credential[]`):

```ts
/**
 * Activity rules moved verbatim from app/ITrackApp.tsx: whether a completion
 * date fits a credential's cycle (or its confirmed-carryover window), the
 * allocations an activity carries (synthesised from the legacy top-level
 * fields when the payload has none), whether a record is still mutable, and
 * the prior-period carry-over test the Log sheet and the allocators share.
 *
 * Pure: no React, DOM or D1 import. Imports carry the `.js` suffix for
 * `npm run build:lib-test` (`tsc --module nodenext`).
 */
import type {
  Activity,
  ActivityAllocation,
  Credential,
  Requirement,
} from "./workspaceTypes.js";
import { portalCarryoverLookbackMonths } from "./carryover.js";
import { confirmedCarryoverWindowStart } from "./credentialRules.js";

export function activityDateFitsCredential(
  completionDate: string,
  credential: Credential,
) {
  if (
    completionDate >= credential.cycleStart &&
    completionDate <= credential.deadline
  ) {
    return true;
  }
  const carryoverStart = confirmedCarryoverWindowStart(credential);
  return Boolean(
    carryoverStart &&
      completionDate >= carryoverStart &&
      completionDate < credential.cycleStart,
  );
}

export function allocationsFor(activity: Activity): ActivityAllocation[] {
  if (activity.allocations?.length) return activity.allocations;
  if (!activity.credentialId || !activity.credentialName) return [];
  return [
    {
      id: `${activity.id}:${activity.credentialId}`,
      credentialId: activity.credentialId,
      credentialName: activity.credentialName,
      requirementId: activity.requirementId,
      categoryName: activity.categoryName,
      allocatedUnits: activity.allocatedUnits,
    },
  ];
}

export function activityIsMutable(
  activity: Activity,
  credentials: readonly Credential[],
) {
  const credentialStatusById = new Map(
    credentials.map((credential) => [credential.id, credential.status]),
  );
  return allocationsFor(activity).every((allocation) => {
    const status = credentialStatusById.get(allocation.credentialId);
    return status === "active" || status === "submitted";
  });
}

export function requirementRawEarned(requirement: Requirement) {
  return Number(requirement.rawEarned ?? requirement.earnedUnits ?? 0);
}

export function hasPortalConfirmedCarryover(
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    credential?.requirements.some(
      (requirement) =>
        requirement.isActive !== false &&
        requirement.applicabilityStatus !== "not_applicable" &&
        portalCarryoverLookbackMonths(requirement.ruleCategoryId) !== null,
    ),
  );
}

export function isPriorPeriodCarryoverEntry(
  completionDate: string | null | undefined,
  credential: Credential | null | undefined,
) {
  return Boolean(
    completionDate &&
      credential &&
      completionDate < credential.cycleStart &&
      hasPortalConfirmedCarryover(credential),
  );
}
```

Create `app/lib/nextAction.ts` (`:1079–1282`; the `today` parameter, `task.dueDate! < today` in place of `daysUntil(task.dueDate!) < 0`, and `dueDate`/`count` on the checklist and records returns — five edited lines, marked in the module comment):

```ts
/**
 * Home's "Best next action": one priority ladder over one credential, moved
 * verbatim from app/ITrackApp.tsx. The only edits are the `today` parameter
 * (the overdue-task test is `task.dueDate < today` — a YYYY-MM-DD string
 * comparison against the app's local today, so the clock never enters this
 * module; critic-01) and two optional fields on the result, `dueDate` and
 * `count`, so a screen can format the date and pluralise the count itself.
 *
 * Pure: no React, DOM or D1 import. Imports carry the `.js` suffix for
 * `npm run build:lib-test` (`tsc --module nodenext`).
 */
import type { Credential, GuidedAction } from "./workspaceTypes.js";
import {
  isCompliancePeriodCredential,
  isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential,
  isNremtCredential,
} from "./credentialRules.js";
import { compactNumber, formatDate } from "./format.js";
import {
  activeDentalCheckpoints,
  activeMinimums,
  requirementEarned,
  requirementStatus,
} from "./readiness.js";

export function bestNextAction(
  credential: Credential,
  missingEvidence: number,
  today: string,
): GuidedAction {
  if (credential.status === "renewed") {
    return {
      kind: "history",
      title: "Review the preserved record for this completed cycle",
      body: "Your credits, proof, submission, and acceptance remain together.",
      buttonLabel: "View cycle history",
    };
  }
  if (credential.status === "submitted") {
    if (isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential)) {
      return {
        kind: "acceptance",
        title: "Confirm the renewed cycle shown in your ISC2 dashboard",
        body: "Keep this cycle open until ISC2 displays the new certification dates.",
        buttonLabel: "Confirm renewed cycle",
      };
    }
    if (isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential)) {
      return {
        kind: "acceptance",
        title: "Confirm the next compliance period from the official record",
        body: "Keep this period open until you have verified the new compliance dates.",
        buttonLabel: "Start next period",
      };
    }
    if (isNremtCredential(credential)) {
      return {
        kind: "acceptance",
        title: "Confirm the renewed dates in your National Registry dashboard",
        body: "Use the same current level template and enter the cycle start and fixed expiration exactly as displayed.",
        buttonLabel: "Confirm renewed cycle",
      };
    }
    return {
      kind: "acceptance",
      title: "Record acceptance when your renewal is approved",
      body: "Keep the cycle open until the issuing organization confirms it.",
      buttonLabel: "Record acceptance",
    };
  }

  const unresolvedRequirement = credential.requirements.find(
    (item) => requirementStatus(item) === "needs_confirmation",
  );
  if (unresolvedRequirement) {
    return {
      kind: "conditions",
      title: `Confirm whether ${unresolvedRequirement.name} applies this cycle`,
      body: "Your readiness score stays cautious until this rule is resolved.",
      buttonLabel: "Review conditions",
    };
  }

  const classificationIssueCount = credential.classificationIssues?.length ?? 0;
  if (classificationIssueCount > 0) {
    return {
      kind: "records",
      title: `Classify ${classificationIssueCount} learning ${
        classificationIssueCount === 1 ? "record" : "records"
      }`,
      body: `${compactNumber(
        credential.unclassifiedUnits ?? 0,
      )} ${credential.unitLabel} are preserved but excluded until each classification conflict is resolved.`,
      buttonLabel: "Review records",
      count: classificationIssueCount,
    };
  }

  const overdueTask = credential.tasks.find(
    (task) =>
      task.status !== "completed" &&
      Boolean(task.dueDate) &&
      task.dueDate! < today,
  );
  if (overdueTask) {
    return {
      kind: "checklist",
      title: overdueTask.title,
      body: `This checklist step was due ${formatDate(overdueTask.dueDate)}.`,
      buttonLabel: "Open checklist",
      dueDate: overdueTask.dueDate!,
    };
  }

  if (missingEvidence > 0) {
    return {
      kind: "records",
      title: `Attach proof to ${missingEvidence} learning ${
        missingEvidence === 1 ? "record" : "records"
      }`,
      body: "A complete audit trail is as important as the credit total.",
      buttonLabel: "Review records",
      count: missingEvidence,
    };
  }

  const missingRequirement = activeMinimums(credential)
    .filter((item) => requirementEarned(item) < item.requiredUnits)
    .sort(
      (a, b) =>
        b.requiredUnits -
        requirementEarned(b) -
        (a.requiredUnits - requirementEarned(a)),
    )[0];

  if (missingRequirement) {
    const left =
      missingRequirement.requiredUnits - requirementEarned(missingRequirement);
    const overallRemaining = Math.max(
      0,
      credential.totalRequired - credential.totalEarned,
    );
    return {
      kind: "learning",
      title: `Complete ${compactNumber(left)} more ${missingRequirement.name} ${
        left === 1
          ? credential.unitLabel.replace(/s$/, "")
          : credential.unitLabel
      }`,
      body:
        overallRemaining === 0
          ? "Your overall total is met, but this active category minimum is still short."
          : `${compactNumber(overallRemaining)} ${credential.unitLabel} remain overall; prioritize this category.`,
      buttonLabel: "Log qualifying learning",
    };
  }

  const overallRemaining = Math.max(
    0,
    credential.totalRequired - credential.totalEarned,
  );
  if (overallRemaining > 0) {
    return {
      kind: "learning",
      title: `Complete ${compactNumber(overallRemaining)} more ${
        overallRemaining === 1
          ? credential.unitLabel.replace(/s$/, "")
          : credential.unitLabel
      }`,
      body: "Log completed learning as you go so the record stays current.",
      buttonLabel: "Add completed learning",
    };
  }

  const pendingDentalCheckpoint = activeDentalCheckpoints(credential).find(
    (requirement) => requirement.checkpointStatus !== "completed",
  );
  if (pendingDentalCheckpoint) {
    return {
      kind: "conditions",
      title: `Complete ${pendingDentalCheckpoint.name}`,
      body:
        "Save a concise certificate, card, portal, or assessment reference. This checkpoint does not add CE units.",
      buttonLabel: "Open requirements",
    };
  }

  const openTask = credential.tasks.find((task) => task.status !== "completed");
  if (openTask) {
    return {
      kind: "checklist",
      title: openTask.title,
      body: isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential)
        ? "Credits are covered. Finish this dashboard step before confirming renewal."
        : isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential)
          ? "Credits are covered. Finish this official-record step before closing the period."
          : isNremtCredential(credential)
            ? "Credits are covered. Complete the Training Officer or Medical Director verification required for Active status, or confirm the Inactive pathway, before applying."
          : "Credits are covered. Finish this packet step before submitting.",
      buttonLabel: "Open checklist",
      dueDate: openTask.dueDate ?? undefined,
    };
  }
  if (isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential)) {
    return {
      kind: "submission",
      title: "Check your ISC2 CPE and fee status in the dashboard",
      body: "Save an attested checkpoint, then wait for renewed dates after cycle end.",
      buttonLabel: "Save dashboard checkpoint",
    };
  }
  if (isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential)) {
    return {
      kind: "submission",
      title: "Verify this compliance period in the official record",
      body: "Save the official milestone before opening the next period.",
      buttonLabel: "Record compliance",
    };
  }
  if (isNremtCredential(credential)) {
    return {
      kind: "submission",
      title: "Verify the National Registry dashboard and submit",
      body: "Confirm accepted post-cap education, every NCCP component, status verification, and the current on-time or reinstatement path.",
      buttonLabel: "Save application record",
    };
  }
  return {
    kind: "submission",
    title: "Review and submit your renewal",
    body: "Your active minimums, overall credits, and checklist are complete.",
    buttonLabel: "Review submission",
  };
}
```

Create `app/lib/allocation.ts` (`:744–934`, `:10099–10107`, `:10146–10160` verbatim with `export`):

```ts
/**
 * The exact-allocation payload builders (NREMT components and topics, CRCC
 * credit types and approval) and the allocator amount helpers, moved verbatim
 * from app/ITrackApp.tsx. They read the allocator's FormData and throw the
 * sentence the sheet shows, so the Log, Reuse and Classify flows validate the
 * same way.
 *
 * Pure: no React or D1 import; `FormData` is a web standard Node 22 provides,
 * which is what lets tests/allocation.test.mjs drive them. Imports carry the
 * `.js` suffix for `npm run build:lib-test` (`tsc --module nodenext`).
 */
import type {
  CrcApprovalPayload,
  Credential,
  Requirement,
  RequirementMatchPayload,
} from "./workspaceTypes.js";
import { compactNumber } from "./format.js";
import { requirementStatus } from "./readiness.js";

export function crcRequirementMatchPayload(
  form: FormData,
  credential: Credential,
  allocatedUnits: number,
): RequirementMatchPayload[] {
  const requirements = credential.requirements.filter(
    (requirement) =>
      requirementStatus(requirement) === "applies" &&
      requirement.isActive !== false,
  );
  const general = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-general"),
  );
  const professionalDevelopment = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-professional-development"),
  );
  const ethics = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-ethics"),
  );
  if (!general || !professionalDevelopment || !ethics) {
    throw new Error(
      "This CRC template is missing an exact-allocation requirement. Refresh the credential before saving.",
    );
  }

  const amountFor = (requirement: Requirement) => {
    const value = Number(form.get(`requirementMatch:${requirement.id}`) ?? 0);
    if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
      throw new Error(`Enter a valid clock-hour amount for ${requirement.name}.`);
    }
    if (value > allocatedUnits + 0.0001) {
      throw new Error(
        `${requirement.name} cannot exceed the ${compactNumber(
          allocatedUnits,
        )} clock hours applied to this CRC.`,
      );
    }
    return value;
  };

  const generalUnits = amountFor(general);
  const professionalDevelopmentUnits = amountFor(professionalDevelopment);
  const ethicsUnits = amountFor(ethics);
  if (
    Math.abs(
      generalUnits + professionalDevelopmentUnits - allocatedUnits,
    ) > 0.0001
  ) {
    throw new Error(
      `General / Other Accepted CRC Credit and Professional Development must total ${compactNumber(
        allocatedUnits,
      )} clock hours.`,
    );
  }
  if (ethicsUnits > generalUnits + 0.0001) {
    throw new Error(
      "Ethics overlaps General / Other Accepted CRC Credit and cannot exceed the General amount.",
    );
  }

  return [
    { requirementId: general.id, matchedUnits: generalUnits },
    {
      requirementId: professionalDevelopment.id,
      matchedUnits: professionalDevelopmentUnits,
    },
    { requirementId: ethics.id, matchedUnits: ethicsUnits },
  ].filter((match) => match.matchedUnits > 0);
}

export function crcApprovalPayload(form: FormData): CrcApprovalPayload {
  const approvalType = String(form.get("crcApprovalType") ?? "");
  if (
    approvalType !== "pre_approved" &&
    approvalType !== "post_approved"
  ) {
    throw new Error("Choose the CRCC pre-approved or post-approved pathway.");
  }
  const programReference = String(
    form.get("crcProgramReference") ?? "",
  ).trim();
  if (!programReference) {
    throw new Error(
      "Enter the CRCC approval number or post-approval program reference.",
    );
  }
  if (form.get("crcApprovalAttested") !== "on") {
    throw new Error(
      "Confirm that the activity and entered hours are accepted by CRCC.",
    );
  }
  return {
    crcApprovalType: approvalType,
    crcProgramReference: programReference,
    crcApprovalAttested: true,
  };
}

export function nremtRequirementMatchPayload(
  form: FormData,
  credential: Credential,
  allocatedUnits: number,
): RequirementMatchPayload[] {
  const requirements = credential.requirements.filter(
    (requirement) =>
      requirementStatus(requirement) === "applies" &&
      requirement.isActive !== false,
  );
  const amountFor = (requirement: Requirement) => {
    const value = Number(form.get(`requirementMatch:${requirement.id}`) ?? 0);
    if (!Number.isFinite(value) || value < 0) {
      throw new Error(
        `Enter a valid accepted-credit amount for ${requirement.name}.`,
      );
    }
    if (value > allocatedUnits + 0.0001) {
      throw new Error(
        `${requirement.name} cannot exceed the ${compactNumber(
          allocatedUnits,
        )} credits applied to this credential.`,
      );
    }
    return value;
  };
  const national = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-national"),
  );
  const local = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-local"),
  );
  const individual = requirements.find((requirement) =>
    requirement.ruleCategoryId?.endsWith("-individual"),
  );
  if (!national || !local || !individual) {
    throw new Error(
      "This National Registry template is missing a component requirement. Refresh the credential before saving.",
    );
  }

  const nationalUnits = amountFor(national);
  const localUnits = amountFor(local);
  const individualUnits = amountFor(individual);
  const componentTotal = nationalUnits + localUnits + individualUnits;
  if (Math.abs(componentTotal - allocatedUnits) > 0.0001) {
    throw new Error(
      `National, Local/State, and Individual must total ${compactNumber(
        allocatedUnits,
      )} credits.`,
    );
  }

  const nationalTopics = requirements.filter(
    (requirement) =>
      requirement.relation === "nested" &&
      requirement.parentRequirementId === national.id,
  );
  const topicTotal = nationalTopics.reduce(
    (sum, requirement) => sum + amountFor(requirement),
    0,
  );
  if (Math.abs(topicTotal - nationalUnits) > 0.0001) {
    throw new Error(
      `The five National topic amounts must total ${compactNumber(
        nationalUnits,
      )} National credits.`,
    );
  }

  const overlapping = requirements.filter(
    (requirement) => requirement.relation === "overlapping",
  );
  for (const requirement of overlapping) {
    if (amountFor(requirement) > nationalUnits + 0.0001) {
      throw new Error(
        `${requirement.name} is overlapping National content and cannot exceed the National amount.`,
      );
    }
  }
  if (form.get("acceptedEducationAttested") !== "on") {
    throw new Error(
      "Confirm that the provider, course, and post-cap credit are accepted by the National Registry.",
    );
  }

  return requirements
    .map((requirement) => ({
      requirementId: requirement.id,
      matchedUnits: amountFor(requirement),
    }))
    .filter((match) => match.matchedUnits > 0);
}

/*
 * These forms are exact to the entered step — CRC hours go to 0.01 — so the
 * tally must not borrow compactNumber's single-decimal rounding, which would
 * report 2.25 as "2.3" and a 0.05 shortfall as "0.1". Rounding at four places
 * removes float noise and nothing else.
 */
export function allocationFigure(value: number) {
  return String(Number(value.toFixed(4)));
}

export function seedAllocationAmounts(initialMatches: RequirementMatchPayload[]) {
  const seeded: Record<string, string> = {};
  for (const match of initialMatches) {
    seeded[match.requirementId] = String(Number(match.matchedUnits));
  }
  return seeded;
}

export function allocationAmount(
  amounts: Record<string, string>,
  requirementId: string,
) {
  const parsed = Number(amounts[requirementId] ?? 0);
  return Number.isFinite(parsed) ? parsed : 0;
}
```

Create `app/lib/format.ts` (`:465–480`, `:595–612`, `:642–651`, `:7504–7519` verbatim with `export`; `daysUntil`, `credentialCountdown`, `credentialInstrumentState`, `credentialRingState`, `cycleCountdownLabel` and `dayPart` with the instant as a parameter — their bodies otherwise unchanged):

```ts
/**
 * Formatters and the clock-taking countdown/state helpers, moved verbatim
 * from app/ITrackApp.tsx (architecture-07: one copy for the screens, the
 * store and the packet). The four helpers that used to read `Date.now()` /
 * `new Date()` take the instant as an argument (`nowMs` / `now`), so the
 * module is pure and the clock read stays in ITrackApp.tsx's module-level
 * `…Now` wrappers, outside every render body (react-hooks/purity, critic-01).
 *
 * Imports carry the `.js` suffix for `npm run build:lib-test` (`tsc --module
 * nodenext`).
 */
import type {
  ActivityAllocation,
  CatalogCategory,
  Credential,
} from "./workspaceTypes.js";
import {
  isCompliancePeriodCredential,
  isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential,
} from "./credentialRules.js";
import { cycleCountdown, isClosedCycle } from "./cycles.js";
import { ringStateOf, stateOf, type InstrumentState } from "./instruments.js";
import { daysUntilDate } from "./readiness.js";

export function formatDate(value?: string | null, options?: Intl.DateTimeFormatOptions) {
  if (!value) return "Not set";
  const parsed = new Date(`${value.slice(0, 10)}T12:00:00`);
  if (Number.isNaN(parsed.getTime())) return value;
  return new Intl.DateTimeFormat("en-US", {
    month: "short",
    day: "numeric",
    year: "numeric",
    ...options,
  }).format(parsed);
}

export function formatFileSize(bytes: number) {
  if (bytes < 1_048_576) return `${Math.max(1, Math.round(bytes / 1024))} KB`;
  return `${(bytes / 1_048_576).toFixed(1)} MB`;
}

/** Whole days to the end of the deadline day (readiness.daysUntilDate) at `nowMs`. */
export function daysUntil(value: string, nowMs: number) {
  return daysUntilDate(value, nowMs);
}

// The clock is the caller's: ITrackApp.tsx passes Date.now() from a
// module-level wrapper, never from a render body.
export function credentialCountdown(credential: Credential, nowMs: number) {
  return cycleCountdown(credential, nowMs);
}

// The instrument state a pill or bar colours by (overdue / due soon / on
// track / submitted / renewed) and the ring state (credits complete wins)
// take the same explicit instant.
export function credentialInstrumentState(
  credential: Credential,
  nowMs: number,
): InstrumentState {
  return stateOf(credential, nowMs);
}

export function credentialRingState(
  credential: Credential,
  nowMs: number,
): InstrumentState {
  return ringStateOf(credential, nowMs);
}

export function allocationCategoryLabel(allocation: ActivityAllocation) {
  if (allocation.categoryNames?.length) {
    return allocation.categoryNames.join(" · ");
  }
  return allocation.categoryName ?? "General";
}

export function catalogCategorySummary(category: CatalogCategory) {
  const qualifier =
    category.applicability === "conditional" ? " if applicable" : "";
  if (category.kind === "informational") {
    return `Track ${category.name}${qualifier}`;
  }
  const units = compactNumber(category.requiredUnits);
  const prefix =
    category.kind === "maximum" ? `Up to ${units}` : `${units}`;
  return `${prefix} ${category.name}${qualifier}`;
}

export function compactNumber(value: number) {
  return Number.isInteger(value) ? String(value) : value.toFixed(1);
}

export function firstName(displayName: string) {
  const candidate = displayName.includes("@")
    ? displayName.split("@")[0]
    : displayName.split(/\s+/)[0];
  return candidate || "there";
}

export function cycleStatusLabel(credential: Credential) {
  if (isClosedCycle(credential)) return "history";
  if (
    credential.status === "submitted" &&
    isIsc2AutomaticRenewalCredential(credential)
  ) {
    return "awaiting ISC2 renewal";
  }
  if (
    credential.status === "submitted" &&
    isCompliancePeriodCredential(credential)
  ) {
    return "compliance recorded";
  }
  return credential.status;
}

export function cycleCountdownLabel(credential: Credential, nowMs: number) {
  const countdown = credentialCountdown(credential, nowMs);
  if (countdown.kind === "closed") {
    return `Renewed ${formatDate(countdown.acceptedAt)}`;
  }
  return `${Math.abs(countdown.days)} days ${
    countdown.kind === "overdue" ? "overdue" : "left"
  }`;
}

export function dayPart(now: Date) {
  const hour = now.getHours();
  if (hour < 12) return "morning";
  if (hour < 18) return "afternoon";
  return "evening";
}
```

```ts
/**
 * The pending-action keys, moved verbatim from app/ITrackApp.tsx. A key names
 * the one control that greys out while its write is on the wire (see the
 * FORM_ACTION_KEY note below). `REMINDERS_ACTION_KEY` and `reminderActionKey`
 * are declared here now for the Account reminders form and Home's check-in
 * rows, so this file is written once.
 *
 * Pure and import-free; compiled by `npm run build:lib-test` for
 * tests/action-keys.test.mjs.
 */

/*
 * In-flight mutations are tracked by key so the control that was actually used
 * is the only thing that changes state while the write is on the wire. Modal
 * and sheet submits share FORM_ACTION_KEY, so a background row write never
 * greys out an open sheet's Save button, and a sheet submit never freezes the
 * rows behind it. Nothing here writes optimistically: the workspace is still
 * only trusted after the server confirms and the refetch lands.
 */
export const FORM_ACTION_KEY = "form";

// The time-zone offer banner's own key: its Use button greys out while the
// preference write is on the wire without freezing any open sheet.
export const TIME_ZONE_ACTION_KEY = "time-zone";

// Where "Not now" is remembered — per account and per device zone, under the
// `itrack:` prefix (the `license-lantern:` draft prefix is load-bearing and
// stays draft-only) — so the offer returns only after a genuine move.
export function zoneOfferStorageKey(draftStorageNamespace: string) {
  return `itrack:time-zone-offer:v1:${draftStorageNamespace}`;
}

export function taskActionKey(taskId: string) {
  return `task:${taskId}`;
}

export function requirementActionKey(requirementId: string) {
  return `requirement:${requirementId}`;
}

export function activityActionKey(activityId: string) {
  return `activity:${activityId}`;
}

export function credentialActionKey(id: string) {
  return `credential:${id}`;
}

export function questActionKey(questKey: string) {
  return `quest:${questKey}`;
}

export const WEEKLY_GOAL_ACTION_KEY = "weeklyGoal";

// The Account screen's inline reminders form (was the "Due-date check-ins"
// modal) keys its save by this so a row write never greys out the form.
export const REMINDERS_ACTION_KEY = "reminders";

// A check-in row's Snooze / Done buttons go pending under the row's own key.
export function reminderActionKey(reminderKey: string) {
  return `reminder:${reminderKey}`;
}
```

### Task 2: Copy and error map: app/lib/copy.ts (ERROR_COPY for every server code, describeApiError, CONFLICT_CODES, checkInTitle/checkInBody, ledgerLede, DIALOG_NAMES), ErrorSummary `detail` disclosure, tests/copy.test.mjs code-coverage proof

**Rationale:** spec §6's copy rules — "errors say what happened and what to do; server strings are never shown raw", "check-in titles ≤ 9 words", "no 'Today'", "no 'countable units' / 'classification gaps' — say 'credits that count' / 'credits still needed'" — and §9 Unit ("node:test for … extracted `app/lib/*` modules"). Today every failed save reaches the user as the server's own sentence: `runAction` (`app/ITrackApp.tsx:2259-2343`) throws `new Error(result.error || "That update didn’t save.")` at `:2320` and, for the ten conflict codes it lists at `:2295-2305`, the composite `` `${result.error || …} The latest version is loaded; reopen it to continue.` `` at `:2313-2317`; the same string lands in the page banner (`:3958-3966`) and in whichever of the seven `<ModalError title message={error} />` sites is open (`:4650, 5243, 5440, 5738, 5891, 6072, 6239`) — the two-alerts-plus-raw-string failure app-ux-24 photographed ("Something needs attention — Simulated server failure" beside "This task did not save — Simulated server failure") and the one-global-`error` design architecture-04 names; app-ux-M-01 is the same path fed a non-JSON body. The server vocabulary is `class RequestError(message, status = 400, code = "invalid_request")` (`app/api/workspace/route.ts:400-408`), `EvidenceApiError` with the same defaults (`app/api/evidence/_shared.ts:11-19`), `packetError(request, sentence, code, status)` (`app/api/export/packet/route.ts:26-66`) and bare `code: "…"` JSON bodies in the export and catalog routes — 195 distinct codes across the eight files under `app/api/` at `c6b1fe4` (`find app/api -name '*.ts'` lists exactly `catalog/route.ts`, `evidence/_shared.ts`, `evidence/[id]/download/route.ts`, `evidence/[id]/route.ts`, `evidence/route.ts`, `export/packet/route.ts`, `export/route.ts`, `workspace/route.ts`), 78 of the `RequestError` throws carrying no third argument (the `invalid_request` default). Nothing on the client maps a code to copy: `app/lib/apiResponse.ts` only classifies a 401 as `session-ended` and a non-JSON body as `unexpected` (its two sentences are pinned by `tests/api-response.test.mjs:36-39` and are reused here, never retyped). Check-in titles are server strings too: `app/lib/reminders.ts:301-388` builds a task check-in's title from the stored `checklist_tasks.title` verbatim, and those titles come from `db/catalog/*.ts`'s `*_RENEWAL_TASK_COPY_BINDINGS` (177 titles; 164 exceed nine words, the 20-word NREMT case app-ux-11 photographed) plus `route.ts`'s `PHARMACIST_RENEWAL_TASK_COPY` (`:255-306`, 18 titles) and inline task builders (44 `title: "…"` literals) — catalog content is governance (spec §11), so the ≤ 9-word rule is met by deriving the title from the task's kind and keeping the full title in the body (`checkInTitle`/`checkInBody`), which Task 8 mounts. `ErrorSummary` (`app/components/Form.tsx:301-355`) is the one alert a form shows (a11y-09, Wave 3 Task 7): it focuses itself when its `announcement` (`errors.map(e => e.message).join("\n")`, `:318`) changes, so the server sentence must travel outside that string — the "Technical details" `<details>` the ErrorFallback already uses (`app/components/ErrorBoundary.tsx:80-83`, pinned by `tests/e2e/error-surfaces.spec.ts:38,71`). The disclosure's ink pairings are claimed in `tokens.css` (`:18-22`: every ink clears AA on every soft fill, `--ink-muted` 5.7:1 on `--state-overdue-soft`), its `summary` gets the global ring (`app/globals.css:494` `:focus-visible`) and the tap floor (`--tap-min`), and the route-level styleguide axe audit runs on load (`tests/e2e/axe.spec.ts:62-69`) before any Save — hence one added axe case that fails the sample form and audits the summary closed and open. Everything below was run before it was written: `app/lib/copy.ts` and `tests/copy.test.mjs` compile under `tsc --module nodenext --target es2022` (the `build:lib-test` flags) and under the project's strict `tsconfig.json` settings, lint clean through `eslint.config.mjs` (`eslint --stdin-filename`), and pass 7/7 with every one of the 195 emitted codes covered; the `Form.tsx`, `Styleguide.tsx`, `primitives.spec.ts` and `axe.spec.ts` edits typecheck and lint the same way; the CSS block audits `0 claims, 0 failing, 0 literals` through `tools/contrast-audit.mjs`'s `auditStylesheet` and carries no px `font-size`.

**Decisions (binding for Tasks 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and 16):** (1) `ERROR_COPY` is a flat object with ONE key per literal code (the test enumerates the literals the API emits, so a new server code fails loudly instead of inheriting); codes that share a family share one `ErrorCopy` object (`ERROR_COPY.activity_version_conflict === ERROR_COPY.task_version_conflict`), the map is `Object.freeze`d and looked up with `Object.hasOwn` so a prototype key (`"constructor"`) is not a code. The copy table's `*_` families expand to the literal codes the extraction finds (`*_next_template_not_selectable` → crcc/dental/expanded_certification/nursing/pharmacist; `*_standard_cycle_dates_required` → dental/nursing/pharmacist; `*_next_cycle_dates_required` → crcc/dental/nursing/pharmacist; `*_template_eligibility_required` → dental, dental_next, expanded_certification, expanded_certification_next, nursing, nursing_next, pharmacist, pharmacist_next; `*_current_template_unavailable` → crcc/dental/expanded_certification/nursing/pharmacist; `*_next_template_unavailable` → nremt). (2) Two codes the API emits are absent from copy-table section J; both take an existing family's sentences (no new prose — the table is the only source of strings) and the raw server sentence stays readable in the disclosure: `isc2_renewal_before_cycle_end` (`route.ts:10508-10511`, "ISC2 renewal cannot be confirmed before the current certification cycle ends.") → the date-window family ("That date is outside the window this step allows."); `nremt_current_template_required` (`route.ts:764, 802`, the credential lacks the current National Registry component structure — "Create or roll into the current National Registry template") → the template-unavailable family beside its sibling `nremt_next_template_required`, which the table already places there. (3) Seven keys are in the map before their code exists: `invalid_date`, `invalid_format`, `invalid_quiet_hours` (Task 4), `confirm_required`, `internal_only`, `demo_workspace` (Task 13), `export_too_large` (Task 15) — the test asserts map ⊇ emitted, so those tasks add no copy. (4) `describeApiError` is applied only to API failures (the three `readApiResponse` kinds); an `Error` a client validator or an allocator builder (Task 1's `app/lib/allocation.ts`) throws is user copy already and is shown as it is — never passed through the map. `code` is `null` for the two non-JSON kinds (only a JSON body carries a server token; the store branches on `kind` for `session-ended`); `detail` is the raw `error` string, or the first 300 characters of a non-JSON body. (5) `CONFLICT_CODES` has seventeen members — today's ten (`:2295-2305`) plus the seven sibling state-changed codes the same server paths emit (`acceptance_state_changed`, `acceptance_activity_state_changed`, `submission_state_changed`, `requirement_state_changed`, `evidence_changed`, `evidence_upload_conflict`, `quest_week_changed`); every member's copy has `recovery: "reopen"`, and `cycle_closed` and `credential_archived` keep their own sentences over the family's. (6) `checkInTitle`: kind `deadline` → `Renewal due {short date}` / `Compliance due …` (from `reminder.compliance`); kind `acceptance` → `reminder.title` (the three server strings are 6, 9 and 3 words); kind `task` with `task === null` → `reminder.title`; `task.isPersonal` → `task.title` verbatim (the row clamps it; the rule covers the titles Home authors); managed kind `review` → "Confirm renewal dates and status", `progress` → "Finish required credits and training", `submission` → "Record the submission"; any other kind → `reminder.title`. `checkInBody`: acceptance → `{credentialName} · awaiting acceptance`; a task of one of the three managed kinds → `{credentialName} · due {long date} · {task.title}` (nothing the catalog says is lost); else `{credentialName} · due {long date}`. Both formatters are parameters — Task 8 passes `formatDate` bound to its options — so the module has no `Intl`, no zone and no `./format.js` import (the skeleton lists `./format.js` as the only other permitted import; it turns out unused). The `Reminder` type is imported as a type from Task 1's `./workspaceTypes.js`, which the emitted ESM does not import (type imports are erased). (7) `CheckInTask.kind` is spelled `string` — the union `"review" | "progress" | "submission" | string` collapses to `string` in TypeScript — with the three managed kinds named in the doc comment; a `RenewalTask` (`kind: string; isPersonal: boolean; title: string`) satisfies the shape structurally. One needs credits before November." is the fixture. (9) `ErrorSummary.detail` renders as `<details className="error-summary-detail"><summary>Technical details</summary><pre>{detail}</pre></details>` after the `<ul>`, inside the `role="alert"` div; `announcement` stays `errors.map(e => e.message).join("\n")` so `detail` never re-triggers the focus effect; the disclosure is closed by default and nothing opens it; `ModalError` stays as it is (Task 5 deletes it with its last caller).
```ts
export type ErrorCopy = { what: string; next: string; recovery: "retry" | "reopen" | "reload" | "sign-in" | "none" };
export const FALLBACK_ERROR: ErrorCopy;            // "That change didn’t save." · "Try again. If it keeps happening, reload the page." · retry
export const SESSION_ENDED_ERROR: ErrorCopy;       // what = SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE · "Reload and sign in to continue." · sign-in
export const UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR: ErrorCopy; // what = UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE · "Try again in a moment." · retry
export const OFFLINE_ERROR: ErrorCopy;             // "You’re offline." · "Your draft stays in this browser. Reconnect to save." · none
export const SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR: ErrorCopy;  // "iTrack is temporarily unavailable." · "Try again in a moment. Nothing was changed." · retry
export const ERROR_COPY: Readonly<Record<string, ErrorCopy>>;   // 202 keys: the 195 codes the API emits at c6b1fe4 + the seven later-task codes
export const CONFLICT_CODES: ReadonlySet<string>;               // 17 codes (decision 5)
export function isConflictCode(code: string | null | undefined): boolean;
export type ApiFailure =
  | { kind: "session-ended" }
  | { kind: "unexpected"; status: number; text: string }
  | { kind: "json"; status: number; code?: string; error?: string };
export type DescribedError = ErrorCopy & { code: string | null; detail: string | null };
export function describeApiError(failure: ApiFailure): DescribedError;
//   json → ERROR_COPY[code] ?? (status >= 500 ? SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR : FALLBACK_ERROR), code = failure.code ?? null, detail = failure.error ?? null;
//   unexpected → UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR, code null, detail = text.slice(0, 300); session-ended → SESSION_ENDED_ERROR, code null, detail null.
export function errorLine(copy: ErrorCopy): string;             // `${what} ${next}` — toasts and the page banner
export const CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT = 9;
export function wordCount(text: string): number;                // whitespace-split after trim; "" → 0
export type CheckInTask = { kind: string; isPersonal: boolean; title: string } | null;   // a RenewalTask fits; null = the task is gone
export function checkInTitle(
  reminder: Pick<Reminder, "kind" | "title" | "eventDate" | "credentialName"> & { compliance: boolean },
  task: CheckInTask,
  formatShortDate: (iso: string) => string,                     // Task 8: (iso) => formatDate(iso, { month: "short", day: "numeric" })
): string;
export function checkInBody(
  reminder: Pick<Reminder, "kind" | "credentialName" | "eventDate">,
  task: CheckInTask,
  formatLongDate: (iso: string) => string,                      // Task 8: formatDate
): string;
export function numberWord(n: number): string;                  // "No", "One" … "Nine"; else String(n)
export function ledgerLede(input: { rows: number; needing: number; overdue: number; soonestMonth: string | null }): string;
```

```js
// `app/lib/copy.ts` is the one place a server code becomes a sentence (spec
// §6 copy rules; app-ux-24, architecture-04) and the home of the string
// helpers more than one screen shares — the check-in title/body rules, the
// ledger lede, the dialog names. It is pure, so it is tested here against
// the ESM that `npm run build:lib-test` emits, exactly like
// tests/instruments.test.mjs. The coverage cases read app/api/**/*.ts and
// db/catalog/*.ts as TEXT: the architecture-03 guard bans client sources
// (ITrackApp.tsx, styles/, components/, screens/), not the API or the
// catalog, so a new server code or a new managed task title fails here,
// not in a user's browser.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { readFileSync, readdirSync, statSync } from "node:fs";
import { join } from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";
import { fileURLToPath } from "node:url";

import {
  SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE,
  UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE,
} from "../.test-build/apiResponse.js";
import {
  CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT,
  CONFLICT_CODES,
  DIALOG_NAMES,
  ERROR_COPY,
  FALLBACK_ERROR,
  OFFLINE_ERROR,
  SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR,
  SESSION_ENDED_ERROR,
  UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR,
  checkInBody,
  checkInTitle,
  describeApiError,
  errorLine,
  isConflictCode,
  ledgerLede,
  numberWord,
  wordCount,
} from "../.test-build/copy.js";

const ROOT = fileURLToPath(new URL("../", import.meta.url));

function walk(dir, out = []) {
  for (const entry of readdirSync(dir)) {
    const full = join(dir, entry);
    if (statSync(full).isDirectory()) walk(full, out);
    else if (/\.ts$/.test(entry)) out.push(full);
  }
  return out;
}

// The arguments of a call whose opening parenthesis is at `openParen`:
// scanned to the matching `)` honouring string, template and nested
// brackets, then split on top-level commas. `new RequestError(` calls run
// over several lines and carry template literals, so a one-line regex
// cannot read their third argument.
function callArguments(source, openParen) {
  const args = [];
  let current = "";
  let depth = 0;
  let quote = null;
  for (let i = openParen; i < source.length; i += 1) {
    const ch = source[i];
    if (quote) {
      current += ch;
      if (ch === "\\") {
        current += source[i + 1] ?? "";
        i += 1;
      } else if (ch === quote) {
        quote = null;
      }
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === '"' || ch === "'" || ch === "`") {
      quote = ch;
      current += ch;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "(" || ch === "[" || ch === "{") {
      depth += 1;
      if (depth === 1) continue; // the call's own "("
      current += ch;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === ")" || ch === "]" || ch === "}") {
      depth -= 1;
      if (depth === 0) {
        args.push(current.trim());
        return args;
      }
      current += ch;
      continue;
    }
    if (ch === "," && depth === 1) {
      args.push(current.trim());
      current = "";
      continue;
    }
    current += ch;
  }
  return args;
}

// Every code the API can answer with: (i) the third argument of every
// `new RequestError(` / `new EvidenceApiError(` call when it is a string
// literal (a missing third argument is the classes' "invalid_request"
// default, not a code); (ii) every `code: "…"` literal (the issue objects,
// errorResponse's synthesised codes, the export/catalog JSON bodies);
// (iii) the packet route's `packetError(request, "<sentence>", "<code>", …)`.
function apiErrorCodes() {
  const codes = new Set(["invalid_request"]);
  for (const file of walk(join(ROOT, "app/api"))) {
    const source = readFileSync(file, "utf8");
    for (const match of source.matchAll(/new (?:RequestError|EvidenceApiError)\s*\(/g)) {
      const third = callArguments(source, match.index + match[0].length - 1)[2];
      const literal = third && /^"([a-z0-9_]+)"$/.exec(third);
      if (literal) codes.add(literal[1]);
    }
    for (const match of source.matchAll(/\bcode:\s*"([a-z0-9_]+)"/g)) codes.add(match[1]);
    for (const match of source.matchAll(/packetError\(\s*request,\s*"[^"]*",\s*"([a-z0-9_]+)"/g)) {
      codes.add(match[1]);
    }
  }
  return codes;
}

// Every managed checklist-task title: the four-tuple rows of the catalog's
// *_TASK_COPY_BINDINGS (id, review, progress, submission — a trailing comma
// closes each row), the pharmacist map's three-tuples in route.ts, and the
// inline `title: "…"` literals of the task builders in route.ts.
function managedTaskTitles() {
  const titles = [];
  const tuple4 = /\[\s*"[^"]+",\s*"([^"]+)",\s*"([^"]+)",\s*"([^"]+)",?\s*\]/g;
  for (const name of readdirSync(join(ROOT, "db/catalog")).filter((entry) => /\.ts$/.test(entry))) {
    const source = readFileSync(join(ROOT, "db/catalog", name), "utf8");
    for (const match of source.matchAll(tuple4)) titles.push(match[1], match[2], match[3]);
  }
  const route = readFileSync(join(ROOT, "app/api/workspace/route.ts"), "utf8");
  const pharmacistStart = route.indexOf("const PHARMACIST_RENEWAL_TASK_COPY");
  const pharmacistEnd = route.indexOf("const NURSING_RENEWAL_TASK_COPY", pharmacistStart);
  assert.ok(pharmacistStart > 0 && pharmacistEnd > pharmacistStart, "route.ts still declares the pharmacist task copy");
  const pharmacist = route.slice(pharmacistStart, pharmacistEnd);
  for (const match of pharmacist.matchAll(/\[\s*"([^"]+)",\s*"([^"]+)",\s*"([^"]+)",?\s*\]/g)) {
    titles.push(match[1], match[2], match[3]);
  }
  for (const match of route.matchAll(/\btitle:\s*(?:\n\s*)?"([^"]+)"/g)) titles.push(match[1]);
  return titles;
}

const NAMED = {
  FALLBACK_ERROR,
  OFFLINE_ERROR,
  SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR,
  SESSION_ENDED_ERROR,
  UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR,
};

const BANNED_WORDS = /\b(Today|ChatGPT|OpenAI|countable|classification gaps?|tracked gaps?|XP|quest|Pro|beta|tier)\b/;
const CODE_SHAPED = /\b[a-z]+_[a-z_]+\b/;
const RECOVERIES = new Set(["retry", "reopen", "reload", "sign-in", "none"]);

test("every error code the API can emit has copy", () => {
  const codes = apiErrorCodes();
  // 195 at c6b1fe4; a broken extraction would pass vacuously without a floor.
  assert.ok(codes.size >= 170, `extracted only ${codes.size} codes from app/api/**`);
  const missing = [...codes].filter((code) => !Object.hasOwn(ERROR_COPY, code)).sort();
  assert.deepEqual(missing, [], "codes the API emits without an ERROR_COPY entry");
  for (const key of Object.keys(ERROR_COPY)) {
    assert.match(key, /^[a-z0-9_]+$/, `${key}: keys are the server's own codes`);
  }
});

test("no copy entry is a raw server sentence", () => {
  const entries = [...Object.entries(NAMED), ...Object.entries(ERROR_COPY)];
  assert.ok(entries.length > 170, "walked the named errors and the map");
  for (const [key, copy] of entries) {
    for (const part of ["what", "next"]) {
      const text = copy[part];
      assert.equal(typeof text, "string", `${key}.${part} is a string`);
      assert.match(text, /\.$/, `${key}.${part} ends with a period: ${JSON.stringify(text)}`);
      assert.doesNotMatch(text, BANNED_WORDS, `${key}.${part} uses a banned word`);
      assert.doesNotMatch(text, CODE_SHAPED, `${key}.${part} leaks a code-shaped token`);
    }
    assert.ok(wordCount(copy.what) <= 12, `${key}.what runs over 12 words: ${JSON.stringify(copy.what)}`);
    assert.ok(RECOVERIES.has(copy.recovery), `${key}.recovery is one of the five`);
  }
  // The pinned sentences are shared by reference, not retyped.
  assert.equal(SESSION_ENDED_ERROR.what, SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE);
  assert.equal(UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR.what, UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE);
  assert.equal(ERROR_COPY.authentication_required, SESSION_ENDED_ERROR);
  assert.equal(SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR.what, "iTrack is temporarily unavailable.");
  // Two conflict codes keep their own sentences over the family's.
  assert.equal(ERROR_COPY.cycle_closed.what, "This cycle is closed.");
  assert.equal(ERROR_COPY.credential_archived.what, "This credential is archived.");
  assert.equal(ERROR_COPY.activity_version_conflict.what, "This item changed in another session.");
  assert.equal(ERROR_COPY.activity_version_conflict, ERROR_COPY.task_version_conflict);
});

test("describeApiError never surfaces the raw text as the headline", () => {
  const unknown = describeApiError({
    kind: "json",
    status: 500,
    code: "whatever_new",
    error: "Simulated server failure",
  });
  assert.equal(unknown.what, SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR.what);
  assert.equal(unknown.next, SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR.next);
  assert.equal(unknown.recovery, "retry");
  assert.equal(unknown.detail, "Simulated server failure");
  assert.equal(unknown.code, "whatever_new");
  assert.deepEqual(describeApiError({ kind: "json", status: 400 }), {
    ...FALLBACK_ERROR,
    code: null,
    detail: null,
  });
  const known = describeApiError({
    kind: "json",
    status: 409,
    code: "credential_archived",
    error: "This credential is archived. Restore it before making changes.",
  });
  assert.equal(known.what, "This credential is archived.");
  assert.equal(known.recovery, "reopen");
  assert.equal(known.detail, "This credential is archived. Restore it before making changes.");
  assert.equal(known.code, "credential_archived");
  // Prototype keys are not codes.
  assert.equal(describeApiError({ kind: "json", status: 400, code: "constructor" }).what, FALLBACK_ERROR.what);
  const html = "<html>502 Bad Gateway</html>".padEnd(400, "x");
  const unexpected = describeApiError({ kind: "unexpected", status: 502, text: html });
  assert.equal(unexpected.what, UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE);
  assert.equal(unexpected.next, UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR.next);
  assert.equal(unexpected.code, null);
  assert.equal(unexpected.detail, html.slice(0, 300));
  const ended = describeApiError({ kind: "session-ended" });
  assert.equal(ended.what, SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE);
  assert.equal(ended.recovery, "sign-in");
  assert.equal(ended.code, null);
  assert.equal(ended.detail, null);
  assert.equal(errorLine(FALLBACK_ERROR), "That change didn’t save. Try again. If it keeps happening, reload the page.");
  assert.equal(errorLine(OFFLINE_ERROR), "You’re offline. Your draft stays in this browser. Reconnect to save.");
});

test("check-in titles never exceed nine words", () => {
  assert.equal(CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT, 9);
  assert.equal(wordCount(""), 0);
  assert.equal(wordCount("  Confirm  renewal dates "), 3);
  const titles = managedTaskTitles();
  // 177 catalog + 18 pharmacist + 44 inline at c6b1fe4.
  assert.ok(titles.length >= 150, `scanned only ${titles.length} managed titles`);
  const over = titles.filter((title) => wordCount(title) > CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT);
  assert.ok(over.length > 0, "the catalog still carries titles the rule cannot show verbatim");
  const short = (iso) => iso;
  const reminder = (title) => ({
    kind: "task",
    title,
    eventDate: "2026-11-30",
    credentialName: "X",
    compliance: false,
  });
  for (const title of titles) {
    for (const kind of ["review", "progress", "submission"]) {
      const derived = checkInTitle(reminder(title), { kind, isPersonal: false, title }, short);
      assert.ok(
        wordCount(derived) <= CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT,
        `${kind}: ${JSON.stringify(derived)} runs over ${CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT} words`,
      );
    }
  }
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder("x"), { kind: "review", isPersonal: false, title: "x" }, short), "Confirm renewal dates and status");
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder("x"), { kind: "progress", isPersonal: false, title: "x" }, short), "Finish required credits and training");
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder("x"), { kind: "submission", isPersonal: false, title: "x" }, short), "Record the submission");
  // Deadlines read the formatted date; a compliance period says so.
  const deadline = { kind: "deadline", title: "LCSW renewal deadline", eventDate: "2026-11-30", credentialName: "LCSW" };
  assert.equal(checkInTitle({ ...deadline, compliance: false }, null, (iso) => `Nov ${iso.slice(8)}`), "Renewal due Nov 30");
  assert.equal(checkInTitle({ ...deadline, compliance: true }, null, (iso) => `Nov ${iso.slice(8)}`), "Compliance due Nov 30");
  // Acceptance reminders keep the server's own title (all three are ≤ 9 words).
  for (const title of [
    "Check the ISC2 dashboard for renewal",
    "Check the official record for the next compliance period",
    "Check renewal acceptance",
  ]) {
    const derived = checkInTitle({ kind: "acceptance", title, eventDate: "2026-11-30", credentialName: "X", compliance: false }, null, short);
    assert.equal(derived, title);
    assert.ok(wordCount(derived) <= CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT);
  }
  // A personal task's title is the user's text, verbatim — the rule covers the titles Home authors.
  const personal = Array.from({ length: 40 }, (_, index) => `word${index + 1}`).join(" ");
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder(personal), { kind: "custom", isPersonal: true, title: personal }, short), personal);
  // A task the workspace no longer holds, or a kind the map does not know, falls back to the reminder's title.
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder("Server title"), null, short), "Server title");
  assert.equal(checkInTitle(reminder("Server title"), { kind: "unknown", isPersonal: false, title: "x" }, short), "Server title");
  // Bodies: credential · date, plus the full managed title for the three managed kinds.
  const long = (iso) => `Nov ${iso.slice(8)}, ${iso.slice(0, 4)}`;
  assert.equal(checkInBody({ kind: "task", credentialName: "LCSW", eventDate: "2026-11-30" }, { kind: "review", isPersonal: false, title: over[0] }, long), `LCSW · due Nov 30, 2026 · ${over[0]}`);
  assert.equal(checkInBody({ kind: "task", credentialName: "LCSW", eventDate: "2026-11-30" }, { kind: "custom", isPersonal: true, title: "Book the ethics course" }, long), "LCSW · due Nov 30, 2026");
  assert.equal(checkInBody({ kind: "task", credentialName: "LCSW", eventDate: "2026-11-30" }, null, long), "LCSW · due Nov 30, 2026");
  assert.equal(checkInBody({ kind: "deadline", credentialName: "LCSW", eventDate: "2026-11-30" }, null, long), "LCSW · due Nov 30, 2026");
  assert.equal(checkInBody({ kind: "acceptance", credentialName: "CLCP", eventDate: "2026-11-30" }, null, long), "CLCP · awaiting acceptance");
});
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Create `app/lib/copy.ts`**

Create `app/lib/copy.ts` (header comment in the `app/lib/instruments.ts` style; no React, DOM, D1, `Intl` or clock import; the only runtime import is `./apiResponse.js` — the `Reminder` import is type-only and is erased from the emitted ESM):

```ts
/**
 * The copy and error map (spec §6 copy rules; app-ux-24, app-ux-11,
 * app-ux-14, architecture-04). One pure module owns every sentence the UI
 * shows for a failed API call and the string helpers more than one screen
 * needs — the check-in title/body rules Home applies to server reminders,
 * the ledger lede, the dialog names — so no screen or modal switches on a
 * `code` string or renders `result.error`.
 *
 * `describeApiError` maps a failed response (the shapes readApiResponse in
 * app/lib/apiResponse.ts returns) to what happened, what to do and a
 * recovery kind; the server's own sentence travels only as `detail`, which
 * ErrorSummary shows inside a closed "Technical details" disclosure. Every
 * code the API can emit is a key of ERROR_COPY — tests/copy.test.mjs
 * extracts them from app/api/** and fails on a missing one — and codes that
 * share a family share one ErrorCopy object.
 *
 * Pure on purpose: no React, DOM, Intl or clock. Date formatting is a
 * parameter of the check-in helpers so the caller binds its own zone and
 * options. Imports carry the `.js` suffix: `npm run build:lib-test` compiles
 * this file with `tsc --module nodenext` for tests/copy.test.mjs.
 */
import {
  SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE,
  UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE,
} from "./apiResponse.js";
import type { Reminder } from "./workspaceTypes.js";

/**
 * What happened, what to do, and what kind of recovery the surface offers:
 * `retry` (the form's own Save), `reopen` (the workspace was refetched and
 * the editor closed — open the item again), `reload` (reload the page),
 * `sign-in` (the session ended), `none` (nothing the user can do here).
 */
export type ErrorCopy = {
  what: string;
  next: string;
  recovery: "retry" | "reopen" | "reload" | "sign-in" | "none";
};

export const FALLBACK_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "That change didn’t save.",
  next: "Try again. If it keeps happening, reload the page.",
  recovery: "retry",
};

export const SESSION_ENDED_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: SESSION_ENDED_MESSAGE,
  next: "Reload and sign in to continue.",
  recovery: "sign-in",
};

export const UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_MESSAGE,
  next: "Try again in a moment.",
  recovery: "retry",
};

export const OFFLINE_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "You’re offline.",
  next: "Your draft stays in this browser. Reconnect to save.",
  recovery: "none",
};

/** Also the load-failure heading (tests/e2e/axe.spec.ts pins the `what`). */
export const SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "iTrack is temporarily unavailable.",
  next: "Try again in a moment. Nothing was changed.",
  recovery: "retry",
};

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Families. One object per family; every code that belongs to it is listed
// literally below, so the map stays a flat per-code object (the test
// enumerates the literal codes the API emits) while the sentences live once.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const INTERNAL_ERROR: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "iTrack couldn’t finish that request.",
  next: "Try again in a moment. Your saved record is unchanged.",
  recovery: "retry",
};

const CROSS_ORIGIN: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "That request came from another site.",
  next: "Open iTrack directly and try again.",
  recovery: "reload",
};

const MALFORMED_REQUEST: ErrorCopy = {
  what: "This request wasn’t in a form iTrack accepts.",
  next: "Reload the page and try again.",
  recovery: "reload",
};

function family(
  copy: ErrorCopy,
  codes: readonly string[],
): Record<string, ErrorCopy> {
  return Object.fromEntries(codes.map((code) => [code, copy]));
}

/**
 * Every code app/api/** can answer with, one key per literal code (the
 * families above are shared objects, not wildcard keys). tests/copy.test.mjs
 * extracts the codes from the API sources — `new RequestError(…, …, "code")`
 * and `new EvidenceApiError(…)` third arguments, `code: "…"` literals and
 * `packetError(…)` calls, plus the two classes' default "invalid_request" —
 * and fails on any key missing here. Keys the API does not emit yet are the
 * codes later Wave 4 tasks add (`invalid_date`, `invalid_format`,
 * `invalid_quiet_hours` in Task 4; `confirm_required`, `internal_only`,
 * `demo_workspace` in Task 13; `export_too_large` in Task 15), so those
 * tasks add no copy. The order matters only where a code overrides its
 * family: `cycle_closed` and `credential_archived` are conflict codes with
 * their own sentences.

/**
 * The codes after which the store refetches the workspace and closes the
 * open editors before reporting (today's list in runAction plus the sibling
 * state-changed codes the API emits on the same paths). The copy for each
 * is the CONFLICT family, except the two with their own sentences.
 */
export const CONFLICT_CODES: ReadonlySet<string> = new Set([
  "activity_version_conflict",
  "activity_state_changed",
  "allocation_state_changed",
  "task_version_conflict",
  "task_state_changed",
  "dental_checkpoint_state_changed",
  "cycle_closed",
  "credential_version_conflict",
  "credential_state_changed",
  "credential_archived",
  "acceptance_state_changed",
  "acceptance_activity_state_changed",
  "submission_state_changed",
  "requirement_state_changed",
  "evidence_changed",
  "evidence_upload_conflict",
  "quest_week_changed",
]);

export function isConflictCode(code: string | null | undefined): boolean {
  return typeof code === "string" && CONFLICT_CODES.has(code);
}

/**
 * A failed API call as readApiResponse classifies it: the session ended
 * (401), a non-JSON body (a proxy page, a broken JSON body), or a JSON
 * refusal carrying the server's `{ error, code }`.
 */
export type ApiFailure =
  | { kind: "session-ended" }
  | { kind: "unexpected"; status: number; text: string }
  | { kind: "json"; status: number; code?: string; error?: string };

/** The copy plus the server's own code and sentence, for the disclosure. */
export type DescribedError = ErrorCopy & {
  code: string | null;
  detail: string | null;
};

function copyForCode(code: string | undefined): ErrorCopy | undefined {
  return code !== undefined && Object.hasOwn(ERROR_COPY, code)
    ? ERROR_COPY[code]
    : undefined;
}

/**
 * The only way a server failure becomes a sentence. The raw `error` text is
 * never the headline: it is `detail`, and an unknown code falls back by
 * status (5xx → iTrack is unavailable, else the generic form copy). Applies
 * to API failures only — an Error thrown by a client validator or an
 * allocator builder is already user copy and is shown as it is.
 */
export function describeApiError(failure: ApiFailure): DescribedError {
  if (failure.kind === "session-ended") {
    return { ...SESSION_ENDED_ERROR, code: null, detail: null };
  }
  if (failure.kind === "unexpected") {
    return {
      ...UNEXPECTED_RESPONSE_ERROR,
      code: null,
      detail: failure.text.slice(0, 300),
    };
  }
  const copy =
    copyForCode(failure.code) ??
    (failure.status >= 500 ? SERVER_UNAVAILABLE_ERROR : FALLBACK_ERROR);
  return { ...copy, code: failure.code ?? null, detail: failure.error ?? null };
}

/** One line for a toast or the page banner: what happened, then what to do. */
export function errorLine(copy: ErrorCopy): string {
  return `${copy.what} ${copy.next}`;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Check-ins (Home's "Needs attention" rows; spec §6: titles ≤ 9 words).
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const CHECK_IN_TITLE_WORD_LIMIT = 9;

export function wordCount(text: string): number {
  const trimmed = text.trim();
  return trimmed ? trimmed.split(/\s+/).length : 0;
}

/**
 * The checklist task behind a `kind: "task"` reminder, or null when the
 * workspace no longer holds it. `kind` is the task's stored kind — the three
 * managed kinds are "review", "progress" and "submission"; a personal task
 * carries whatever the server stored and `isPersonal: true`.
 */
export type CheckInTask = {
  kind: string;
  isPersonal: boolean;
  title: string;
} | null;

const MANAGED_TASK_TITLES: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  review: "Confirm renewal dates and status",
  progress: "Finish required credits and training",
  submission: "Record the submission",
};

/**
 * The row title Home shows for a server reminder. Managed catalog task
 * titles run 10–26 words, so a task check-in derives a fixed ≤ 9-word title
 * from the task's kind and keeps the full title in the body; a personal
 * task's own title is shown verbatim (the row clamps it to two lines); a
 * deadline reads "Renewal due Nov 30" (or "Compliance due …" for a
 * compliance period); an acceptance reminder's server title is already
 * ≤ 9 words. `formatShortDate` is the caller's `Mon D` formatter.
 */
export function checkInTitle(
  reminder: Pick<Reminder, "kind" | "title" | "eventDate" | "credentialName"> & {
    compliance: boolean;
  },
  task: CheckInTask,
  formatShortDate: (iso: string) => string,
): string {
  if (reminder.kind === "deadline") {
    return `${reminder.compliance ? "Compliance" : "Renewal"} due ${formatShortDate(reminder.eventDate)}`;
  }
  if (reminder.kind === "acceptance" || task === null) return reminder.title;
  if (task.isPersonal) return task.title;
  return MANAGED_TASK_TITLES[task.kind] ?? reminder.title;
}

/**
 * The row's second line: the credential and the date, plus the full managed
 * task title for the three managed kinds so nothing the catalog says is
 * lost. `formatLongDate` is the caller's `Mon D, YYYY` formatter.
 */
export function checkInBody(
  reminder: Pick<Reminder, "kind" | "credentialName" | "eventDate">,
  task: CheckInTask,
  formatLongDate: (iso: string) => string,
): string {
  if (reminder.kind === "acceptance") {
    return `${reminder.credentialName} · awaiting acceptance`;
  }
  const base = `${reminder.credentialName} · due ${formatLongDate(reminder.eventDate)}`;
  if (
    reminder.kind === "task" &&
    task !== null &&
    !task.isPersonal &&
    Object.hasOwn(MANAGED_TASK_TITLES, task.kind)
  ) {
    return `${base} · ${task.title}`;
  }
  return base;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// The ledger lede (Home's page lede under "Your renewals").
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

const NUMBER_WORDS = [
  "No",
  "One",
  "Two",
  "Three",
  "Four",
  "Five",
  "Six",
  "Seven",
  "Eight",
  "Nine",
] as const;

/** 0–9 as a capitalised word ("No", "One" … "Nine"); anything else as digits. */
export function numberWord(n: number): string {
  return Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 0 && n < NUMBER_WORDS.length
    ? NUMBER_WORDS[n]
    : String(n);
}

/**
 * The mockup's "Three credentials on the record. One needs credits before
 * November." `rows` is the ledger's row count, `overdue` the rows past their
 * deadline, `needing` the open rows still short of credits, `soonestMonth`
 * the long month name of the earliest such deadline (null when the caller
 * has none to name). Overdue rows take the second sentence; the on-track
 * sentence closes a ledger with nothing outstanding.
 */
export function ledgerLede(input: {
  rows: number;
  needing: number;
  overdue: number;
  soonestMonth: string | null;
}): string {
  if (input.rows === 0) return "Nothing on the record yet.";
  const first = `${numberWord(input.rows)} credential${input.rows === 1 ? "" : "s"} on the record.`;
  if (input.overdue >= 1) {
    return `${first} ${numberWord(input.overdue)} past ${input.overdue === 1 ? "its deadline" : "their deadlines"}.`;
  }
  if (input.needing >= 1) {
    const before = input.soonestMonth ? ` before ${input.soonestMonth}` : "";
    return `${first} ${numberWord(input.needing)} need${input.needing === 1 ? "s" : ""} credits${before}.`;
  }
  return `${first} Everything is on track.`;
}

// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Dialog accessible names (copy table section I) — the one spelling every
// modal and every e2e fixture reads.
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

export const DIALOG_NAMES = {
  logActivity: "Log activity",
  editActivity: "Edit activity",
  discardActivity: "Discard this activity?",
  discardChanges: "Discard your changes?",
  scanNotice: "Download the certificate reader?",
  credentialSetup: "Add a credential",
  editCredential: "Edit credential",
  deleteCredential: (name: string) => `Delete ${name}?`,
  addTask: "Add a personal task",
  editTask: "Edit personal task",
  submission: "Record submission",
  allocate: "Apply to another credential",
  categorize: "Categorize this activity",
  editTags: "Edit requirement tags",
  evidence: "Evidence",
  installHelp: "Add iTrack to your phone",
  changeEmail: "Change email",
  changePassword: "Change password",
  deleteAccount: "Delete this account",
} as const;
```

Notes on the shape: `family(copy, codes)` returns a plain object keyed by each literal code, spread into one frozen object — so `Object.keys(ERROR_COPY)` lists every code once (202 keys), `ERROR_COPY.activity_version_conflict === ERROR_COPY.task_version_conflict` (one family object), and the two explicit entries `credential_archived` / `cycle_closed` sit after the conflict spread so nothing overrides them. `copyForCode` uses `Object.hasOwn` (lib es2022 under both `build:lib-test`'s `--target es2022` and the project's `"lib": ["esnext"]`) because `Readonly<Record<string, ErrorCopy>>` types every index as present and a prototype key must not read as a code. `describeApiError` spreads the family object into a fresh `DescribedError`, so a caller may mutate what it receives without touching the map. `checkInTitle` only ever consults `MANAGED_TASK_TITLES` for a non-personal task, and `checkInBody` appends `task.title` only for those same three kinds — a personal task's title is the row title already. `NUMBER_WORDS` is `as const` so `NUMBER_WORDS[n]` narrows to a literal union and the `?? String(n)` shape is unnecessary; the index is guarded by `Number.isInteger(n) && n >= 0 && n < NUMBER_WORDS.length` instead. `DIALOG_NAMES` is `as const`, so `DIALOG_NAMES.logActivity` is the literal type `"Log activity"` and `tests/e2e/fixtures.ts`' `LOG_SHEET_NAME` (Task 10) can be typed against it.
