```bash
cd "/Users/chrisskerritt/Documents/New project/Vigilo-wt/wave4"
python3 - <<'EOF'
from pathlib import Path
path = Path("app/components/Form.tsx")
src = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
start_line = "// The persistent error summary: rendered only while there are errors, so an\n"
end_line = "// The seven `<ModalError title message />` sites in app/ITrackApp.tsx keep\n"
assert src.count(start_line) == 1 and src.count(end_line) == 1, "anchors"
assert "error-summary-detail" not in src, "already applied"
start, end = src.index(start_line), src.index(end_line)
block = '''// The persistent error summary: rendered only while there are errors, so an
// empty alert never shadows another one in the same dialog; it takes focus
// and scrolls into view when its messages change, because a phone sheet is
// usually already scrolled to the submit row that produced them. Entries with
// a fieldId link to the field (looked up by id — useId() values are not
// selector-safe). It stays until its owner clears the errors; nothing here
// auto-dismisses. `detail` is the server's own sentence for a failed save
// (describeApiError's `detail`): it renders after the list inside a closed
// "Technical details" disclosure — outside the focus/scroll logic, never the
// headline, never announced (app-ux-24).
export function ErrorSummary({
  title,
  errors,
  detail,
}: {
  title?: string;
  errors: ReadonlyArray<ErrorSummaryEntry>;
  detail?: string;
}) {
  const ref = useRef<HTMLDivElement>(null);
  const announcement = errors.map((entry) => entry.message).join("\\n");

  useEffect(() => {
    if (!announcement) return;
    const node = ref.current;
    if (!node) return;
    node.scrollIntoView({ block: "center" });
    node.focus({ preventScroll: true });
  }, [announcement]);

  if (errors.length === 0) return null;

  const focusField =
    (fieldId: string) => (event: MouseEvent<HTMLAnchorElement>) => {
      const target = document.getElementById(fieldId);
      if (!target) return;
      event.preventDefault();
      target.focus();
    };

  return (
    <div className="error-summary" role="alert" tabIndex={-1} ref={ref}>
      <strong>{title ?? "Check the form"}</strong>
      <ul>
        {errors.map((entry, index) => (
          <li key={`${entry.fieldId ?? ""}:${index}`}>
            {entry.fieldId ? (
              <a href={`#${entry.fieldId}`} onClick={focusField(entry.fieldId)}>
                {entry.message}
              </a>
            ) : (
              entry.message
            )}
          </li>
        ))}
      </ul>
      {detail ? (
        <details className="error-summary-detail">
          <summary>Technical details</summary>
          <pre>{detail}</pre>
        </details>
      ) : null}
    </div>
  );
}

'''

print("ErrorSummary: detail added")
EOF

### Task 3: Server gates, no route split: setReminderState status `active` (Undo), 409 credential_archived on the seven task/activity writes, self-proving orphan-evidence flip, the five 'Sign in with ChatGPT' strings replaced

**Rationale:** spec §6 Home ("Snooze" / "Done" with an Undo toast — app-ux-08): the check-in inbox has no way back today. `setReminderState` (`app/api/workspace/route.ts:13333-13462`) accepts only `dismissed` | `snoozed` (`:13350-13352`, "status must be dismissed or snoozed"), and `app/lib/reminders.ts:399-416` hides a `dismissed` row and a `snoozed` row until `snoozedUntil`, while a reminder with **no** state row falls through as visible — so "restore" is "delete the row", which needs a third status the action does not yet take. Spec §4 credential archive and the Wave 2/3 carried minor "archived credentials not fully frozen": `assertCredentialNotArchived` (`:3966-3976`, 409 `credential_archived`, `CREDENTIAL_ARCHIVED_MESSAGE` at `:3959-3960`) guards every credential write and `addActivity`, `createPersonalTask` (`:8343-8357`), `markSubmitted`, `addActivityAllocation`, `markRenewalAccepted`, `updateRequirementApplicability` and `setReminderState` (`:13372`), but the task and activity writes read only `credential.status` — `getTaskForMutation` (`:8226-8255`), `getActivityAllocationValidationRows` (`:7441-7467`), the allocation row of `updateActivityAllocationRequirements` (`:9822-9855`) and the INSERT…SELECT of `saveDentalCheckpoint` (its `credential.status` predicate at `:12619`) — and archiving never changes `status`, so `toggleTask`, `updatePersonalTask`, `archivePersonalTask`, `restorePersonalTask`, `updateActivity`, `archiveActivity`, `restoreActivity`, `updateActivityAllocationRequirements` and `saveDentalCheckpoint` all still write against an archived credential (the Wave 3 plan's reviewer minor). The other carried minor, "the orphan-proof SELECT runs outside the delete batch": `deleteCredential` (`:7174-7438`) decides its orphan list at `:7217-7243`, before `database.batch(statements)` at `:7401`; the in-batch flip at `:7298-7306` trusts that list, and the R2 delete at `:7424-7437` trusts it again — an allocation that lands between the SELECT and the batch is flipped to `deleting` and loses its object. Spec §1.1 (every ChatGPT residue removed): five 401 bodies still read "Sign in with ChatGPT …" — `route.ts:13513`, `app/api/export/route.ts:33`, `app/api/catalog/route.ts:31`, `app/api/evidence/_shared.ts:98`, `app/api/export/packet/route.ts:90` — pinned by `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:13040, 24028, 26834`. Global Constraints "No route split (architecture-M-05 deferred)": every edit here is a contained change inside `route.ts` and the four sibling files; no function moves. Consumers: Home (Task 8) posts `status: "active"` from its Undo toast; the store (Task 5) maps `credential_archived` to the archived toast and the credential detail's stale-tab e2e (Task 7) relies on the 409; the copy map (Task 2) already keys `credential_archived` and `authentication_required` — the codes do not change here, only the sentences behind `authentication_required`.

**Decisions:** (1) Undo reuses `setReminderState` with `status: "active"` — no new action (`WORKSPACE_ACTIONS` stays 27 in this task; `tests/isolation.test.mjs:557` is untouched here — Task 13 moves it to 28), no change to the `{ ok, action, id }` envelope. `active` runs the same credential 404 (`:13358-13371`), `assertCredentialNotArchived` (`:13372`) and reminder-key validation (`:13374-13413`) as the other two statuses, then `DELETE`s the row and returns the deleted row's id (or the key when no row existed) — a second Undo is a 200 no-op. The `INSERT … ON CONFLICT` never runs for `active`, so the binding pin at `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:20091-20104` (status `dismissed`) holds untouched. The developer string becomes "status must be dismissed, snoozed or active" (copy table row 18; the client maps it through `invalid_request`). (2) The archived gate is a pre-flight throw at the narrowest point of each write **plus** the same predicate beside every existing credential-status guard on that write, so the window between the pre-flight and the statement is closed too, and the diagnosis paths (which re-run the pre-flight) answer `credential_archived`. Tasks: `getTaskForMutation` selects `credential.archived_at AS credentialArchivedAt` and `assertTaskMutationState` throws right after its 404 — before `managed_task_immutable`, the revision check and `cycle_closed` — which covers `toggleTask` (`:8622`), `updatePersonalTask` (`:8458`), `setPersonalTaskArchivedState` (`:8518`, archive and restore) and `diagnoseTaskMutationFailure` (`:8303`). Activities: `getActivityAllocationValidationRows` selects `credential.archived_at AS credentialArchivedAt` and `validateActivityMutationAllocations` throws before its `cycle_closed` check and before its `revalidateTags === false` early return — which covers `updateActivity` (`:7710`), `setActivityArchivedState` (`:7957`, archive and restore) and `diagnoseActivityMutationFailure` (`:7673`). `updateActivityAllocationRequirements` selects `credential.archived_at` into its allocation row and throws after its 404, **before** `cycle_closed` (the repo convention `route.ts:3961-3965` "after its ownership 404 and before any status rule", and the cross-task contract: a renewed-and-archived credential must answer `credential_archived`, the code the store maps to the archived toast — not `cycle_closed`). `saveDentalCheckpoint` adds `AND credential.archived_at IS NULL` to its INSERT…SELECT and reports `credential_archived` from its diagnosis SELECT before `cycle_closed`. Every new throw reuses `CREDENTIAL_ARCHIVED_MESSAGE`, so the sentence stays byte-identical to `assertCredentialNotArchived`'s. (3) Orphan flip: the pre-batch SELECT stays (it names the candidate ids), the in-batch `UPDATE evidence_files SET status = 'deleting'` gains `AND NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM activity_allocations y WHERE y.activity_id = evidence_files.activity_id)` — inside the transaction the series' credentials are already deleted and their allocations cascaded, so any allocation still standing is by definition outside the series — and the R2 delete after the batch acts only on the rows the batch actually flipped (re-selected by `status = 'deleting'`), never on the pre-batch list; otherwise a row the guard spared would still lose its object. The activity recompute statements already read `stored.status = 'ready'`, so a spared row keeps its activity `attached`. (4) The five 401 sentences become exactly "Sign in to continue." (copy table row 17); codes stay `authentication_required`; the three rendered-html pins are rewritten to the new sentence in the same commit — they are behaviour tests over the built worker's response, not source pins. Task 17 later gives the packet its own 401 sentence. (5) Every proof is a real-SQLite behaviour test in `tests/workspace-credential-actions.test.mjs` (the `boot()` harness). The in-batch proof for (3) simulates the race by overriding the harness's own `SQLiteD1Database.batch` on one boot's instance for exactly the `deleteCredential` batch: the override inserts an allocation to a second credential after the orphan SELECT has run and before the batch executes. The ninth write, `saveDentalCheckpoint`, is exercised on a Dental credential seeded the way `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:24142-24182` seeds its dental lifecycle case — a raw `credentials` row on `tx-dentist-2026-v1` plus one informational requirement on `tx-dentist-2026-human-trafficking` (both catalog rows are seeded by `initializeDatabase`, so the foreign keys resolve) — because no action creates a dental template without its date and eligibility rules, and the checkpoint contract is what is under test.

  await t.test("a snoozed check-in is restored by status active, twice", async () => {
    const credential = await createCustom({
      credentialName: "Snoozed LMHC",
      cycleStart: shiftDays(today, -345),
      deadline: shiftDays(today, 20),
    });
    const reminderKey = `deadline:${credential.id}:${credential.deadline}`;
    const listed = async () =>
      (await api.workspace(OWNER)).reminders.some((reminder) => reminder.key === reminderKey);
    const stateRows = () =>
      Number(raw("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM reminder_states WHERE reminder_key = ?", reminderKey)[0].n);
    assert.equal(await listed(), true, "a deadline 20 days out is a check-in (lead day 30)");
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 0);

    const snoozed = await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
      reminderKey,
      credentialId: credential.id,
      status: "snoozed",
      snoozedUntil: shiftDays(today, 7),
    });
    assert.equal(snoozed.status, 200, JSON.stringify(snoozed.body));
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 1);
    assert.equal(await listed(), false, "a snoozed check-in leaves the list until snoozedUntil");

    // Undo: the same action, status active. The row goes; the key is back;
    // the id names the row that went.
    const restored = await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
      reminderKey,
      credentialId: credential.id,
      status: "active",
      snoozedUntil: null,
    });
    assert.deepEqual(restored, {
      status: 200,
      body: { ok: true, action: "setReminderState", id: snoozed.body.id },
    });
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 0);
    assert.equal(await listed(), true, "Undo puts the check-in back");

    // Twice: with no row to delete it is still a 200, and the id is the key.
    const again = await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
      reminderKey,
      credentialId: credential.id,
      status: "active",
      snoozedUntil: null,
    });
    assert.deepEqual(again, {
      status: 200,
      body: { ok: true, action: "setReminderState", id: reminderKey },
    });
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 0);

    // Done (dismissed) comes back the same way, and snoozedUntil is ignored
    // for active — a date that would be refused for a snooze goes unread.
    const dismissed = await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
      reminderKey,
      credentialId: credential.id,
      status: "dismissed",
      snoozedUntil: null,
    });
    assert.equal(dismissed.status, 200, JSON.stringify(dismissed.body));
    assert.equal(await listed(), false);
    const undone = await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
      reminderKey,
      credentialId: credential.id,
      status: "active",
      snoozedUntil: "2000-01-01",
    });
    assert.equal(undone.status, 200, JSON.stringify(undone.body));
    assert.equal(undone.body.id, dismissed.body.id);
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 0);
    assert.equal(await listed(), true);

    // The status set is closed, and ownership is checked before anything else.
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "setReminderState", {
        reminderKey,
        credentialId: credential.id,
        status: "later",
        snoozedUntil: null,
      }),
      400,
      "invalid_request",
      /^status must be dismissed, snoozed or active$/,
    );
    expectError(
      await api.post(OTHER, "setReminderState", {
        reminderKey,
        credentialId: credential.id,
        status: "active",
        snoozedUntil: null,
      }),
      404,
      "credential_not_found",
    );
    assert.equal(stateRows(), 0);
  });

  await t.test("delete flips only evidence with no surviving allocation, proven inside the batch", async () => {
    const doomed = await createCustom({ credentialName: "Epsilon OT" });
    const survivor = await createCustom({ credentialName: "Zeta SLP" });
    const activity = await logActivity(doomed.id, { title: "Raced course" });
    const evidence = await api.upload(OWNER, activity.id, "raced.png");
    const [{ objectKey }] = raw("SELECT object_key AS objectKey FROM evidence_files WHERE id = ?", evidence.id);
    assert.ok(bucket.objects.has(objectKey));

    // The race the carried minor names: deleteCredential's orphan SELECT has
    // already listed this file (its activity is allocated to `doomed` alone)
    // when an allocation to `survivor` lands, and only then does the batch
    // run. SQLiteD1Database is the harness's own class, so overriding `batch`
    // on this boot's instance for exactly the deleteCredential batch (its
    // first statement is the renewal_acceptances delete; ensureUser's batch
    // starts with an INSERT INTO users and passes through) inserts that
    // allocation between the two. The insert satisfies the
    // activity_allocations_mutable_guard_v2 trigger: the activity is live and
    // the survivor is active.
    let raced = false;
    db.batch = async function racedBatch(statements) {
      if (!raced && /^DELETE FROM renewal_acceptances/i.test(statements[0]?.sql ?? "")) {
        raced = true;
        db.raw
          .prepare(
            `INSERT INTO activity_allocations (id, activity_id, credential_id, requirement_id, allocated_units)
             VALUES (?, ?, ?, NULL, 1)`,
          )
          .run("allocation-task3-race", activity.id, survivor.id);
        delete db.batch; // back to the class method for this and every later batch
      }
      return SQLiteD1Database.prototype.batch.call(db, statements);
    };
    const deleted = await api.post(OWNER, "deleteCredential", {
      credentialId: doomed.id,
      expectedRevision: doomed.revision,
      confirmName: "Epsilon OT",
    });
    delete db.batch;
    assert.equal(deleted.status, 200, JSON.stringify(deleted.body));
    assert.equal(raced, true, "the override saw the deleteCredential batch");
    assert.equal(await api.count("credentials", "id", doomed.id), 0);
    // The batch proved the allocation survived: the row was not flipped, the
    // object was not deleted, the activity still reads attached and is now
    // allocated to the survivor alone.
    assert.deepEqual(
      raw("SELECT status FROM evidence_files WHERE id = ?", evidence.id),
      [{ status: "ready" }],
    );
    assert.ok(!bucket.deletes.includes(objectKey), "no R2 delete for a file whose activity kept an allocation");
    assert.ok(bucket.objects.has(objectKey));
    assert.deepEqual(
      raw("SELECT evidence_status AS evidenceStatus FROM activities WHERE id = ?", activity.id),
      [{ evidenceStatus: "attached" }],
    );
    const afterFirst = await api.workspace(OWNER);
    assert.deepEqual(
      afterFirst.activities
        .find((candidate) => candidate.id === activity.id)
        .allocations.map((candidate) => candidate.credentialId),
      [survivor.id],
    );

    // Delete the survivor: now no allocation stands, so the flip and the
    // object delete both happen.
    const survivorNow = (await api.credential(OWNER, survivor.id)).active;
    const deletedSurvivor = await api.post(OWNER, "deleteCredential", {
      credentialId: survivor.id,
      expectedRevision: survivorNow.revision,
      confirmName: "Zeta SLP",
    });
    assert.equal(deletedSurvivor.status, 200, JSON.stringify(deletedSurvivor.body));
    assert.equal(await api.count("evidence_files", "id", evidence.id), 0);
    assert.ok(bucket.deletes.includes(objectKey), "the object goes once no allocation survives");
    assert.ok(!bucket.objects.has(objectKey));
    assert.deepEqual(
      raw("SELECT evidence_status AS evidenceStatus FROM activities WHERE id = ?", activity.id),
      [{ evidenceStatus: "missing" }],
    );
  });

D1 reports `meta.changes` as a total_changes() delta that counts cascaded rows (`route.ts:7402-7409`), so a `changes` count never decides `credential_archived` — the diagnosis SELECTs do; that is also why the deleteCredential test reads the evidence row's `status` back rather than counting statement changes. Do not edit `CREDENTIAL_ARCHIVED_MESSAGE` or spell the sentence again: the four new throws reuse the constant, and the probes assert the exact string. In the race subtest the override must let `ensureUser`'s batch (first statement `INSERT INTO users`) through untouched and act on the batch whose first statement starts `DELETE FROM renewal_acceptances` — the `raced` flag plus `delete db.batch` make it fire once; `bucket.deletes` accumulates across the whole Task 9 block, so the assertions use `includes(objectKey)` on the one key, never `deepEqual([])`. `raw()` is synchronous and returns plain objects (`api.count` awaits it, harmlessly); `SELECT archived_at IS NULL AS live` comes back as the integers `1`/`0`. `expectedRevision` for a checkpoint is the non-negative `checkpointRevision` (`0` for a fresh one, `1` after the first save); for tasks and activities it is the positive `revision` read from the table. `isoDaysFromToday` and `shiftDays(today, n)` both count in UTC, which is the stored reminder zone every new identity starts with, so `snoozedUntil: shiftDays(today, 7)` is never "in the past" and a deadline 20 days out is inside the default 30-day lead. The raw dental rows carry no `revision` column value, so the credential's revision defaults to 1 — hence `expectedRevision: 1` on its archive.

### Task 4: Server fields — migration 0015_wave4_fields: activity format + notes, reminder quiet hours (+ pure quietHours.ts, scheduler skip), GET /api/export filters and two CSV columns

**Rationale:** spec §6 gives three Wave 4 screens fields the server does not have: the Log activity Details step ("optional details (provider, format, notes …)"), the Account Reminders section ("reminders (time zone auto-detected, quiet hours)") and the Activity log ("filters by credential, date range, tag; CSV export here"). At `main@c6b1fe4` the `activities` table has no `format`/`notes` column (`db/runtime.ts:237-251`; `addActivity` at `app/api/workspace/route.ts:5953` and `updateActivity` at `:7710` ignore unknown keys), `reminder_preferences` has no quiet-hours columns (`db/runtime.ts:390-400`, `app/lib/reminders.ts:25-32` `ReminderPreferenceData`), the push scheduler decides by `clock.hour < pushHour` alone (`app/lib/pushDelivery.ts:773-774`), and `GET /api/export` reads no query at all (`app/api/export/route.ts:27-144`). This task lands the schema and the contracts first so Task 10 (`LogActivityModal` → `activityPayload` with `format`/`notes`), Task 11 (`exportHref` → `/api/export?credentialId=&from=&to=&tag=`), Task 15 (`_activityCsv.ts` re-uses the query, the filters and the two columns) and Task 16 (the Reminders form's "Quiet from" / "Quiet until") build on a server that already stores, returns and honours them. §8 keeps migrations in `drizzle/` ("D1 migrations continue in `drizzle/`"), and the Global Constraints name this one: `0015_wave4_fields` — four nullable columns, added to the runtime `CREATE TABLE`s for fresh databases, to `RICH_RULE_COLUMNS` so `ensureRichRuleColumns` (`db/runtime.ts:5636-5667`) ALTERs an existing volume on the first request after deploy, to `db/schema.ts`, and generated into `drizzle/` exactly as 0014 was (commit `138aa61`). perf-M-02 stays client-side: no page contract enters the workspace payload; the CSV filters are the only server-side narrowing this wave. critic-01's rule holds for quiet hours — the window is compared against `localReminderClock(now, timeZone).hour` in the user's stored zone, never UTC. architecture-M-05 is deferred: every route.ts edit is a contained insertion, no function moves. The one copy string this task writes, "Choose the dates as YYYY-MM-DD." (`invalid_date`), is copy-table row `export/route.ts:136-141` (owner 4); the CSV's format labels are the copy table's five Log-sheet option labels (Task 10's row) and the "Format" / "Notes" header words are the columns Task 15's `buildActivitiesCsv` header names.

**Decisions (binding for Tasks 10, 11, 15, 16):**
1. **The runtime DDL is authoritative; drizzle is the record, generated, not hand-written.** `db/runtime.ts` `TABLE_STATEMENTS` + `RICH_RULE_COLUMNS` are what `initializeDatabase` runs on the Railway volume; `drizzle/0015_wave4_fields.sql`, `drizzle/meta/0015_snapshot.json` and the journal entry are produced by `npx drizzle-kit generate --name wave4_fields` (`drizzle-kit` 0.31.10 is in `devDependencies`, `drizzle.config.ts` points at `db/schema.ts`; `npm run db:generate` is the same command). Probed in a scratch copy of the repo at `c6b1fe4`: before the schema edit drizzle-kit prints `No schema changes, nothing to migrate`; after the four column lines it emits exactly the four `ALTER TABLE … ADD …` statements below, journal `idx 15` / `tag "0015_wave4_fields"` / `version "6"`, and a 2 970-line snapshot whose `prevId` is 0014's id `50431e12-207f-41a7-a81d-712827538551`. The 0014 commit committed all three files; so does this one.
2. **The pins that 0014 moved are moved the same way, and the two value pins the contract changes are rewritten to the new contract in this commit.** `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs` reads every migration file into one `migration` string and pins the journal's last tag twice (`:7386-7390`, `:7765-7769`); commit `138aa61` re-pointed both from `0013_drop_apns` to `0014_credential_archive` and added the new file to the `Promise.all` list, the concatenation and per-statement `assert.match` calls — this task does the identical thing for 0015. Two behaviour assertions over the built worker change because the payload changes: `assert.deepEqual(workspace.reminderPreferences, {…})` at `:18802` gains `quietHoursStart: null, quietHoursEnd: null`, and `assert.deepEqual(preferenceUpsert.bindings, […])` at `:20055` gains the two trailing `null`s the upsert now binds. `tests/real-sqlite-seed.test.mjs` gains the fresh-boot column subtest 0014 added for its columns.
3. **Format is an enum key on the server; labels are a client concern.** `addActivity`/`updateActivity` store one of `live_course | live_webinar | self_study | conference | other` (anything else → 400 `invalid_format`); `""`, `null` and absent all store NULL so the Log sheet's empty select and a Wave 3 client agree. The CSV writes the copy table's labels ("Live course" / "Live webinar" / "On-demand or self-study" / "Conference" / "Other") through an inline `FORMAT_LABELS` map in `app/api/export/route.ts`; Task 15 moves that map with the query into `app/api/export/_activityCsv.ts`.
4. **`updateActivity` is present-only for the two details.** A key absent from the payload leaves its column alone; `null` (or `""`) clears it; a value replaces it. The UPDATE gains a `SET` fragment only for the keys present, so a payload without either is byte-identical to today's statement and bindings (the fake-D1 `updateActivity` cases in rendered-html never send them).
5. **Quiet hours are a pair or nothing, and absent means nothing.** `updateReminderPreferences` accepts `quietHoursStart` / `quietHoursEnd`: both absent or both `null` → both columns NULL; both whole hours 0–23 and different → stored; one without the other, a non-integer, out of range, or `start === end` → 400 `invalid_quiet_hours`. The upsert always writes both columns, so the run-check's payload (`deploy/railway/runcheck.sh:127`, no quiet fields) keeps answering 200 and clears any earlier window — Task 16's form always sends both. `0` is a valid hour (never treated as absent).
6. **Quiet hours are enforced only in the scheduler's scan loop, as one `continue`.** `app/lib/quietHours.ts` decides (start-inclusive, end-exclusive; `start > end` wraps midnight; `null` either side or `start === end` → never quiet); `pushDelivery.ts` selects the two columns beside `push_hour_local` and skips the user for the run exactly like a user before their push hour. A check-in whose push hour falls inside the window is materialised by the first run after the window; the ledger's `INSERT … WHERE NOT EXISTS (… prior.scheduled_for >= ?)` dedupe makes that safe. Nothing else in `pushDelivery.ts` changes (it is not on Wave 4's keep-list; this is a two-line edit plus the import). `pushDelivery.ts` imports its siblings without a suffix (`./rfc8291Push`, `./reminders` at `:9`, `:15`) — the new import matches that file's style; `quietHours.ts` itself imports nothing, so the `./x.js` rule for pure modules is moot for it.
7. **Export filters gate the ACTIVITY, never the joined allocation row.** Each filter is an `EXISTS` (credential, tag) or a comparison on `a.completion_date` (from, to) appended AFTER the literal text `AND a.archived_at IS NULL` — the substring `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:7803-7806` pins (`/WHERE a\.user_id = \?[\s\S]*?a\.archived_at IS NULL/`) — so a matching activity keeps every allocation line and, with no query, the SQL and the file are byte-identical to today's except the two appended columns. The tag `EXISTS` mirrors the client rule Task 11's `activityTags` applies (matched requirement names when matches exist, else the direct requirement). `from`/`to` must match `ISO_DATE_PATTERN` (`app/lib/dates.ts:12`) or the route answers 400 `invalid_date` before touching the database; `credentialId` is sliced to 160 characters and `tag` to 100; an empty value is "not set".
8. **The scheduler skip is proven by driving the real cron.** Besides the pure unit suite, `tests/workspace-credential-actions.test.mjs` runs `worker.scheduled()` on the built worker over real SQLite with in-test VAPID keys and a stubbed `fetch` — the way `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs:20485-20500` drives it — at 14:00 UTC inside a 13→15 window (nothing materialised, nothing sent) and again at 16:00 (materialised and delivered).

// `app/lib/quietHours.ts` is the one place the push scheduler decides whether
// a user's local hour sits inside their quiet window (spec §6 Account
// reminders — "Alerts due inside quiet hours wait until they end."). It is
// pure: two bounds (or nulls) and an hour in, a boolean out. The scheduler
// (app/lib/pushDelivery.ts) hands it `localReminderClock(now, timeZone).hour`,
// so no clock and no zone appear here, and it is tested against the ESM that
// `npm run build:lib-test` emits, exactly like tests/instruments.test.mjs.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import test from "node:test";

import { inQuietHours } from "../.test-build/quietHours.js";

test("a window inside one day is start-inclusive and end-exclusive", () => {
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(9, 9, 17), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(10, 9, 17), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(16, 9, 17), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(17, 9, 17), false);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(8, 9, 17), false);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(0, 9, 17), false);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(23, 9, 17), false);
});

test("a window that wraps midnight covers the late evening and the early morning", () => {
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(22, 22, 7), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(23, 22, 7), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(0, 22, 7), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(3, 22, 7), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(6, 22, 7), true);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(7, 22, 7), false);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(12, 22, 7), false);
  assert.equal(inQuietHours(21, 22, 7), false);
});

test("no window: a null bound never quiets, and start === end is no window", () => {
  for (let hour = 0; hour < 24; hour += 1) {
    assert.equal(inQuietHours(hour, null, null), false, `null/null at ${hour}`);
    assert.equal(inQuietHours(hour, null, 7), false, `null/7 at ${hour}`);
    assert.equal(inQuietHours(hour, 22, null), false, `22/null at ${hour}`);
    assert.equal(inQuietHours(hour, 5, 5), false, `5/5 at ${hour}`);
  }
});

test("every ordered pair of distinct bounds quiets exactly (end - start) mod 24 hours", () => {
  // The two branches (same-day, wrapping) partition the day: the window
  // always contains its start, never its end, and never any other hour.
  for (let start = 0; start < 24; start += 1) {
    for (let end = 0; end < 24; end += 1) {
      if (start === end) continue;
      const quiet = [];
      for (let hour = 0; hour < 24; hour += 1) {
        if (inQuietHours(hour, start, end)) quiet.push(hour);
      }
      assert.equal(quiet.length, (end - start + 24) % 24, `${start} → ${end}`);
      assert.ok(quiet.includes(start), `${start} → ${end} includes its start`);
      assert.ok(!quiet.includes(end), `${start} → ${end} excludes its end`);
    }
  }
});
```

Create `app/lib/quietHours.ts`:

```ts
// Quiet hours for phone alerts (spec §6 Account reminders). A window is two
// local hours, start-inclusive and end-exclusive: 22 → 7 quiets 22:00 through
// 06:59 (it wraps midnight); 9 → 17 quiets 09:00 through 16:59. Either bound
// null means no window. start === end is also no window — the preference
// validation refuses it, and reading it as "never" rather than "all day"
// keeps a stray equal pair from silencing every alert.
//
// Pure and import-free: `npm run build:lib-test` compiles this file for
// tests/quiet-hours.test.mjs, and app/lib/pushDelivery.ts calls it with
// `localReminderClock(now, timeZone).hour`, so the comparison happens in the
// user's stored zone (critic-01), never in UTC.
export function inQuietHours(
  hour: number,
  start: number | null,
  end: number | null,
): boolean {
  if (start === null || end === null || start === end) return false;
  if (
    !Number.isInteger(hour) ||
    !Number.isInteger(start) ||
    !Number.isInteger(end)
  ) {
    return false;
  }
  if (start < end) return hour >= start && hour < end;
  return hour >= start || hour < end;
}
```

  await t.test("a fresh boot creates the four 0015 columns", () => {
    const activityColumns = api

  await t.test("every activity carries format and notes; both default to null", async () => {
    const logged = await api.post(OWNER, "addActivity", logPayload({ title: "Plain course" }));
    assert.equal(logged.status, 200, JSON.stringify(logged.body));

    assert.equal(plain.format, null);

  await t.test("format and notes round-trip, an empty string stores null, and the enum is validated", async () => {
    const logged = await api.post(
      OWNER,
      "addActivity",
      logPayload({ title: "Conference course", format: "conference", notes: "Room 4" }),
    );
    assert.equal(logged.status, 200, JSON.stringify(logged.body));
    const saved = await activity(logged.body.id);
    assert.equal(saved.format, "conference");
    assert.equal(saved.notes, "Room 4");
    assert.deepEqual(
      api.raw("SELECT format, notes FROM activities WHERE id = ?", logged.body.id),
      [{ format: "conference", notes: "Room 4" }],
    );
    const blank = await api.post(
      OWNER,
      "addActivity",
      logPayload({ title: "Blank format course", format: "", notes: "   " }),
    );
    assert.equal(blank.status, 200, JSON.stringify(blank.body));
    const blankSaved = await activity(blank.body.id);
    assert.equal(blankSaved.format, null);
    assert.equal(blankSaved.notes, null);
    const longest = await api.post(
      OWNER,
      "addActivity",
      logPayload({ title: "Two thousand", notes: "y".repeat(2000) }),
    );
    assert.equal(longest.status, 200, JSON.stringify(longest.body));
    assert.equal((await activity(longest.body.id)).notes.length, 2000);
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "addActivity", logPayload({ format: "zoom" })),
      400,
      "invalid_format",
      ACTIVITY_FORMAT_MESSAGE,
    );
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "addActivity", logPayload({ format: 3 })),
      400,
      "invalid_format",
      ACTIVITY_FORMAT_MESSAGE,
    );
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "addActivity", logPayload({ notes: "x".repeat(2001) })),
      400,
      "invalid_request",
      "notes must be 2000 characters or fewer",
    );
  });

  await t.test("updateActivity changes a detail only when its key is present; null clears it", async () => {
    const logged = await api.post(
      OWNER,
      "addActivity",
      logPayload({ title: "Editable course", format: "live_webinar", notes: "Before" }),
    );
    assert.equal(logged.status, 200, JSON.stringify(logged.body));
    let current = await activity(logged.body.id);
    const corePayload = () => ({
      activityId: current.id,
      expectedRevision: current.revision,
      title: current.title,
      provider: current.provider,
      completionDate: current.completionDate,
      totalUnits: current.totalUnits,
    });
    const update = async (extra = {}) => {
      const result = await api.post(OWNER, "updateActivity", { ...corePayload(), ...extra });
      assert.equal(result.status, 200, JSON.stringify(result.body));
      current = await activity(current.id);
      return current;
    };
    // Neither key: both unchanged.
    await update();
    assert.equal(current.format, "live_webinar");
    assert.equal(current.notes, "Before");
    // notes: null clears the notes and leaves the format alone.
    await update({ notes: null });
    assert.equal(current.format, "live_webinar");
    assert.equal(current.notes, null);
    // Values replace; "" clears the format.
    await update({ format: "other", notes: "After" });
    assert.equal(current.format, "other");
    assert.equal(current.notes, "After");
    await update({ format: "" });
    assert.equal(current.format, null);
    assert.equal(current.notes, "After");
    // The same validation as addActivity, and a refusal leaves the row alone.
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "updateActivity", { ...corePayload(), format: "zoom" }),
      400,
      "invalid_format",
      ACTIVITY_FORMAT_MESSAGE,
    );
    expectError(
      await api.post(OWNER, "updateActivity", { ...corePayload(), notes: "z".repeat(2001) }),
      400,
      "invalid_request",
      "notes must be 2000 characters or fewer",
    );
    const untouched = await activity(current.id);
    assert.equal(untouched.revision, current.revision);
    assert.equal(untouched.format, null);
    assert.equal(untouched.notes, "After");
  });

  await t.test("quiet hours round-trip, validate, and clear when both are absent", async () => {
    const userId = api.raw("SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?", OWNER)[0].id;
    const storedWindow = () =>
      api.raw(
        "SELECT quiet_hours_start AS start, quiet_hours_end AS end FROM reminder_preferences WHERE user_id = ?",
        userId,
      )[0];
    const saved = await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
      ...RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD,
      quietHoursStart: 22,
      quietHoursEnd: 7,
    });
    assert.equal(saved.status, 200, JSON.stringify(saved.body));
    assert.deepEqual(saved.body, {
      ok: true,
      action: "updateReminderPreferences",
      id: "reminder-preferences",
    });
    let workspace = await api.workspace(OWNER);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursStart, 22);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursEnd, 7);
    assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: 22, end: 7 });
    // 0 is an hour, not "absent".
    const midnight = await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
      ...RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD,
      quietHoursStart: 0,
      quietHoursEnd: 23,
    });
    assert.equal(midnight.status, 200, JSON.stringify(midnight.body));
    assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: 0, end: 23 });
    workspace = await api.workspace(OWNER);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursStart, 0);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursEnd, 23);
    // Every refusal leaves the stored window alone.
    for (const invalid of [
      { quietHoursStart: 22 },
      { quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: 22, quietHoursEnd: null },
      { quietHoursStart: null, quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: 24, quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: -1, quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: 5.5, quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: "22", quietHoursEnd: 7 },
      { quietHoursStart: 5, quietHoursEnd: 5 },
    ]) {
      expectError(
        await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
          ...RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD,
          ...invalid,
        }),
        400,
        "invalid_quiet_hours",
        QUIET_HOURS_MESSAGE,
      );
      assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: 0, end: 23 }, JSON.stringify(invalid));
    }
    // Both null clears.
    const cleared = await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
      ...RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD,
      quietHoursStart: null,
      quietHoursEnd: null,
    });
    assert.equal(cleared.status, 200, JSON.stringify(cleared.body));
    assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: null, end: null });
    // Set again, then the run-check payload (no quiet fields at all): 200, and
    // absent means "no window" — the upsert always writes both columns.
    await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
      ...RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD,
      quietHoursStart: 9,
      quietHoursEnd: 17,
    });
    assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: 9, end: 17 });
    const runcheck = await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", RUNCHECK_REMINDER_PAYLOAD);
    assert.equal(runcheck.status, 200, JSON.stringify(runcheck.body));
    assert.deepEqual(storedWindow(), { start: null, end: null });
    workspace = await api.workspace(OWNER);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursStart, null);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursEnd, null);
    assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.timeZone, "America/New_York");
  });

  await t.test("the scheduler skips a user whose local hour is inside quiet hours and delivers on the first run after the window", async () => {
    // The check-in: a credential due 2026-07-27 has an active deadline
    // check-in on 2026-07-26 under the 1-day lead — the fixture
    // tests/rendered-html.test.mjs drives the cron with. Everything is
    // relative to the run's scheduledTime, never to the real clock.
    const due = await api.post(
      OWNER,
      "createCredential",
      customCredential({
        credentialName: "Quiet-hours credential",
        cycleStart: "2026-01-01",
        deadline: "2026-07-27",
      }),
    );
    assert.equal(due.status, 200, JSON.stringify(due.body));
    // A device to deliver to: a real P-256 subscription key, as a browser sends.
    const clientKey = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(
      { name: "ECDH", namedCurve: "P-256" },
      true,
      ["deriveBits"],
    );
    const subscription = {
      endpoint: "https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/quiet-hours-device",
      expirationTime: null,
      keys: {
        p256dh: base64url(
          new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey("raw", clientKey.publicKey)),
        ),
        auth: base64url(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))),
      },
    };
    const device = await api.post(OWNER, "savePushSubscription", {
      subscription,
      deviceLabel: "Quiet-hours phone",
      enableAccountPush: true,
    });
    assert.equal(device.status, 200, JSON.stringify(device.body));
    // Push hour 00:00 UTC (so a 14:00 run is past it); quiet 13 → 15.
    const prefs = await api.post(OWNER, "updateReminderPreferences", {
      inAppEnabled: true,
      pushEnabled: true,
      pushHourLocal: 0,
      leadDays: [90, 30, 7, 1],
      timeZone: "UTC",
      quietHoursStart: 13,
      quietHoursEnd: 15,
    });
    assert.equal(prefs.status, 200, JSON.stringify(prefs.body));
    // VAPID keys the way tests/rendered-html.test.mjs generates them; fetch is
    // stubbed so no push leaves the process.
    const vapidPair = await crypto.subtle.generateKey(
      { name: "ECDSA", namedCurve: "P-256" },
      true,
      ["sign", "verify"],
    );
    const vapidPublicKey = base64url(
      new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey("raw", vapidPair.publicKey)),
    );
    const vapidPrivateKey = (await crypto.subtle.exportKey("jwk", vapidPair.privateKey)).d;
    assert.ok(vapidPrivateKey);
    const userId = api.raw("SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?", OWNER)[0].id;
    const ledgerCount = (where = "") =>
      Number(
        api.raw(
          `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM push_delivery_ledger WHERE user_id = ?${where}`,
          userId,
        )[0].n,
      );
    const runScheduled = async (scheduledTime) => {
      const waits = [];
      await api.worker.scheduled(
        { scheduledTime, cron: "*/15 * * * *" },
        {
          ASSETS: { fetch: async () => new Response("Not found", { status: 404 }) },
          DB: api.db,
          EVIDENCE: api.bucket,
          VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY: vapidPublicKey,
          VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY: vapidPrivateKey,
          VAPID_SUBJECT: "https://itrack.example",
        },
        {
          waitUntil(promise) {
            waits.push(promise);
          },
          passThroughOnException() {},
        },
      );
      await Promise.all(waits);
    };
    const pushEndpoints = [];
    const originalFetch = globalThis.fetch;
    globalThis.fetch = async (input) => {
      pushEndpoints.push(
        typeof input === "string" ? input : input instanceof URL ? input.href : input.url,
      );
      return new Response(null, { status: 201 });
    };
    try {
      assert.equal(ledgerCount(), 0);
      await runScheduled(Date.parse("2026-07-26T14:00:00.000Z")); // 14:00 UTC — inside 13 → 15
      assert.equal(ledgerCount(), 0, "inside quiet hours nothing is materialised");
      assert.deepEqual(pushEndpoints, [], "and nothing is sent");
      await runScheduled(Date.parse("2026-07-26T16:00:00.000Z")); // 16:00 UTC — the first run after the window
      assert.ok(ledgerCount() >= 1, "after the window the check-in is materialised");
      assert.ok(
        pushEndpoints.some((endpoint) => endpoint.endsWith("/quiet-hours-device")),
        `and delivered to the device: ${pushEndpoints.join(", ") || "(nothing sent)"}`,
      );
      assert.ok(ledgerCount(" AND status = 'delivered'") >= 1, "the ledger records the delivery");
    } finally {
      globalThis.fetch = originalFetch;
    }
  });
});

test("booting over a pre-0015 activities and reminder_preferences table adds the four columns", async () => {
  const api = await boot({ pre0015Tables: true });
  const names = (table) => api.raw(`PRAGMA table_info(${table})`).map((column) => column.name);
  assert.deepEqual(
    names("activities").filter((name) => name === "format" || name === "notes"),
    [],
    "the pre-0015 activities table must start without format and notes",
  );
  assert.deepEqual(
    names("reminder_preferences").filter((name) => name.startsWith("quiet_hours_")),
    [],
    "the pre-0015 reminder_preferences table must start without the quiet-hours pair",
  );

  await api.workspace(OWNER); // first request: initializeDatabase + ensureRichRuleColumns

  const activityColumns = api.raw("PRAGMA table_info(activities)");
  for (const name of ["format", "notes"]) {
    const column = activityColumns.find((candidate) => candidate.name === name);
    assert.ok(column, `${name} missing from ${activityColumns.map((c) => c.name).join(", ")}`);
    assert.equal(column.type, "TEXT");
    assert.equal(column.notnull, 0);
    assert.equal(column.dflt_value, null);
  }
  const preferenceColumns = api.raw("PRAGMA table_info(reminder_preferences)");
  for (const name of ["quiet_hours_start", "quiet_hours_end"]) {
    const column = preferenceColumns.find((candidate) => candidate.name === name);
    assert.ok(column, `${name} missing from ${preferenceColumns.map((c) => c.name).join(", ")}`);
    assert.equal(column.type, "INTEGER");
    assert.equal(column.notnull, 0);
    assert.equal(column.dflt_value, null);
  }
  // The preference row the first request seeded lives in the upgraded table and reads back as "no window".
  const workspace = await api.workspace(OWNER);
  assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursStart, null);
  assert.equal(workspace.reminderPreferences.quietHoursEnd, null);
  // And a write through the new columns lands.
  const created = await api.post(OWNER, "createCredential", customCredential());
  assert.equal(created.status, 200, JSON.stringify(created.body));
  const logged = await api.post(OWNER, "addActivity", {
    title: "Post-upgrade course",
    provider: "Wave 4",
    completionDate: isoDaysFromToday(-10),
    totalUnits: 1,
    credentialId: created.body.id,
    format: "self_study",
    notes: "Logged after the ALTERs",
  });
  assert.equal(logged.status, 200, JSON.stringify(logged.body));
  assert.deepEqual(
    api.raw("SELECT format, notes FROM activities WHERE id = ?", logged.body.id),
    [{ format: "self_study", notes: "Logged after the ALTERs" }],
  );
});

**5b — `tests/isolation.test.mjs`: the export filters and the two columns.** The subtest `await t.test("GET /api/export as B exports only B's activities", …)` (`:706-713`; `grep -n "exports only B's activities" tests/isolation.test.mjs`) ends with `  });` followed by a blank line and `  await t.test("GET /api/export/packet refuses A's credential for B in JSON and HTML", …` (`:715`). Insert between them (after the `});` of the export subtest, before the packet subtest):

```js
  // Task 4 (Wave 4): the export's query filters gate the ACTIVITY, and the
  // two new columns ride at the end of every row. Everything below writes B's
  // data only, so "identity A is byte-for-byte unchanged" at the end holds.
  const exportAs = async (id, search = "") => {
    const response = await fetchAs(id, `/api/export${search}`);
    const text = await response.text();
    return {
      status: response.status,
      headers: response.headers,
      text,
      lines: text.replace(/^\uFEFF/, "").trimEnd().split("\r\n"),
    };
  };
  // Every cell is quoted and no seeded title contains a quote, so the title is
  // the text between the row's first `"` and its first `",`.
  const titlesOf = (lines) =>
    lines.slice(1).map((line) => line.slice(1, line.indexOf('",'))).sort();
  let bravoSecondCredentialId = "";

  await t.test("GET /api/export ends every row with Format and Notes and writes the format's label", async () => {
    const tagged = await post(B, "addActivity", {
      title: "Bravo tagged course",
      provider: "Bravo U",
      completionDate: "2026-06-10",
      totalUnits: 1,
      allocatedUnits: 1,
      credentialId: seedB.credentialId,
      requirementIds: [seedB.requirementId],
      format: "conference",
      notes: "Room 4",
    });
    assert.equal(tagged.status, 200, await tagged.text());
    const { status, lines } = await exportAs(B);
    assert.equal(status, 200);
    assert.equal(
      lines[0],
      '"Activity","Provider","Completion date","Activity units","Evidence status","Evidence reference","Credential","Jurisdiction","Requirement tags","Allocated units","Format","Notes"',
    );
    const taggedRow = lines.find((line) => line.startsWith('"Bravo tagged course",'));
    assert.ok(taggedRow, lines.join("\n"));
    assert.ok(taggedRow.endsWith(',"Conference","Room 4"'), taggedRow);
    const plainRow = lines.find((line) => line.startsWith('"Bravo course",'));
    assert.ok(plainRow, lines.join("\n"));
    assert.ok(plainRow.endsWith(',"",""'), plainRow);
  });

  await t.test("?credentialId= narrows the export to that credential's activities", async () => {
    const second = await post(B, "createCredential", {
      credentialName: "Bravo second",
      profession: "Social work",
      jurisdiction: "New Jersey",
      issuer: "Bravo second board",
      totalRequired: 10,
      unitLabel: "hours",
      cycleStart: "2026-01-01",
      deadline: "2027-12-31",
      categories: [{ name: "General", requiredUnits: 10 }],
    });
    assert.equal(second.status, 200, await second.text());
    bravoSecondCredentialId = (await second.json()).id;
    const logged = await post(B, "addActivity", {
      title: "Bravo second course",
      provider: "Bravo U",
      completionDate: "2026-05-01",
      totalUnits: 1,
      allocatedUnits: 1,
      credentialId: bravoSecondCredentialId,
    });
    assert.equal(logged.status, 200, await logged.text());
    const onlySecond = await exportAs(B, `?credentialId=${bravoSecondCredentialId}`);
    assert.equal(onlySecond.status, 200);
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf(onlySecond.lines), ["Bravo second course"]);
    const onlyFirst = await exportAs(B, `?credentialId=${seedB.credentialId}`);
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf(onlyFirst.lines), ["Bravo course", "Bravo tagged course"]);
    // A's credential id as B: the header alone — the EXISTS joins credentials on B's user_id.
    const foreign = await exportAs(B, `?credentialId=${seedA.credentialId}`);
    assert.equal(foreign.status, 200);
    assert.equal(foreign.lines.length, 1, foreign.text);
  });

  await t.test("?from= and ?to= bound the completion date inclusively", async () => {
    // B now holds 2026-05-01 (second), 2026-06-02 (seed) and 2026-06-10 (tagged).
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf((await exportAs(B, "?from=2026-06-01")).lines), [
      "Bravo course",
      "Bravo tagged course",
    ]);
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf((await exportAs(B, "?to=2026-05-31")).lines), ["Bravo second course"]);
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf((await exportAs(B, "?from=2026-06-02&to=2026-06-02")).lines), [
      "Bravo course",
    ]);
    const none = await exportAs(B, "?from=2026-07-01");
    assert.equal(none.status, 200);
    assert.equal(none.lines.length, 1, none.text);
    assert.ok(none.text.endsWith("\r\n"), "the header line still ends with CRLF");
  });

  await t.test("?tag= matches a requirement name, alone and with a credential", async () => {
    const general = await exportAs(B, "?tag=General");
    assert.equal(general.status, 200);
    assert.ok(titlesOf(general.lines).includes("Bravo tagged course"), general.text);
    const nope = await exportAs(B, "?tag=Nope");
    assert.equal(nope.status, 200);
    assert.equal(nope.lines.length, 1, nope.text);
    const combined = await exportAs(B, `?tag=General&credentialId=${bravoSecondCredentialId}`);
    assert.ok(!titlesOf(combined.lines).includes("Bravo tagged course"), combined.text);
  });

  await t.test("a malformed from or to is 400 invalid_date; an empty value is not set", async () => {
    for (const search of ["?from=09/15/2026", "?to=2026-9-1", "?from=2026-06-01&to=tomorrow"]) {
      const response = await fetchAs(B, `/api/export${search}`);
      assert.equal(response.status, 400, search);
      assert.equal(response.headers.get("cache-control"), "no-store");
      assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), {
        error: "Choose the dates as YYYY-MM-DD.",
        code: "invalid_date",
      });
    }
    const empty = await exportAs(B, "?from=&to=&credentialId=&tag=");
    assert.equal(empty.status, 200);
    assert.deepEqual(titlesOf(empty.lines), ["Bravo course", "Bravo second course", "Bravo tagged course"]);
  });

```

(`fetchAs`, `post`, `seedA`, `seedB`, `A`/`B` and `t` are all in scope at that point of the top-level test; "Bravo course" is `seedB.activityTitle`, dated `2026-06-02` by `seedOwner`.)

   function isWholeHour(value: unknown): value is number {
     return (
       typeof value === "number" &&
       Number.isInteger(value) &&
       value >= 0 &&
       value <= 23
     );
   }

   // Quiet hours (Wave 4 Account reminders): both bounds as whole hours 0-23
   // and different, or both absent / null. Absent means "no window" — the
   // upsert always writes both columns, so a client that omits them (the
   // run-check's payload, a Wave 3 client) clears any earlier window rather
   // than leaving it half-set. 0 is an hour, never "absent".
   function quietHoursField(payload: JsonRecord): {
     start: number | null;
     end: number | null;
   } {
     const start = payload.quietHoursStart;
     const end = payload.quietHoursEnd;
     const startUnset = start === undefined || start === null;
     const endUnset = end === undefined || end === null;
     if (startUnset && endUnset) return { start: null, end: null };
     if (!isWholeHour(start) || !isWholeHour(end) || start === end) {
       throw new RequestError(
         "quietHoursStart and quietHoursEnd must both be hours 0-23, or both be null",
         400,
         "invalid_quiet_hours",
       );
     }
     return { start, end };
   }

   ```

   // The Log activity Details step's "Format" keys → the labels the sheet
   // shows (copy table, Task 10). Task 15 moves this map, with the query, into

   const FORMAT_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
     live_course: "Live course",
     live_webinar: "Live webinar",
     self_study: "On-demand or self-study",
     conference: "Conference",
     other: "Other",
   };

   type ExportFilters = {
     from: string | null;
     to: string | null;
     credentialId: string | null;
     tag: string | null;
   };

   // Optional narrowing (the Activity log's filters, Task 11). A missing or
   // empty value is "not set"; `from`/`to` must be YYYY-MM-DD as typed — no
   // slicing before the test, or "2026-06-01x" would pass as "2026-06-01".
   function exportFilters(request: Request): ExportFilters | "invalid_date" {
     const params = new URL(request.url).searchParams;
     const read = (key: string) => params.get(key)?.trim() || null;
     const from = read("from");
     const to = read("to");
     if (
       (from !== null && !ISO_DATE_PATTERN.test(from)) ||
       (to !== null && !ISO_DATE_PATTERN.test(to))
     ) {
       return "invalid_date";
     }
     return {
       from,
       to,
       credentialId: read("credentialId")?.slice(0, 160) ?? null,
       tag: read("tag")?.slice(0, 100) ?? null,
     };
   }
   ```

       const filters = exportFilters(request);
       if (filters === "invalid_date") {

           { error: "Choose the dates as YYYY-MM-DD.", code: "invalid_date" },
           { status: 400, headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
         );
       }
       // Filters gate the ACTIVITY (one EXISTS per clause), never the joined
       // allocation row, so a matching activity keeps every allocation line.
       // They are appended after the `AND a.archived_at IS NULL` that
       // tests/rendered-html.test.mjs pins, and with no query the SQL is
       // byte-identical to Wave 3's.
       const clauses: string[] = [];
       const bindings: unknown[] = [identity.userId];
       if (filters.from) {
         clauses.push("AND a.completion_date >= ?");
         bindings.push(filters.from);
       }
       if (filters.to) {
         clauses.push("AND a.completion_date <= ?");
         bindings.push(filters.to);
       }
       if (filters.credentialId) {
         clauses.push(`AND EXISTS (
               SELECT 1
               FROM activity_allocations f
               JOIN credentials fc
                 ON fc.id = f.credential_id AND fc.user_id = a.user_id
               WHERE f.activity_id = a.id AND fc.id = ?
             )`);
         bindings.push(filters.credentialId);
       }
       if (filters.tag) {
         // The client's tag rule (Task 11 activityTags): the matched requirement
         // names when matches exist, else the allocation's direct requirement.
         clauses.push(`AND EXISTS (
               SELECT 1
               FROM activity_allocations f
               LEFT JOIN activity_requirement_matches m ON m.allocation_id = f.id
               LEFT JOIN credential_requirements r
                 ON r.id = COALESCE(m.requirement_id, f.requirement_id)
               WHERE f.activity_id = a.id AND r.name = ?
             )`);
         bindings.push(filters.tag);
       }
       const filterSql = clauses.map((clause) => `\n          ${clause}`).join("");
   ```

### Task 5: Workspace store and composition root at pixel parity: workspaceApi.ts, workspaceStore.tsx (WorkspaceProvider/useWorkspace, run() with per-caller errors, 13 modal slices, row actions with Undo), useReminderLaunch, useCatalog, ModalsHost, WorkspaceStates, Banners, allocators/ProgressRow as files, useActivityDraft/usePushDevice/useCalendarActions; selectedCredentialId deleted

**Rationale:** spec §1.5 ("decompose while restyling; no fresh client") and the §2 Wave 4 finish gate ("no code left in `ITrackApp.tsx` beyond composition") need one owner for the app state before any screen can leave the monolith: today `ITrackApp()` (`app/ITrackApp.tsx:1327-6380` at main @c6b1fe4) holds 43 `useState`, 8 `useRef`, 13 `useMemo`, 12 `useCallback`, 14 `useEffect` and 51 handlers, and hands 72 props to five views plus nine `() => { setError(""); setX(…) }` closures whose only reason is that the thirteen modals are rendered in the root. Four audit findings are closed here rather than screen by screen: **architecture-04 / app-ux-24** — one global `error` string (`:1380`) is written by every write and rendered at once by the page banner (`:3957-3967`) and by whichever modal is open (the seven `<ModalError … message={error}>` sites at `:4650, 5243, 5440, 5738, 5891, 6072, 6239`), so a failed row write shows up inside an unrelated sheet and a failed sheet submit shows up in the banner behind the inert page; after this task `run()` returns the failure to its caller and only keyed row writes and refetch failures reach the banner, which now renders `what`/`next` copy instead of the raw server sentence (spec §6 copy rule "a server string is never the visible sentence", through Task 2's `describeApiError`). **architecture-05** — `selectedCredentialId` (`:1336`) is written by four mechanisms (`loadWorkspace :1697`, `openActivityEntryFor :1549/1573`, the `popstate` mirror `:2143-2151`, `openCredentialDetail :3908-3916`) and read by the submission, acceptance and reminders modals through `selectedCredential` (`:2111-2122`); it is deleted, the two milestone modals take the credential they act on from the request that opened them, Home shows `workspace.activeCycleId`'s credential (the second half of `:2111-2122`) until Task 8's ledger, and the Log sheet keeps its credential as local state seeded from the shortcut, the restored draft or the active cycle in that order (`:1543-1580`). **architecture-14** — the modals, the load states, the banners, the allocators and `ProgressRow` become files with props and hooks instead of closures over root state; the two `document.getElementById(…).focus()` calls in `archiveActivityRecord`/`restoreActivityRecord` (`:3607-3610, 3624-3627`) and their task-editor twins (`:3805-3808, 3823-3826`) are kept verbatim this task and retired by Task 11 with the Activity log. **app-ux-M-01** stays closed: `handleSessionEnded` keeps its exact spelling in the new store so `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs:63-98` still finds one owner, ≥ 6 gated and ≥ 5 ungated modal sites, and every ungated setter. The proof is pixel parity (`tests/e2e/parity.spec.ts`, baselines shot on the parent commit — the only intended pixel change, the page banner's copy, never renders on the demo identity), the four e2e projects with exactly one spec edit (the hero-switch describe in `instruments.spec.ts:122-176`, whose premise — the sheet's credential select re-pointing Home's hero — is exactly the coupling architecture-05 removes), and the static guards.

**Decisions.** (1) **One React context.** `WorkspaceProvider` in `app/lib/workspaceStore.tsx` owns the workspace, its load status, the online flag, the pending-key array, the page error, the thirteen modal slices, the two new slices (`focusRequest`, `recentlyClosedSeriesId`) and the row-level actions; `useWorkspace()` reads it and throws outside the provider. A bare hook cannot work because the store must be ONE instance above the route switch (one fetch, one pending array, one conflict reload); an external store library is excluded by spec decision 5 and the `package.json` rule. The value is a `useMemo` listing every field; every handler placed in it is a `useCallback` (or lives in a `useMemo`'d object) with complete deps, so `react-hooks/preserve-manual-memoization` and `exhaustive-deps` stay quiet. Only one screen mounts at a time, so fan-out is bounded; `ModalsHost` re-renders with the store, which it needs. (2) **`run()` keeps `runAction`'s array semantics** (`:2272` push, `:2334-2341` remove ONE occurrence in `finally` — two concurrent same-key writes stay pending until both settle; the array is copied with `slice()` before `splice`, as today). It never writes `error.page` when the key is `FORM_ACTION_KEY` (the default): it returns `{ ok: false, copy, code }` and the caller renders it. It writes `error.page` for a keyed row write unless the caller passes `surface: "caller"` — the one addition to the brief's `RunOptions`, used by `actions.deleteCredential`, whose only caller is the delete dialog and whose failure must stay inside that dialog rather than on a banner the dialog has just made inert. The conflict branch (`:2295-2320`) stays inside `run`: `isConflictCode(code)` → `await reload()`; when the reload succeeded, `closeAllEditors()` (the six editor slices, `:2309-2314`); `credential_archived` additionally shows the one error toast the copy table names (section D, "`credential_archived` handling", owner 5) and never sets `error.page`. Offline (`:2265-2270`) becomes `setIsOnline(false)` plus a returned `OFFLINE_ERROR`; a lapsed session becomes `handleSessionEnded()` plus a returned `SESSION_ENDED_ERROR`; a fetch that never reached the server returns `NETWORK_ERROR`. Success: `await reload()`, the optional success toast, `{ ok: true, id }`. (3) **`handleSessionEnded` is spelled exactly** `const handleSessionEnded = useCallback(() => {` … `}, []);` in `workspaceStore.tsx`, with `setWorkspace(null)` and every modal setter (`setEditingActivity(null)`, `setTaskEditor(null)`, `setInstallHelpOpen(false)`, `setClassificationRepair(null)`, `setEvidenceActivity(null)`, `setCredentialEditor(null)`, `setCredentialDeletion(null)`, `setAllocationActivity(null)`, `setActivityOpen(false)`, `setCredentialOpen(false)`, `setSubmissionCredentialId(null)`, `setAcceptanceCredentialId(null)`, `setRemindersOpen(false)`) in its body; every slice is a plain `useState` — never a reducer, never one `modal` object — because the guard derives setter names from the identifiers in an ungated condition, and independent slices keep nested opens working. (4) **`selectedCredentialId` is deleted** together with the `popstate` mirror (`:2143-2151`), `selectionBeforeActivityEntry` / `restoreSelectionBeforeActivityEntry` (`:1459, 1611-1616`), the `setSelectedCredentialId` lines in `loadWorkspace` (`:1697-1703`), `openActivityEntryFor` (`:1549, 1573, 1576`), `handleAcceptance` (`:3279`), `deleteCredentialRecord` (`:3744`), `openCredentialDetail` (`:3914`) and the reminder-launch resolver (`:2001`), and `finishSavedActivityEntry`'s selection line (`:2407`). `SubmissionModal`/`AcceptanceModal` receive the credential resolved by `ModalsHost` from `modals.submissionCredentialId` / `acceptanceCredentialId`; the legacy `TodayView`/`CredentialDetailScreen` call sites pass the credential they render (`onSubmit={() => modals.open({ kind: "submission", credentialId: credential.id })}`); Home's `credential` prop becomes `workspace.credentials.find((c) => c.id === workspace.activeCycleId) ?? null`; `CredentialsView`'s `selectedId` follows the same credential (on the demo identity that is the one credential, so the `.active` row is unchanged); `openCredentialDetail(id)` is `nav.openCredential(id)`. The Log sheet seeds its credential once, in a lazy `useState` (Decision 8). `tests/e2e/instruments.spec.ts:122-176` (the hero-switch describe) is deleted whole in this commit — its premise no longer exists. (5) **The routed detail resolves only from `workspace.credentials` this task**, not from `archivedCredentials` as the brief's `Routed` sketch drew it: `tests/e2e/credential-edit-archive-delete.spec.ts:26-30` pins that "Archive credential" on the detail lands on `/credentials`, which is exactly the provider's dead-detail replace effect (`:2153-2161`, moved) firing because the archived id is no longer in the open list. Widening the lookup is Task 7's, with the spec rewrite that gives the archived detail its presentation; doing it here would leave that spec red, and every spec must be green at every commit. (6) **ModalsHost sites, exact spelling** (the guard regex is `\{([^{}]+?)\s\?\s\(\s*<\w*Modal\b`): eight gated — `{workspace && activityOpen ? (\n<LogActivityModal`, `{workspace && credentialOpen ? (\n<CredentialSetupModal`, `{workspace && submissionCredential ? (\n<SubmissionModal`, `{workspace && acceptanceCredential ? (\n<AcceptanceModal`, `{workspace && remindersOpen ? (\n<RemindersModal`, `{workspace && allocationActivity ? (\n<AllocationModal`, `{workspace && evidenceActivity ? (\n<EvidenceModal`, `{workspace && credentialEditor ? (\n<CredentialEditorModal` — and five ungated — `{editingActivity ? (\n<ActivityEditorModal`, `{credentialDeletion ? (\n<ConfirmDeleteCredentialModal`, `{taskEditor ? (\n<PersonalTaskEditorModal`, `{installHelpOpen ? (\n<InstallHelpModal`, `{classificationRepair ? (\n<ClassificationModal` — each ungated name has its setter in `handleSessionEnded`. `submissionCredential` and `acceptanceCredential` are resolved in `ModalsHost` (`workspace.credentials.find(...)`, the acceptance one also `status === "submitted"` as the old condition `:5474-5475` did) so both modals receive a non-null `credential` prop and their moved bodies stay verbatim. (7) **Each modal owns its error.** A modal whose body moves verbatim keeps the name `error` and `setError`: `useModalError(title)` (`app/screens/modals/useModalError.ts`, a 20-line helper this task adds beside the modals) returns `[DescribedError | null, setError]` where `setError` accepts a `DescribedError` (a store result), a string (the modal's own validation sentence — the allocator arithmetic messages thrown by `nremtRequirementMatchPayload` and friends are user copy already; they become the summary's one entry with the modal's title as `what`) or `""`/`null` (clear). The seven `ModalError` sites become `<ErrorSummary title="…the existing title…" errors={[{ message: error.next }]} detail={error.detail ?? undefined} />` (the copy table, section A, "every ErrorSummary with a server failure"); the four editor components take `error: DescribedError | null` and `ModalsHost` holds their four error states because their bodies are verbatim and take `error` as a prop. The seven titles keep their words this task (Task 6/10 rewrite them per the copy table). (8) **The Log sheet's credential** is `useState` seeded once with the precedence of `:1543-1580`: a shortcut that named an open credential wins; else a restored draft's credential when it is still open; else, when no draft was restored, the credential Home shows (`activeCycleId`), else the first open cycle; a restored draft whose credential is no longer open seeds `""` and shows the existing warning sentence (derived: `restored && credentialId === ""`, cleared the moment a credential is chosen — `:4514-4515`). The draft purge and the legacy-key migration that ran once per workspace load (`:2056-2080`) run at read time inside `readSavedActivityDraft()` — the same statements, executed before the restore instead of after it, so an expired draft can never be restored on the first open after a load. (9) **`usePushDevice` mounts with the Account route** (`AccountRoute`, the wrapper `Screen` renders for the profile tab), because the Due-date check-ins modal reads only `workspace.reminderPreferences` (verified: no `push` identifier in `:5772-5918`) and no other screen reads the push state; its install branch opens the install sheet through `store.modals.open({ kind: "installHelp" })`. `useCalendarActions` mounts in the Home, detail and Account wrappers. The service-worker registration effect (`:1863-1879`) moves into `useReminderLaunch`, which every route mounts, with one edit: the `.then((registration) => { pushRegistrationRef.current = registration; })` that cached the registration in a push ref is dropped, because the ref now belongs to `usePushDevice`, whose every reader already falls back to `await navigator.serviceWorker.ready` (`:1780-1782, 2465-2467, 2541`); `register()`'s call, scope and `updateViaCache` are byte-identical. (10) **Effects that set state defer** through `window.setTimeout(…, 0)` or an event listener exactly as today (`react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` is at error); `zoneOfferDismissedEarlier` stays a render-time `useMemo` localStorage read inside `Banners.tsx`; `today()` is `useCallback(() => todayLocal(dateZone), [dateZone])` and `nowMs()` is `useCallback(() => Date.now(), [])` — screens call both in handlers and memos, never in a render body. (11) **Two additions to the brief's store shape**, both additive: `sessionEnded(): void` (the store's `handleSessionEnded`, which the evidence, push, catalog and delivery fetches must reach on a 401 — today they call the root's closure directly) and `error.showPage(copy: DescribedError): void` (what `usePushDevice` and `useCalendarActions` use for the banner where they used `setError` today). Two divergences from the brief's interface text, both dictated by the repo: `fetchCatalog()` is typed on the shape the server sends and `loadCatalog` reads — `{ catalog?: CatalogRule[]; error?: string }` (`:1737-1747`), not `{ rules }`; and `useCatalog().selectedNremtNextRule` is a function of the credential it is asked about (`currentNremtCatalogRule(workspace.catalog, credential)`, `:2163-2168`), because there is no app-wide selection left to memo it against. (12) **Only one sentence is new in this task**: the network-failure body `Check your connection, then try again.` under the kept title "We couldn’t reach your workspace." (copy table A's `NETWORK_ERROR` row, owner 5; the `WorkspaceLoadFailure` row delegates every body to `copy.next`). The page banner's "Reload workspace" button is copy-table row A/15 (owner 5). The ABVE refusal sentence (`:3238-3241`) keeps its words and moves from the global banner to an error toast, because it is neither a reload failure nor a keyed write.

The seven fetch sites in the monolith are `GET /api/workspace` (`:1675-1678`), `GET /api/catalog` (`:1731-1733`), the push refresh `POST /api/workspace` (`:1804-1815`), `GET /api/workspace?delivery=` (`:1951-1960`), `runAction`'s and `postPushAction`'s `POST /api/workspace` (`:2275-2279`, `:2354-2358`), `POST /api/evidence` (`:2967-2970`), `GET /api/evidence?activityId=` (`:3002-3005`) and `DELETE /api/evidence/:id` (`:3049-3052`). Create `app/lib/workspaceApi.ts`:

```ts
// The only file under app/ that spells the API paths. Every function hands
// back readApiResponse()'s ApiResult (a lapsed session is a state, a proxy
// page is "unexpected") and never parses a body of its own: the store and
// the hooks map each result through app/lib/copy.ts before anything reaches
// a screen (architecture-04, app-ux-24).
import { readApiResponse, type ApiResult } from "./apiResponse";
import type { CatalogRule, EvidenceFile, Workspace } from "./workspaceTypes";

// tests/helpers/workspaceActions.mjs, in dispatch order. The type keeps a
// screen from posting a label the switch in app/api/workspace/route.ts does
// not have (critic-08).
export const WORKSPACE_ACTION_NAMES = [
  "createCredential",
  "updateCredential",
  "archiveCredential",
  "restoreCredential",
  "deleteCredential",
  "addActivity",
  "updateActivity",
  "archiveActivity",
  "restoreActivity",
  "addActivityAllocation",
  "updateActivityAllocationRequirements",
  "claimWeeklyQuest",
  "toggleTask",
  "createPersonalTask",
  "updatePersonalTask",
  "archivePersonalTask",
  "restorePersonalTask",
  "markSubmitted",
  "markRenewalAccepted",
  "updateRequirementApplicability",
  "saveDentalCheckpoint",
  "updateWeeklyGoal",
  "updateReminderPreferences",
  "savePushSubscription",
  "removePushSubscription",
  "sendTestPush",
  "setReminderState",
] as const;

export type ActionName = (typeof WORKSPACE_ACTION_NAMES)[number];

// What every POST /api/workspace answers: `{ ok, action, id }` on success,
// `{ error, code }` on a refusal.
export type ActionEnvelope = {
  ok?: boolean;
  error?: string;
  code?: string;
  id?: string;
};

const JSON_ACCEPT = { accept: "application/json" } as const;

export async function fetchWorkspace(): Promise<ApiResult<Workspace>> {
  const response = await fetch("/api/workspace", {
    headers: JSON_ACCEPT,
    cache: "no-store",
  });
  return readApiResponse<Workspace>(response);
}

// The template catalog is global reference data; the shape is what
// app/api/catalog/route.ts sends and the chooser reads.
export async function fetchCatalog(): Promise<
  ApiResult<{ catalog?: CatalogRule[]; error?: string }>
> {
  const response = await fetch("/api/catalog", { headers: JSON_ACCEPT });
  return readApiResponse<{ catalog?: CatalogRule[]; error?: string }>(response);
}

export type DeliveryTarget = {
  target?: { credentialId?: unknown; reminderKey?: unknown };
};

// The one-time `?delivery=` token a push alert launched the app with.
export async function fetchDelivery(
  deliveryId: string,
  signal?: AbortSignal,
): Promise<ApiResult<DeliveryTarget>> {
  const response = await fetch(
    `/api/workspace?delivery=${encodeURIComponent(deliveryId)}`,
    { headers: JSON_ACCEPT, cache: "no-store", signal },
  );
  return readApiResponse<DeliveryTarget>(response);
}

export async function postWorkspaceAction(
  action: ActionName,
  payload: Record<string, unknown>,
): Promise<{ response: Response; parsed: ApiResult<ActionEnvelope> }> {
  const response = await fetch("/api/workspace", {
    method: "POST",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json" },
    body: JSON.stringify({ action, payload }),
  });
  return { response, parsed: await readApiResponse<ActionEnvelope>(response) };
}

export type EvidenceUploadEnvelope = {
  ok?: boolean;
  evidence?: EvidenceFile;
  error?: string;
  code?: string;
};

export async function uploadEvidenceFile(
  activityId: string,
  file: File,
): Promise<{ response: Response; parsed: ApiResult<EvidenceUploadEnvelope> }> {
  const payload = new FormData();
  payload.set("activityId", activityId);
  payload.set("file", file);
  const response = await fetch("/api/evidence", { method: "POST", body: payload });
  return {
    response,
    parsed: await readApiResponse<EvidenceUploadEnvelope>(response),
  };
}

export async function listEvidence(
  activityId: string,
): Promise<ApiResult<{ evidence?: EvidenceFile[]; error?: string; code?: string }>> {
  const response = await fetch(
    `/api/evidence?activityId=${encodeURIComponent(activityId)}`,
    { headers: JSON_ACCEPT, cache: "no-store" },
  );
  return readApiResponse<{ evidence?: EvidenceFile[]; error?: string; code?: string }>(
    response,
  );
}

export async function deleteEvidenceFile(
  id: string,
): Promise<{ response: Response; parsed: ApiResult<ActionEnvelope> }> {
  const response = await fetch(`/api/evidence/${encodeURIComponent(id)}`, {
    method: "DELETE",
  });
  return { response, parsed: await readApiResponse<ActionEnvelope>(response) };
}
```

Run: `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json 2>&1 | grep -c 'workspaceApi' ; node --experimental-sqlite --test tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs 2>&1 | grep -E '^# (pass|fail)'`
