### Task 12: Gateway /account/* route family (account-routes.mjs, JSON error grammar, CSRF/session/limiter): GET /account, POST /account/profile, POST /account/password (12-char floor, other sessions dropped); AuthStore.updateDisplayName/changePassword; shared password bucket exposed

**Rationale:** spec §6 lists what Account (was Profile) must offer — "display name, email change (re-verify), password change, reminders …, delete account …. Sign out." — and §8 makes account deletion and email change "gateway-orchestrated" operations that touch both stores. Every one of those needs the same thing first: a route family the signed-in app can call, owned by the gateway (the auth store `/data/auth.db` lives there, not in the worker), answering in the worker's `{ error, code }` grammar so the Account sheets (Task 16) map a code to copy exactly as `describeApiError` does for `/api/*`. This task lands that family with the two operations that touch auth.db alone — the display name and the password — so Tasks 13 and 14 add `delete` and `email` to a tested skeleton instead of inventing one. audit app-ux-M-02 ("No account self-service: display name, email, password and account deletion cannot be changed or requested anywhere in the product"; its recommendation names "change password … requiring the current password") is the finding closed here for name and password. The security posture is reused, never rewritten (spec §3.1, carried by §7): the same Origin/Referer rule as `/auth/*` (`auth-routes.mjs:280-291`), the same session (`sessionForRequest`), `RateLimiter`, `readBody`, and — the point of exposing `passwordAttemptAllowed`/`recordPasswordFailure` — the one per-account failure bucket that login and verify already share (`auth-routes.mjs:196`, keyed `account:${email}` at `:342` and `:380`), so a password cannot be guessed on one route once another has locked it (security-04: the refusal is one generic sentence whatever the reason; infra-M-02: nothing here reveals whether an address has an account — every answer needs a session). A wrong password answers **403**, never 401, because `app/lib/apiResponse.ts:13` reads every 401 as a lapsed session. The 12-character floor lives in `password-policy.mjs` on this route only: signup (`auth-routes.mjs:316`), reset (`:415`) and bootstrap (`bootstrap.mjs:9`) stay at 10 this wave and Wave 5 (§7 "password guidance (12+ characters …)") points them at the module — their tests use 10–11 character passwords and are not this task's to rewrite.

**Decisions.** (1) JSON routes, not HTML forms: the sheets `fetch()` them and render the error in place; every JSON answer carries `content-type: application/json; charset=utf-8` and `cache-control: no-store` (the `sendJson` shape at `gateway.mjs:135-143`). (2) The display name is durable in auth.db only — D1's `users.display_name` is a per-request mirror that `ensureUser` rewrites from the identity header (`db/runtime.ts:6027-6046`), so after `POST /account/profile` the very next proxied request carries the new name (`gateway.mjs:158-164`) and the workspace shows it; no worker action, no migration. (3) `changePassword` keeps the session that made the change (`keepSessionRaw = session.raw`) and drops every other one — `resetPassword` (`auth.mjs:326-335`) drops all because a reset link proves inbox access, not presence at a signed-in device; the sheet's toast ("Password changed. Other devices were signed out.", copy table G) says so. (4) Two limiters: `opLimiter = new RateLimiter(5, 15 * 60 * 1000, { now })` per `op:${userId}` counts every `/account/*` POST that reaches a route (a sheet resubmit is one; a script is not), and a wrong current password also counts in the shared `account:${email}` bucket (10 per 15 min) — once that is tripped the route answers after `sleep(2000)` with the generic 403 and burns no scrypt, the login rule at `auth-routes.mjs:340-348`. (5) `handle` order: CSRF (`Origin ?? Referer` origin must equal `new URL(baseUrl).origin`, else 403 `cross_origin_request` — for every POST; the read-only `GET /account` is exempt, because a same-origin `fetch()` carries no `Origin`, a referrer-suppressing browser, extension or proxy sends no `Referer` either, and a JSON GET behind a `SameSite=Lax` cookie has nothing a CSRF check protects — without the exemption the Account screen could never learn `mailConfigured`/`pendingEmail`/`displayName` on such a browser) → session (`authRoutes.sessionForRequest(req)`, else 401 `authentication_required`) → the method/path table (`GET /account`, `POST /account/profile`, `POST /account/password`; anything else a plain-text 404 `Not Found`, like `/auth/*`'s) → for POSTs: `content-type` must match `/^application\/json(?:\s*;|$)/i` (415), `content-length` ≤ 8192 checked before reading (413 — `readBody` destroys the socket on an overrun, the `gateway.mjs:211-217` pattern), `readBody(req, 8 * 1024)`, `JSON.parse` into a plain object (400) → `opLimiter.allow` (429) → the route. So a malformed body never spends the account's write budget, and a validation 400 from a route (`name_invalid`, `password_policy`) does. Same-origin `fetch()` GETs carry no `Origin` and may carry no `Referer` — hence the exemption; the run-check's `account_get` still sends a Referer (harmless), and the tests prove both the bare GET (200) and the bare POST (403). (6) The handler never logs an address, a name or a password: `console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_name_changed", userId }))` and `{ event: "account_password_changed", userId }` are the only lines. (7) `createGateway` takes `accountRoutes` as an optional dependency (default `null`; the family answers 404 without one, never proxied) so the exception-barrier stack at `tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs:281` — which builds a gateway without it — keeps working; `serve.mjs` always passes one. `internalSecret` is not a gateway parameter: Task 13's `createWorkerCaller` takes it directly. (8) `callWorker` is accepted (and passed as `null` by `serve.mjs` and the tests) but unused until Task 13; `runPendingDeletions` is the stub `{ finished: 0, deferred: 0 }`. (9) The run-check gains `run_account` (three writes: password → rename → password back, so the throwaway is left as found and the function re-runs) but no mode line and no header count — Task 13 wires the `account` mode and Task 20 derives the counts.

- Consumes (`deploy/railway/auth.mjs`): `class AuthStore` — `authenticate(email, password)` (`:260-275`) → `{ ok: false, reason: "bad-credentials" | "unverified" } | { ok: true, user: { id, email, displayName } }` (always burns one scrypt); `sessionUser(rawSessionId)` (`:288-304`, slides the row on every read); `createSession(userId): raw` (`:277-286`); `createVerifiedUser({ email, displayName, password })` (`:189-201`); `deleteSession(raw)` (`:312-316`); module-private `hashPassword` (`:27-31`) and `sha256Hex(value)` (`:50-52`) used inside the class; `#userById(id)` (`:135-142`) → `{ id, email, displayName }`.
- Consumes (`deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs`): `createAuthRoutes({ store, sendEmail, secret, baseUrl, now, sleep, mailConfigured, responseFloorMs })` (`:181-193`) returning `{ handle, sessionForRequest, issueSessionCookie, slideSessionCookie }` (`:436`); `sessionForRequest(req)` (`:201-218`) → `{ user: { id, email, displayName, cookieIssuedAt }, raw, cookie } | null`; `const accountLimiter = new RateLimiter(10, 15 * 60 * 1000, { now })` (`:196`) keyed `` `account:${email}` `` by login (`:342-355`) and verify (`:380-390`); `class RateLimiter` (`:23-55`) with `allow(key): boolean` (counting) and `check(key): boolean` (non-counting); `readBody(req, maxBytes = 32 * 1024): Promise<string>` (`:119-135`, rejects "body too large" and destroys the socket on an overrun); `SESSION_COOKIE` (`:5`), `signValue` (`:61-63`); the CSRF rule (`:280-291`) and the tripped-account rule `await sleep(ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS)` + generic answer, no scrypt (`:168`, `:343-348`).
- Consumes (`deploy/railway/gateway.mjs`): `createGateway({ authRoutes, baseUrl, pagesDir, upstreamPort, now })` (`:75`); the inbound strip loop (`:147-149`); `proxy` forwarding `oai-authenticated-user-email` and the percent-encoded full name (`:158-164`); `sendJson`'s header shape (`:135-143`); the `/auth/` branch (`:307-310`); the declared-`content-length`-first pattern (`:211-217`). (`deploy/railway/serve.mjs:186-202`): `createAuthRoutes` + `createGateway` wiring and `createResendSender` (`email.mjs:5-30`, whose returned function carries `mailConfigured`). (`app/lib/apiResponse.ts:13`): `if (response.status === 401) return { kind: "session-ended", status: 401 };` — the reason a wrong password is 403.
- Consumes (tests): the `tests/auth-routes.test.mjs` harness (`makeRoutes` `:23-42`, `fakeReq` `:44-55`, `fakeRes` `:57-64`, `post` `:66-71`, the `sleeps` recorder and the `console.log` spy at `:617-638`); `tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs` `startStack` (`:15-51`, `upstreamSeen()` = the last upstream request), `get` (`:53-54`), `signedInCookie(stack, email, password)` (`:85-89`, creates a verified user named "User" and a session under the `"gw-secret"` signing key).

- Produces (`deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs`): `export function createAccountRoutes({ store, authRoutes, baseUrl, sendEmail, callWorker = null, now = () => Date.now(), sleep = defaultSleep, mailConfigured = sendEmail.mailConfigured !== false }): { handle(req, res, pathname): Promise<boolean>; runPendingDeletions(): Promise<{ finished: number; deferred: number }> }` — `handle` returns `false` untouched for any path outside `/account` and `/account/…`, `true` after answering; `runPendingDeletions` is the `{ finished: 0, deferred: 0 }` stub until Task 13 (which gives it `{ log }` options and the real body). Routes: `GET /account` → 200 `{ email, identityEmail: email, displayName, pendingEmail: null, mailConfigured }` (`identityEmail` and `pendingEmail` become real in Task 14; `displayName` is `""` for an account that never set one, e.g. a bootstrap account); `POST /account/profile` body `{ name }` → 400 `name_invalid` ("Use 1 to 80 characters for your name.") / 200 `{ ok: true, displayName }`; `POST /account/password` body `{ currentPassword, newPassword }` → 400 `password_policy` ("Use at least 12 characters." / "Use at most 256 characters.") / 403 `password_incorrect` ("That password doesn’t match. Try again.") / 200 `{ ok: true }`. Common answers: 403 `cross_origin_request` ("Cross-origin request rejected."), 401 `authentication_required` ("Sign in to manage your account."), 415 `invalid_content_type` ("Send JSON."), 413 `body_too_large` ("The request is too large."), 400 `invalid_request` ("The request body must be a JSON object."), 429 `rate_limited` ("Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again."), plain-text 404 `Not Found` for unknown paths and methods. Log lines: `{ event: "account_name_changed", userId }`, `{ event: "account_password_changed", userId }`.

WHERE id = ?`; true when one row changed); `changePassword(userId, newPassword, { keepSessionRaw } = {}): boolean` (rehash; with `keepSessionRaw` → `DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ? AND session_hash <> ?`, without → every session of the user; false, nothing touched, for an unknown id).
- Produces (`deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs`): `export const CLEAR_COOKIE`; the returned object adds `passwordAttemptAllowed(email) = accountLimiter.check(\`account:${email}\`)` and `recordPasswordFailure(email) = accountLimiter.allow(\`account:${email}\`)`.

- Produces (`deploy/railway/runcheck.sh`): `login_as <email> <password>` (prints the `itrack_session=…` cookie pair, empty when refused), `ws_as <cookie>`, `account_get <cookie>`, `post_json <cookie> <path> <json>` → `"<status> <body>"`, and `run_account` (needs `THROWAWAY_PASSWORD`, 12+ characters, of the bootstrap account `wave4-throwaway@example.test`; three writes, leaving two of the five per quarter hour for Task 13's delete).
- Produces (tests): `tests/account-routes.test.mjs` with `makeRoutes`, `fakeReq`, `fakeRes`, `signedIn`, `send`/`post`/`get`, `postForm` (Tasks 13 and 14 append their cases to it); `startStack` in `tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs` now builds `accountRoutes` (Task 13 extends it with `upstreamRequests[]`).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the failing test file for the policy module and the route family**

Create `tests/account-routes.test.mjs`:

```js
import test from "node:test";
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { EventEmitter } from "node:events";
import { AuthStore } from "../deploy/railway/auth.mjs";
import { createAccountRoutes } from "../deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs";
import { SESSION_COOKIE, createAuthRoutes, signValue } from "../deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs";
import {
  MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
  MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH,
  passwordProblem,
} from "../deploy/railway/password-policy.mjs";

const SECRET = "test-secret";
const BASE_URL = "https://itrack.test";

// The auth-routes harness, plus the account routes over the same store and
// the same createAuthRoutes instance — that instance owns the per-account
// failure bucket the two route families share (auth-routes.mjs:196).
// `sleeps` records the delays the routes ask for (the 2 s lock delay) instead
// of waiting for them; `sent` would hold mail (nothing in this task sends).
function makeRoutes({ mailConfigured } = {}) {
  let clock = 1_700_000_000_000;
  const store = new AuthStore(":memory:", { now: () => clock });
  const sent = [];
  const sleeps = [];
  const now = () => clock;
  const sleep = async (ms) => { sleeps.push(ms); };
  const sendEmail = async (message) => { sent.push(message); return { ok: true }; };
  const authRoutes = createAuthRoutes({ store, secret: SECRET, baseUrl: BASE_URL, now, sleep, sendEmail });
  const routes = createAccountRoutes({
    store, authRoutes, baseUrl: BASE_URL, sendEmail, callWorker: null, now, sleep,
    ...(mailConfigured === undefined ? {} : { mailConfigured }),
  });
  return { store, authRoutes, routes, sent, sleeps, tick: (ms) => (clock += ms) };
}

function fakeReq({ method = "POST", url = "/account", body = "", headers = {} } = {}) {
  const req = new EventEmitter();
  req.method = method;
  req.url = url;
  req.headers = { host: "itrack.test", origin: BASE_URL, ...headers };
  req.socket = { remoteAddress: "203.0.113.9" };
  process.nextTick(() => {
    if (body) req.emit("data", Buffer.from(body));
    req.emit("end");
  });
  return req;
}

function fakeRes() {
  return {
    statusCode: null, headers: {}, body: "",
    writeHead(status, headers) { this.statusCode = status; Object.assign(this.headers, headers ?? {}); },
    setHeader(name, value) { this.headers[name.toLowerCase()] = value; },
    end(chunk) { this.body += chunk ?? ""; this.ended = true; },
  };
}

// A verified account with one live session, and what a test needs to act as
// it: the Cookie header, the raw session id, the user id and the credentials.
function signedIn(store, email = "acct@e.co", password = "current-pass-12", displayName = "Before") {
  const { userId } = store.createVerifiedUser({ email, displayName, password });
  const raw = store.createSession(userId);
  return { userId, raw, cookie: `${SESSION_COOKIE}=${signValue(raw, SECRET)}`, email, password };
}

// One request to the account routes. `json` is an object (serialised) or a
// raw string (sent as is); a POST carries `content-type: application/json`
// unless the headers say otherwise. The answer's body is parsed when it is JSON.
async function send(routes, { method = "POST", pathname, json, headers = {} }) {
  const body = json === undefined ? "" : typeof json === "string" ? json : JSON.stringify(json);
  const req = fakeReq({
    method, url: pathname, body,
    headers: { ...(method === "POST" ? { "content-type": "application/json" } : {}), ...headers },
  });
  const res = fakeRes();
  const handled = await routes.handle(req, res, pathname);
  let parsed = null;
  try { parsed = JSON.parse(res.body); } catch { parsed = null; }
  return { handled, res, json: parsed };
}
const post = (routes, pathname, json, headers) => send(routes, { pathname, json, headers });
const get = (routes, pathname, headers) => send(routes, { method: "GET", pathname, headers });

// A form POST to the auth routes (login), the way a browser sends it.
async function postForm(authRoutes, pathname, fields, headers = {}) {
  const req = fakeReq({
    url: pathname, body: new URLSearchParams(fields).toString(),
    headers: { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", ...headers },
  });
  const res = fakeRes();
  await authRoutes.handle(req, res, pathname);
  return { res };
}

const PASSWORD_INCORRECT = { error: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.", code: "password_incorrect" };

test("password-policy: 12 to 256 characters; anything else is named, and a missing field is never an empty password that passes", () => {
  assert.equal(MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH, 12);
  assert.equal(MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH, 256);
  assert.equal(passwordProblem("x".repeat(11)), "too_short");
  assert.equal(passwordProblem("x".repeat(12)), null);
  assert.equal(passwordProblem("x".repeat(256)), null);
  assert.equal(passwordProblem("x".repeat(257)), "too_long");
  assert.equal(passwordProblem(""), "too_short");
  assert.equal(passwordProblem(undefined), "too_short");
  assert.equal(passwordProblem(null), "too_short");
  assert.equal(passwordProblem(123456789012), "too_short", "not a string");
});

test("CSRF: without Origin and Referer every /account POST is 403 cross_origin_request; a matching Referer suffices; the read-only GET /account is exempt (a same-origin fetch() carries no Origin, a referrer-suppressing browser no Referer)", async () => {
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie } = signedIn(store);
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "X" }, { origin: undefined, cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Cross-origin request rejected.", code: "cross_origin_request" });
  assert.equal(res.headers["content-type"], "application/json; charset=utf-8");
  assert.equal(res.headers["cache-control"], "no-store");
  ({ res, json } = await get(routes, "/account", { origin: undefined, cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, "the read-only GET needs neither Origin nor Referer");
  assert.equal(json.email, "acct@e.co");
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "X" }, { origin: "https://itrack.test.evil.example", cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403);
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "X" }, { origin: "not a url", cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403, "an unparseable Origin is a mismatch, not a crash");
  ({ res, json } = await get(routes, "/account", { origin: undefined, referer: "https://itrack.test/profile", cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.equal(json.email, "acct@e.co");
});

test("401 authentication_required without a session; unknown paths and methods 404; other prefixes are not handled", async () => {
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();
  let { res, json } = await get(routes, "/account");
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 401);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Sign in to manage your account.", code: "authentication_required" });
  assert.equal(res.headers["cache-control"], "no-store");
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: "a", newPassword: "b".repeat(12) }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 401, "a POST without a session never reaches the password check");
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Sign in to manage your account.", code: "authentication_required" });
  const { cookie } = signedIn(store);
  for (const [method, pathname] of [
    ["GET", "/account/nope"], ["POST", "/account"], ["GET", "/account/profile"],
    ["GET", "/account/password"], ["DELETE", "/account/password"],
  ]) {
    const answer = await send(routes, { method, pathname, headers: { cookie }, json: method === "POST" ? {} : undefined });
    assert.equal(answer.handled, true, `${method} ${pathname}`);
    assert.equal(answer.res.statusCode, 404, `${method} ${pathname}`);
    assert.equal(answer.res.body, "Not Found", `${method} ${pathname}`);
  }
  const outside = await send(routes, { method: "GET", pathname: "/accounts", headers: { cookie } });
  assert.equal(outside.handled, false, "/accounts is not this family");
  assert.equal(outside.res.statusCode, null, "…and nothing was written");
});

test("POST bodies: 415 without JSON, 413 over 8 kB (declared or streamed), 400 for anything but an object; none of them spend the write budget", async () => {
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie } = signedIn(store);
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", "name=X", { cookie, "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded" });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 415);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Send JSON.", code: "invalid_content_type" });
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "X" }, { cookie, "content-type": "" }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 415, "no content-type at all");
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "X" }, { cookie, "content-length": "9000" }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 413, "the declared length is checked before the body is read");
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "The request is too large.", code: "body_too_large" });
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "x".repeat(9000) }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 413, "an undeclared overrun is caught by readBody");
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "The request is too large.", code: "body_too_large" });
  for (const raw of ["", "[]", "\"x\"", "null", "42", "{not json"]) {
    ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", raw, { cookie }));
    assert.equal(res.statusCode, 400, JSON.stringify(raw));
    assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "The request body must be a JSON object.", code: "invalid_request" }, JSON.stringify(raw));
  }
  // Ten rejected bodies later the account still has all five writes: the
  // limiter counts only what reaches a route.
  for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i += 1) {
    ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: `Fine ${i}` }, { cookie }));
    assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, `write ${i}`);
  }
});

test("GET /account returns the profile shape: email, identityEmail (= email until Task 14), displayName, pendingEmail null, mailConfigured", async () => {
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie } = signedIn(store, "who@e.co", "current-pass-12", "Who Ami");
  const { res, json } = await get(routes, "/account", { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.equal(res.headers["content-type"], "application/json; charset=utf-8");
  assert.equal(res.headers["cache-control"], "no-store");
  assert.equal(res.headers["content-length"], Buffer.byteLength(res.body));
  assert.deepEqual(json, {
    email: "who@e.co", identityEmail: "who@e.co", displayName: "Who Ami", pendingEmail: null, mailConfigured: true,
  });
  // A bootstrap account has no name yet (bootstrap.mjs:36 passes null): the
  // field is an empty string, never null, so the sheet's input has a value.
  const boot = signedIn(store, "boot@e.co", "boot-pass-12345", null);
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie: boot.cookie })).json.displayName, "");
  // mailConfigured is configuration, reported up front (Task 14's email sheet
  // reads it before any attempt) — passed explicitly…
  const unconfigured = makeRoutes({ mailConfigured: false });
  const { cookie: c2 } = signedIn(unconfigured.store);
  assert.equal((await get(unconfigured.routes, "/account", { cookie: c2 })).json.mailConfigured, false);
  // …or read off the sender, as createAuthRoutes does (email.mjs:28).
  const send = Object.assign(async () => ({ ok: false, error: "mail_unconfigured" }), { mailConfigured: false });
  const store2 = new AuthStore(":memory:");
  const auth2 = createAuthRoutes({ store: store2, secret: SECRET, baseUrl: BASE_URL, sleep: async () => {}, sendEmail: send });
  const fromSender = createAccountRoutes({
    store: store2, authRoutes: auth2, baseUrl: BASE_URL, sendEmail: send, callWorker: null, sleep: async () => {},
  });
  const { cookie: c3 } = signedIn(store2);
  assert.equal((await get(fromSender, "/account", { cookie: c3 })).json.mailConfigured, false, "read off the sender when not passed explicitly");
});

test("POST /account/profile: 400 name_invalid for '', whitespace and 81 characters; 200 renames what the session and sign-in carry; 80 is the ceiling", async () => {
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, raw, email, password } = signedIn(store);
  // Five writes reach a route in this test — exactly the account's budget.
  for (const name of ["", "   ", "x".repeat(81)]) {
    const { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name }, { cookie });
    assert.equal(res.statusCode, 400, JSON.stringify(name));
    assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Use 1 to 80 characters for your name.", code: "name_invalid" });
  }
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(raw).displayName, "Before", "a refused name changes nothing");
  const { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "  After Hours  " }, {
    cookie, "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true, displayName: "After Hours" });
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(raw).displayName, "After Hours", "what the gateway forwards on the next proxied request");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate(email, password).user.displayName, "After Hours");
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.displayName, "After Hours");
  assert.equal((await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "y".repeat(80) }, { cookie })).res.statusCode, 200, "the signup ceiling, auth-routes.mjs:316");
});

test("POST /account/password: 400 password_policy under 12 or over 256; 403 password_incorrect for a wrong or missing current password, and the failure counts in the bucket login shares", async () => {
  const { store, authRoutes, routes, sleeps } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, raw, email, password } = signedIn(store);
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: password, newPassword: "x".repeat(11) }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 400);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Use at least 12 characters.", code: "password_policy" });
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: password, newPassword: "x".repeat(257) }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 400);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Use at most 256 characters.", code: "password_policy" });
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { newPassword: "x".repeat(12) }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403, "a missing current password is a wrong one");
  assert.deepEqual(json, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: "not-it-1234567", newPassword: "x".repeat(12) }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403);
  assert.deepEqual(json, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
  assert.equal(store.authenticate(email, password).ok, true, "nothing changed");
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(raw), "the session survives a refusal");
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [], "under the limit there is no delay");
  // Those two failures sit in the same `account:<email>` bucket that login
  // fills (auth-routes.mjs:342-355): eight wrong logins bring it to ten, and
  // the next attempt — the right password, at login — is refused with the
  // lock delay. One route cannot be used to guess what another has locked.
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i += 1) {
    const login = await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/login", { email, password: "wrong-pass-1" }, { "x-forwarded-for": `10.0.${i}.1` });
    assert.equal(login.res.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials", `wrong login ${i}`);
  }
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [], "ten failures do not delay; the eleventh attempt does");
  const locked = await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/login", { email, password }, { "x-forwarded-for": "10.9.9.9" });
  assert.equal(locked.res.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials", "even the right password is refused while tripped");
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [2000]);
});

test("POST /account/password: once login has tripped the account bucket, the route answers 403 after the 2 s delay without hashing — even for the right password", async () => {
  const { store, authRoutes, routes, sleeps, tick } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, raw, email, password } = signedIn(store);
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) {
    await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/login", { email, password: "wrong-pass-1" }, { "x-forwarded-for": `10.1.${i}.1` });
  }
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), false);
  let authenticateCalls = 0;
  const original = store.authenticate.bind(store);
  store.authenticate = (...args) => { authenticateCalls += 1; return original(...args); };
  const { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: password, newPassword: "brand-new-pass-12" }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403);
  assert.deepEqual(json, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [2000]);
  assert.equal(authenticateCalls, 0, "scrypt is not burned for a tripped account");
  assert.equal(original(email, password).ok, true, "the password did not change");
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(raw), "…and the session was not touched");
  // The bucket is a fixed fifteen-minute window (RateLimiter.allow): after
  // it, the same request would go through.
  tick(15 * 60 * 1000 + 1);
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), true);
});

test("passwordAttemptAllowed / recordPasswordFailure expose the login bucket: ten recorded failures trip it for login too, per account", async () => {
  const { store, authRoutes, sleeps } = makeRoutes();
  const { email, password } = signedIn(store);
  for (let i = 0; i < 9; i += 1) authRoutes.recordPasswordFailure(email);
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), true, "nine is under the limit");
  authRoutes.recordPasswordFailure(email);
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), false);
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed("other@e.co"), true, "per account");
  const locked = await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/login", { email, password });
  assert.equal(locked.res.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials");
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [2000], "login honours what the account routes recorded");
});

test("POST /account/password: 200 rehashes, keeps this session, drops the other device's, and the new password signs in", async () => {
  const { store, authRoutes, routes } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, raw, userId, email, password } = signedIn(store);
  const other = store.createSession(userId);
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(other));
  const { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/password", { currentPassword: password, newPassword: "brand-new-pass-12" }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true });
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(raw), "the session that made the change stays signed in");
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(other), null, "every other device is signed out");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate(email, password).ok, false, "the old password is gone");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate(email, "brand-new-pass-12").ok, true);
  const login = await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/login", { email, password: "brand-new-pass-12" });
  assert.equal(login.res.headers.location, "/");
  assert.match(login.res.headers["set-cookie"], new RegExp(`^${SESSION_COOKIE}=`));
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).res.statusCode, 200, "the kept session still answers");
});

test("429 rate_limited after five POSTs in fifteen minutes for one account; GETs and other accounts are unaffected; the window resets", async () => {
  const { store, routes, tick } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie } = signedIn(store);
  for (let i = 1; i <= 5; i += 1) {
    const { res } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: `Name ${i}` }, { cookie });
    assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, `write ${i}`);
  }
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "Name 6" }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 429);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again.", code: "rate_limited" });
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.displayName, "Name 5", "the sixth write did not land; reads still answer");
  const { cookie: otherCookie } = signedIn(store, "other@e.co");
  assert.equal((await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "Other" }, { cookie: otherCookie })).res.statusCode, 200, "per account, not global");
  tick(15 * 60 * 1000 + 1);
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/profile", { name: "Name 7" }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, "a new window");
});
```

- [ ] **Step 5: The password policy module**

Create `deploy/railway/password-policy.mjs`:

```js
// The password floor for the account routes (spec §6 Account). Length only:
// the top-10k list and the signup/reset/bootstrap floors are Wave 5's (§7
// "password guidance (12+ characters, checked against a top-10k list)");
// until then signup (auth-routes.mjs:316), reset (:415) and bootstrap
// (bootstrap.mjs:9) keep their own 10. `length` counts UTF-16 code units,
// the same measure those checks apply.
export const MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 12;
export const MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH = 256;

// "too_short" | "too_long" | null. Anything that is not a string is too
// short: a missing field must never pass as an empty password that fits.
export function passwordProblem(password) {
  if (typeof password !== "string" || password.length < MIN_PASSWORD_LENGTH) return "too_short";
  if (password.length > MAX_PASSWORD_LENGTH) return "too_long";
  return null;
}
```

- [ ] **Step 6: The two store methods**

In `deploy/railway/auth.mjs`, insert the following between line 335 (the `  }` that closes `resetPassword`, whose last statement is `    return user ? { email: user.email } : null;` at `:334`) and the comment at `:337` that begins `  // Rows whose address is not printable ASCII — created before signup`:

```js

  // The display name lives here. D1's users.display_name is a per-request
  // mirror that ensureUser (db/runtime.ts) rewrites from the identity header
  // the gateway forwards, so the next proxied request carries the new name to
  // the worker; no worker action exists or is needed.
  updateDisplayName(userId, name) {
    const changed = this.db
      .prepare("UPDATE users SET display_name = ? WHERE id = ?")
      .run(String(name), userId).changes;
    return Number(changed) === 1;
  }

  // Rehashes and signs every OTHER device out. resetPassword drops all
  // sessions because a reset link proves inbox access, not presence at a
  // signed-in device; a change made from a signed-in session keeps that one
  // (`keepSessionRaw` is the raw session id the cookie carries). An unknown
  // id changes nothing and returns false.
  changePassword(userId, newPassword, { keepSessionRaw } = {}) {
    const changed = this.db
      .prepare("UPDATE users SET password_scrypt = ? WHERE id = ?")
      .run(hashPassword(newPassword), userId).changes;
    if (Number(changed) !== 1) return false;
    if (keepSessionRaw) {
      this.db
        .prepare("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ? AND session_hash <> ?")
        .run(userId, sha256Hex(String(keepSessionRaw)));
    } else {
      this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?").run(userId);
    }
    return true;
  }
```

(`hashPassword` at `:27` and `sha256Hex` at `:50` are the module's own helpers; nothing new is imported.)

- [ ] **Step 8: The account routes**

Create `deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs`:

```js
// HTTP handlers for /account/* — the signed-in account's own profile,
// display name and password (spec §6 Account; Tasks 13 and 14 add delete and
// email change). JSON in, JSON out, in the worker's error grammar
// `{ error, code }`: the Account screen's sheets fetch() these routes and
// render the code's copy in place. A wrong password is 403, never 401 — the
// app reads every 401 as a lapsed session (app/lib/apiResponse.ts).
//
// The auth posture is reused, never rewritten (spec §3.1, §7): the same
// Origin/Referer rule as /auth/*, the session from createAuthRoutes,
// RateLimiter, readBody, and the per-account failure bucket login and verify
// already share. Nothing here says whether an address has an account: every
// answer needs a session first.
import { RateLimiter, readBody } from "./auth-routes.mjs";
import { passwordProblem } from "./password-policy.mjs";

const MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES = 8 * 1024;
// The login rule (auth-routes.mjs, the tripped-account branch): once the
// account bucket is tripped, answer after a fixed delay with the generic
// refusal and burn no scrypt.
const ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS = 2000;
const JSON_CONTENT_TYPE_RE = /^application\/json(?:\s*;|$)/i;
const defaultSleep = (ms) => new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, ms));

const PASSWORD_INCORRECT = { error: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.", code: "password_incorrect" };
const RATE_LIMITED = { error: "Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again.", code: "rate_limited" };

function json(res, status, payload) {
  const body = JSON.stringify(payload);
  res.writeHead(status, {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
    "cache-control": "no-store",
    "content-length": Buffer.byteLength(body),
  });
  res.end(body);
  return true;
}

function notFound(res) {
  res.writeHead(404, { "content-type": "text/plain" });
  res.end("Not Found");
  return true;
}

export function createAccountRoutes({
  store,
  authRoutes,
  baseUrl,
  sendEmail,
  // Task 13's delete route calls the worker through this; null until then.
  callWorker = null,
  now = () => Date.now(),
  sleep = defaultSleep,
  // Decided from configuration, never from whether an address has an
  // account — the same flag createAuthRoutes reads off the sender.
  mailConfigured = sendEmail.mailConfigured !== false,
}) {
  const expectedOrigin = new URL(baseUrl).origin;
  // Five writes per account per quarter hour, whatever the route: a sheet
  // resubmit is one, a script hammering the routes is not. Counted only
  // when a well-formed body reaches a route (see handle).
  const opLimiter = new RateLimiter(5, 15 * 60 * 1000, { now });

  // A POST body as a plain JSON object, or the answer already written and
  // null. Nothing here counts against the account's write budget.
  async function readJsonBody(req, res) {
    if (!JSON_CONTENT_TYPE_RE.test(String(req.headers["content-type"] ?? ""))) {
      json(res, 415, { error: "Send JSON.", code: "invalid_content_type" });
      return null;
    }
    // Declared size first: readBody() destroys the socket when the stream
    // overruns, which would swallow the 413 (the gateway's beacon does the
    // same). Browsers and fetch() always send Content-Length for a string.
    if (Number(req.headers["content-length"] ?? 0) > MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES) {
      json(res, 413, { error: "The request is too large.", code: "body_too_large" });
      return null;
    }
    let text;
    try {
      text = await readBody(req, MAX_JSON_BODY_BYTES);
    } catch {
      json(res, 413, { error: "The request is too large.", code: "body_too_large" });
      return null;
    }
    let body;
    try {
      body = JSON.parse(text);
    } catch {
      body = undefined;
    }
    if (typeof body !== "object" || body === null || Array.isArray(body)) {
      json(res, 400, { error: "The request body must be a JSON object.", code: "invalid_request" });
      return null;
    }
    return body;
  }

  function profile(res, session, body) {
    const name = String(body.name ?? "").trim();
    // The signup rule (auth-routes.mjs signup branch): 1 to 80 characters.
    if (name.length < 1 || name.length > 80) {
      return json(res, 400, { error: "Use 1 to 80 characters for your name.", code: "name_invalid" });
    }
    store.updateDisplayName(session.user.id, name);
    // The id — never the name, never the address.
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_name_changed", userId: session.user.id }));
    return json(res, 200, { ok: true, displayName: name });
  }

  async function password(res, session, body) {
    const newPassword = String(body.newPassword ?? "");
    const problem = passwordProblem(newPassword);
    if (problem) {
      return json(res, 400, {
        error: problem === "too_long" ? "Use at most 256 characters." : "Use at least 12 characters.",
        code: "password_policy",
      });
    }
    if (!authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(session.user.email)) {
      // Tripped by this route or by login: fixed delay, generic answer, no scrypt.
      await sleep(ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS);
      return json(res, 403, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
    }
    const attempt = store.authenticate(session.user.email, String(body.currentPassword ?? ""));
    if (!attempt.ok) {
      authRoutes.recordPasswordFailure(session.user.email);
      return json(res, 403, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
    }
    // This session stays; every other device is signed out (the sheet's
    // toast says so). resetPassword, by contrast, drops them all.
    store.changePassword(session.user.id, newPassword, { keepSessionRaw: session.raw });
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_password_changed", userId: session.user.id }));
    return json(res, 200, { ok: true });
  }

  const POST_ROUTES = new Map([
    ["/account/profile", profile],
    ["/account/password", password],
  ]);

  async function handle(req, res, pathname) {
    if (pathname !== "/account" && !pathname.startsWith("/account/")) return false;

    // Same rule as /auth/* (auth-routes.mjs, the CSRF check at the top of
    // its handle) for every POST: Origin, else Referer, must name this
    // origin. The read-only GET /account is exempt — a same-origin fetch()
    // carries no Origin, a browser or extension that suppresses referrers
    // sends no Referer either, and a JSON GET behind a SameSite=Lax cookie
    // has nothing a CSRF check would protect.
    const readOnly = req.method === "GET" && pathname === "/account";
    if (!readOnly) {
      const declared = req.headers.origin ?? req.headers.referer;
      let declaredOrigin = null;
      try {
        declaredOrigin = declared ? new URL(declared).origin : null;
      } catch {
        declaredOrigin = null;
      }
      if (declaredOrigin !== expectedOrigin) {
        return json(res, 403, { error: "Cross-origin request rejected.", code: "cross_origin_request" });
      }
    }

    const session = authRoutes.sessionForRequest(req);
    if (!session) {
      return json(res, 401, { error: "Sign in to manage your account.", code: "authentication_required" });
    }

    if (req.method === "GET" && pathname === "/account") {
      return json(res, 200, {
        email: session.user.email,
        // Task 14 pins the workspace identity to the sign-up address and
        // makes these two real; until then they read the one address.
        identityEmail: session.user.email,
        // A bootstrap account has no name until it saves one (the worker
        // greets by the address's local part meanwhile): "" so the sheet's
        // input always has a value.
        displayName: session.user.displayName ?? "",
        pendingEmail: null,
        mailConfigured,
      });
    }

    const route = req.method === "POST" ? POST_ROUTES.get(pathname) : undefined;
    if (!route) return notFound(res);

    const body = await readJsonBody(req, res);
    if (!body) return true;
    if (!opLimiter.allow(`op:${session.user.id}`)) return json(res, 429, RATE_LIMITED);
    return route(res, session, body);
  }

  // The 15-minute sweep that finishes parked deletions. Task 13 gives it its
  // body (one callWorker attempt per parked row, `{ log }` options); until
  // then nothing is parked and serve.mjs's cron sees zeros.
  async function runPendingDeletions() {
    void callWorker;
    return { finished: 0, deferred: 0 };
  }

  return { handle, runPendingDeletions };
}
```

```bash

# --- /account/* (Task 12). The `account` mode, its dispatcher line and its
# header count are Task 13's; until then these run only when called by hand.
login_as() { # login_as <email> <password> -> the itrack_session cookie pair, "" when refused; never echoes the password
  curl -si -X POST "$B/auth/login" -H "origin: $B" \
    --data-urlencode "email=$1" --data-urlencode "password=$2" | tr -d '\r' \
    | awk 'tolower($1)=="set-cookie:" && $2 ~ /^itrack_session=/ { sub(/;.*/, "", $2); print $2 }'
}
ws_as() { curl -s "$B/api/workspace" -H 'accept: application/json' -H "cookie: $1"; }   # ws_as <cookie>
account_get() { # account_get <cookie> -> "<status> <body>"; a same-origin GET carries a Referer, not an Origin
  local status
  status=$(curl -s -o "$TMP/body.json" -w '%{http_code}' "$B/account" \
    -H 'accept: application/json' -H "referer: $B/profile" -H "cookie: $1")
  printf '%s %s' "$status" "$(cat "$TMP/body.json")"
}
post_json() { # post_json <cookie> <path> <json> -> "<status> <body>"
  local cookie="$1" path="$2" data="$3" status
  status=$(curl -s -o "$TMP/body.json" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$B$path" \
    -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "origin: $B" -H "cookie: $cookie" --data "$data")
  printf '%s %s' "$status" "$(cat "$TMP/body.json")"
}
```

### Task 13: Delete account end to end: beginDeletion → internal-secret deleteWorkspace (D1 batch in dependency order + R2 prefix delete) → deleteUser → cleared cookie; in-request retry + cron sweep; R2Bucket.list typed and faked; WORKSPACE_ACTIONS 28; workspace-account-actions test; run-check modes account/throwaway-empty

**Rationale:** spec §8 — "Account deletion and email change (Wave 4) are the first operations that touch both stores; they are implemented as a gateway-orchestrated sequence (auth row → worker action `deleteWorkspace(identity)` → R2 prefix delete) with an idempotent retry" — and §6 Account: "delete account (types email; deletes auth row, D1 rows by identity hash, R2 objects — architecture-M-03)". Today nothing named delete exists on either side: `deploy/railway/auth.mjs` has `createUser`/`createVerifiedUser`/`authenticate`/`createSession`/`sessionUser`/`deleteSession`/`resetPassword`/`cleanup` and no `deleteUser` (`cleanup()` at `:349-357` removes only unverified rows), and `app/api/workspace/route.ts` dispatches 27 actions (`:13597-13698`) none of which touches more than one credential (audit architecture-M-03: "no account deletion, email change or data export for self-serve users"; app-ux-M-02: "account deletion cannot be … requested anywhere in the product"). The identity join is the hash the worker computes at `db/identity.ts:48-55` (`usr_${sha256("license-lantern:" + email)}`), so the purge is keyed by that id and the auth row must outlive the worker call that needs the address. The proof surface is spec §9's three tiers — node:test for gateway and auth (`tests/account-routes.test.mjs`, `tests/auth-store.test.mjs`, `tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs`), the built worker over real node:sqlite (`tests/workspace-account-actions.test.mjs` plus the two-identity probe table of critic-08 in `tests/isolation.test.mjs`), and the Docker run-check on the bootstrap throwaway (`deploy/railway/runcheck.sh account` / `throwaway-empty`, counted in Task 20). Task 16 builds the "Delete this account" sheet on the `POST /account/delete` contract this task fixes.

**Decisions this task fixes (each has a test below):** (1) Transport: `deleteWorkspace` is a public `/api/workspace` action guarded by `x-itrack-internal-secret` — listed in `WORKSPACE_ACTIONS`, probed by the isolation suite (an empty-payload dispatch answers 403 `internal_only`, never 400 `unsupported_action`), reachable in the run-check only through the gateway — not a second `/internal/*` route. (2) Order in the gateway: `store.beginDeletion` FIRST (the user is signed out everywhere and cannot recreate rows), the worker purge SECOND (the identity is read from the parked row before it goes), `store.deleteUser` LAST (a failed purge leaves a parked row for the sweep). (3) Retry: `purgeWorkspaceWithRetry` calls `callWorker` up to three times (delays 0, 250 ms, 1 s through the injectable `sleep`); any status but 200 or a thrown socket error → 503 `delete_deferred` with the cookie cleared and the row parked; the sweep `runPendingDeletions` finishes rows older than 60 s once per cron tick (serve.mjs `fireCron`, every 15 minutes). (4) Envelope unchanged: `{ ok, action, id }` with `id = identity.userId`; the per-table counts are logged as one `workspace_deleted` line, never returned and never with the address. (5) One D1 batch in `IDENTITY_TABLES_DELETE_ORDER`: `renewal_acceptances`, `credential_cycle_links`, `renewal_submissions` (the RESTRICT parents — `db/runtime.ts:378-380` and `:359`), `push_delivery_ledger`, `push_subscriptions`, `reminder_states`, `credentials` (cascades requirements, checkpoints, allocations, matches, checklist tasks), `activity_requirement_matches`, `evidence_files` (no cascade from users or activities, `db/runtime.ts:267-268` — before `activities`), `activities`, `checklist_tasks`, `dental_checkpoint_states` (sweeps, no-ops after the cascade), `xp_events`, `badge_events`, `weekly_quest_claims`, `weekly_progression_periods`, `reminder_preferences`, `profiles`, then `users`. SQLite runs foreign-key actions after the parent row is gone, so the three BEFORE DELETE guards — `dental_checkpoint_states_delete_guard_v1` (`db/runtime.ts:591`), `activity_allocations_delete_guard_v2` (`:837`), `activity_requirement_matches_mutable_delete_guard_v2` (`:907`) — see no parent and do not abort, the reasoning `deleteCredential` documents at `route.ts:7263-7271`; the renewed cycle the test seeds is what exercises them. (6) R2 after D1: the `object_key` rows are collected before the batch, then `deleteEvidencePrefix(bucket, "evidence/<userId>/", keys)` lists the prefix (cursor loop, 1000 per page) ∪ the known keys and deletes in chunks of 1000; a throw → 503 `evidence_delete_retry` (D1 already clean; the retry re-lists). (7) A retry after a full success re-creates `users`/`profiles`/`reminder_preferences` through `ensureUser` (`db/runtime.ts:6031-6061`) and deletes them again — idempotent by construction; the test pins those three counts and zero objects. (8) `requireInternalCaller(request)` compares the header against `env.INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET` with a full-length XOR walk; the dev server (`npm run dev`) sets no secret → 403 always; no e2e calls it. (9) `deleteWorkspace(request, database, bucket, identity, payload)` takes the `Request` — the switch passes it for this case only. (10) `stableUserId` is exported from `db/identity.ts` without touching the salt expression at `:49` (`tests/protected-identifiers.test.mjs:57` pins it); `R2Bucket.list` is typed by hand in `db/cloudflare.d.ts` (no `@cloudflare/workers-types` is installed) and faked identically in the three `FakeEvidenceBucket` copies.

```js
function json(res, status, payload) {
  const body = JSON.stringify(payload);
  res.writeHead(status, {
    "content-type": "application/json; charset=utf-8",
    "cache-control": "no-store",
    "content-length": Buffer.byteLength(body),
  });
  res.end(body);
}

const PASSWORD_INCORRECT = { error: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.", code: "password_incorrect" };
```

```js
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { register } from "node:module";
import { DatabaseSync } from "node:sqlite";
import test from "node:test";

// Real-SQLite harness for the account half of spec §8: the `deleteWorkspace`
// action the gateway calls itself after parking the auth row. Like
// tests/isolation.test.mjs it drives the BUILT worker (dist/server/index.js —
// run `npm run build` first) over node:sqlite with PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON,
// never imports app/** or db/**, and seeds through public routes only (plus
// the one raw push_delivery_ledger row no public route writes). Two owners:
// A is purged, B is the control whose fingerprint must not move; C exercises
// the R2 failure path. The secret lives on the `cloudflare:workers` env the
// loader shim maps to a shared global, exactly where db/index.ts reads it.

const testCloudflareEnv = {};
globalThis.__LICENSE_LANTERN_TEST_ENV__ = testCloudflareEnv;

const cloudflareWorkersMockUrl = `data:text/javascript,${encodeURIComponent(
  "export const env = globalThis.__LICENSE_LANTERN_TEST_ENV__;",
)}`;
const loaderSource = `
  export async function resolve(specifier, context, nextResolve) {
    if (specifier === "cloudflare:workers") {
      return {
        url: ${JSON.stringify(cloudflareWorkersMockUrl)},
        shortCircuit: true,
      };
    }
    return nextResolve(specifier, context);
  }
`;
register(
  `data:text/javascript,${encodeURIComponent(loaderSource)}`,
  import.meta.url,
);

const BASE_URL = "https://itrack.example";
// The demo identity is resolved for a localhost request that carries no
// identity header (db/identity.ts isLocalHostname); nothing else is local.
const DEMO_BASE_URL = "http://localhost";
const INTERNAL_SECRET = "test-secret";
const A = "alpha@example.com";
const B = "bravo@example.com";
const C = "charlie@example.com";

let bootSequence = 0;
async function importWorker() {
  const workerUrl = new URL("../dist/server/index.js", import.meta.url);
  workerUrl.searchParams.set(
    "test",
    `${process.pid}-${Date.now()}-${bootSequence++}`,
  );
  return (await import(workerUrl.href)).default;
}

// SQLiteD1Statement, SQLiteD1Database and FakeEvidenceBucket are copied
// verbatim from tests/workspace-credential-actions.test.mjs (importing a
// *.test.mjs would re-register its tests in this process).
class SQLiteD1Statement {
  constructor(database, sql) {
    this.database = database;
    this.sql = sql;
    this.bindings = [];
  }

  bind(...bindings) {
    this.bindings = bindings;
    return this;
  }

  statement() {
    return this.database.raw.prepare(this.sql);
  }

  async first() {
    return this.statement().get(...this.bindings) ?? null;
  }

  async all() {
    return { results: this.statement().all(...this.bindings) };
  }

  async run() {
    return this.runSync();
  }

  runSync() {
    const result = this.statement().run(...this.bindings);
    return {
      success: true,
      results: [],
      meta: {
        changes: Number(result.changes),
        last_row_id: Number(result.lastInsertRowid),
      },
    };
  }
}

class SQLiteD1Database {
  constructor(DatabaseSync) {
    this.raw = new DatabaseSync(":memory:");
    this.raw.exec("PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON");
  }

  prepare(sql) {
    return new SQLiteD1Statement(this, sql);
  }

  async batch(statements) {
    this.raw.exec("BEGIN IMMEDIATE");
    try {
      const results = statements.map((statement) => statement.runSync());
      this.raw.exec("COMMIT");
      return results;
    } catch (error) {
      this.raw.exec("ROLLBACK");
      throw error;
    }
  }

  close() {
    this.raw.close();
  }
}

class FakeEvidenceBucket {
  constructor() {
    this.puts = [];
    this.gets = [];
    this.deletes = [];
    this.objects = new Map();
  }

  async head(key) {
    return this.objects.get(key) ?? null;
  }

  async get(key) {
    this.gets.push(key);
    return this.objects.get(key) ?? null;
  }

  async put(key, value, options = {}) {
    const buffer =
      value instanceof ArrayBuffer
        ? value
        : ArrayBuffer.isView(value)
          ? value.buffer.slice(
              value.byteOffset,
              value.byteOffset + value.byteLength,
            )
          : await new Response(value).arrayBuffer();
    const stored = {
      key,
      version: "test-version",
      size: buffer.byteLength,
      etag: "test-etag",
      httpEtag: '"test-etag"',
      uploaded: new Date("2026-07-25T12:00:00.000Z"),
      httpMetadata: options.httpMetadata,
      customMetadata: options.customMetadata,
      body: new Blob([buffer]).stream(),
      arrayBuffer: async () => buffer,
    };
    this.puts.push({ key, buffer, options });
    this.objects.set(key, stored);
    return stored;
  }

  async delete(keyOrKeys) {
    const keys = Array.isArray(keyOrKeys) ? keyOrKeys : [keyOrKeys];
    this.deletes.push(...keys);
    keys.forEach((key) => this.objects.delete(key));
  }

  // A real bucket pages; the fake holds everything, so one page, never
  // truncated, and the cursor a caller hands back is accepted and ignored.
  async list({ prefix = "", cursor, limit = 1000 } = {}) {
    void cursor;
    const objects = [...this.objects.values()]
      .filter((object) => object.key.startsWith(prefix))
      .slice(0, limit);
    return { objects, truncated: false, cursor: undefined, delimitedPrefixes: [] };
  }
}

// The R2 failure path (decision 6): one delete throws, the next succeeds.
class FlakyEvidenceBucket extends FakeEvidenceBucket {
  constructor() {
    super();
    this.failNextDelete = false;
  }

  async delete(keyOrKeys) {
    if (this.failNextDelete) {
      this.failNextDelete = false;
      throw new Error("R2 unavailable (simulated)");
    }
    return super.delete(keyOrKeys);
  }
}

const executionContext = {
  waitUntil() {},
  passThroughOnException() {},
};

function identityHeaders(email) {
  return {
    accept: "application/json",
    "content-type": "application/json",
    "oai-authenticated-user-email": email,
  };
}

const PNG_BYTES = new Uint8Array([
  0x89, 0x50, 0x4e, 0x47, 0x0d, 0x0a, 0x1a, 0x0a, ...new Array(64).fill(0),
]);

function base64url(bytes) {
  return Buffer.from(bytes).toString("base64").replace(/\+/g, "-").replace(/\//g, "_").replace(/=+$/, "");
}

async function boot() {
  const db = new SQLiteD1Database(DatabaseSync);
  const bucket = new FlakyEvidenceBucket();
  const worker = await importWorker();

  const fetchAs = (email, path, init = {}) => {
    testCloudflareEnv.DB = db;
    testCloudflareEnv.EVIDENCE = bucket;
    testCloudflareEnv.INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET = INTERNAL_SECRET;
    const headers = {
      accept: "application/json",
      "oai-authenticated-user-email": email,
      ...(init.headers ?? {}),
    };
    return worker.fetch(
      new Request(`${BASE_URL}${path}`, { ...init, headers }),
      {
        ASSETS: {
          fetch: async () => new Response("Not found", { status: 404 }),
        },
        DB: db,
        EVIDENCE: bucket,
      },
      executionContext,
    );
  };

  // The demo user: a localhost URL and no identity header.
  const fetchDemo = (path, init = {}) => {
    testCloudflareEnv.DB = db;
    testCloudflareEnv.EVIDENCE = bucket;
    testCloudflareEnv.INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET = INTERNAL_SECRET;
    return worker.fetch(
      new Request(`${DEMO_BASE_URL}${path}`, {
        ...init,
        headers: { accept: "application/json", ...(init.headers ?? {}) },
      }),
      {
        ASSETS: {
          fetch: async () => new Response("Not found", { status: 404 }),
        },
        DB: db,
        EVIDENCE: bucket,
      },
      executionContext,
    );
  };

  const post = async (email, action, payload, extraHeaders = {}) => {
    const response = await fetchAs(email, "/api/workspace", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { ...identityHeaders(email), ...extraHeaders },
      body: JSON.stringify({ action, payload }),
    });
    return { status: response.status, body: await response.json() };
  };

  const workspace = async (email) => {
    const response = await fetchAs(email, "/api/workspace", {
      headers: identityHeaders(email),
    });
    const text = await response.text();
    assert.equal(response.status, 200, text);
    return JSON.parse(text);
  };

  const upload = async (email, activityId, fileName) => {
    const form = new FormData();
    form.set("activityId", activityId);
    form.set("file", new File([PNG_BYTES], fileName, { type: "image/png" }));
    const response = await fetchAs(email, "/api/evidence", { method: "POST", body: form });
    assert.equal(response.status, 201, await response.clone().text());
    return (await response.json()).evidence;
  };

  const raw = (sql, ...bindings) =>
    db.raw
      .prepare(sql)
      .all(...bindings)
      .map((row) => ({ ...row }));

  return { db, bucket, fetchAs, fetchDemo, post, workspace, upload, raw };
}

// Every table carrying user_id (db/runtime.ts TABLE_STATEMENTS) — the list
// tests/isolation.test.mjs fingerprints — plus the two scoped only through a
// parent, checked for orphans below.
const USER_SCOPED_TABLES = [
  "profiles",
  "weekly_progression_periods",
  "credentials",
  "dental_checkpoint_states",
  "activities",
  "evidence_files",
  "activity_requirement_matches",
  "checklist_tasks",
  "renewal_submissions",
  "credential_cycle_links",
  "renewal_acceptances",
  "reminder_preferences",
  "reminder_states",
  "push_subscriptions",
  "push_delivery_ledger",
  "xp_events",
  "weekly_quest_claims",
  "badge_events",
];

function userIdOf(db, email) {
  return db.raw.prepare("SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?").get(email).id;
}

// The per-table row counts for one identity, keyed like the action's log line.
function countsFor(db, userId) {
  const counts = {};
  for (const table of USER_SCOPED_TABLES) {
    counts[table] = Number(db.raw.prepare(`SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ${table} WHERE user_id = ?`).get(userId).n);
  }
  counts.users = Number(db.raw.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users WHERE id = ?").get(userId).n);
  return counts;
}

function orphanCounts(db) {
  return {
    credential_requirements: Number(
      db.raw.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM credential_requirements WHERE credential_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM credentials)").get().n,
    ),
    activity_allocations: Number(
      db.raw.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM activity_allocations WHERE activity_id NOT IN (SELECT id FROM activities)").get().n,
    ),
  };
}

function ownerFingerprint(db, bucket, userId) {
  const tables = {};
  for (const table of USER_SCOPED_TABLES) {
    tables[table] = db.raw.prepare(`SELECT * FROM ${table} WHERE user_id = ? ORDER BY rowid`).all(userId);
  }
  tables.credential_requirements = db.raw
    .prepare(
      `SELECT credential_requirements.* FROM credential_requirements
       JOIN credentials c ON c.id = credential_requirements.credential_id
       WHERE c.user_id = ? ORDER BY credential_requirements.rowid`,
    )
    .all(userId);
  tables.activity_allocations = db.raw
    .prepare(
      `SELECT activity_allocations.* FROM activity_allocations
       JOIN activities a ON a.id = activity_allocations.activity_id
       WHERE a.user_id = ? ORDER BY activity_allocations.rowid`,
    )
    .all(userId);
  const bucketKeys = [...bucket.objects.keys()].filter((key) => key.startsWith(`evidence/${userId}/`)).sort();
  return JSON.stringify({ tables, bucketKeys });
}

// tests/isolation.test.mjs's seedOwner: credential, activity, personal task,
// one evidence upload, a push subscription, one raw ledger row — and, with
// `renew`, a submitted-then-accepted cycle so the purge meets the RESTRICT
// parents and the closed-cycle delete guards.
async function seedOwner(api, email, { credentialName, activityTitle, taskTitle, device, renew = false }) {
  await api.workspace(email); // the first request runs initializeDatabase + ensureUser
  const userId = userIdOf(api.db, email);

  const created = await api.post(email, "createCredential", {
    credentialName,
    profession: "Social work",
    jurisdiction: "New Jersey",
    issuer: `${credentialName} board`,
    totalRequired: 10,
    unitLabel: "hours",
    cycleStart: "2026-01-01",
    deadline: "2027-12-31",
    categories: [{ name: "General", requiredUnits: 10 }],
  });
  assert.equal(created.status, 200, JSON.stringify(created.body));
  const credentialId = created.body.id;

  const logged = await api.post(email, "addActivity", {
    title: activityTitle,
    provider: `${credentialName} U`,
    completionDate: "2026-06-02",
    totalUnits: 2,
    allocatedUnits: 2,
    credentialId,
  });
  assert.equal(logged.status, 200, JSON.stringify(logged.body));
  const activityId = logged.body.id;

  const task = await api.post(email, "createPersonalTask", { credentialId, title: taskTitle, dueDate: "2026-10-01" });
  assert.equal(task.status, 200, JSON.stringify(task.body));

  const evidence = await api.upload(email, activityId, `${device}.png`);
  const evidenceKey = `evidence/${userId}/${activityId}/${evidence.id}`;
  assert.ok(api.bucket.objects.has(evidenceKey), `${email}: evidence object stored under the owner's key`);

  const key = await crypto.subtle.generateKey({ name: "ECDH", namedCurve: "P-256" }, true, ["deriveBits"]);
  const subscription = {
    endpoint: `https://fcm.googleapis.com/fcm/send/${device}-device`,
    expirationTime: null,
    keys: {
      p256dh: base64url(new Uint8Array(await crypto.subtle.exportKey("raw", key.publicKey))),
      auth: base64url(crypto.getRandomValues(new Uint8Array(16))),
    },
  };
  const pushed = await api.post(email, "savePushSubscription", {
    subscription,
    deviceLabel: `${credentialName} browser`,
    enableAccountPush: false,
  });
  assert.equal(pushed.status, 200, JSON.stringify(pushed.body));
  api.db.raw
    .prepare(
      `INSERT INTO push_delivery_ledger (id, user_id, subscription_id, reminder_key, scheduled_for, status, attempt_count, dispatched_at)
       VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, 'delivered', 1, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)`,
    )
    .run(crypto.randomUUID(), userId, pushed.body.id, `deadline:${credentialId}:2027-12-31`, "2027-10-02");

  if (renew) {
    const submitted = await api.post(email, "markSubmitted", {
      credentialId,
      submissionDate: "2026-09-01",
      confirmationNumber: "CONF-1",
    });
    assert.equal(submitted.status, 200, JSON.stringify(submitted.body));
    const accepted = await api.post(email, "markRenewalAccepted", {
      credentialId,
      acceptedAt: "2026-09-02",
      reference: "ACC-1",
      nextCycleStart: "2028-01-01",
      nextDeadline: "2029-12-31",
    });
    assert.equal(accepted.status, 200, JSON.stringify(accepted.body));
  }

  return { userId, credentialId, activityId, evidenceKey };
}

// Captures the one structured line the action logs; everything else on
// console.log is passed through untouched.
async function captureWorkspaceDeletedLog(run) {
  const original = console.log;
  const lines = [];
  console.log = (...args) => {
    lines.push(args.map(String).join(" "));
    original(...args);
  };
  try {
    return { result: await run(), events: lines.flatMap((line) => {
      try {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(line);
        return parsed?.event === "workspace_deleted" ? [parsed] : [];
      } catch {
        return [];
      }
    }) };
  } finally {
    console.log = original;
  }
}

const SECRET_HEADER = { "x-itrack-internal-secret": INTERNAL_SECRET };

test("deleteWorkspace purges one identity's D1 rows and R2 objects idempotently under the internal secret (spec §8)", async (t) => {
  const api = await boot();
  const seedA = await seedOwner(api, A, {
    credentialName: "Alpha LCSW",
    activityTitle: "Alpha ethics course",
    taskTitle: "Alpha task",
    device: "alpha",
    renew: true,
  });
  const seedB = await seedOwner(api, B, {
    credentialName: "Bravo LMHC",
    activityTitle: "Bravo course",
    taskTitle: "Bravo task",
    device: "bravo",
  });
  const fingerprintB = ownerFingerprint(api.db, api.bucket, seedB.userId);
  const countsABefore = countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId);
  assert.equal(countsABefore.credentials, 2, "A: the renewed cycle and its successor");
  assert.equal(countsABefore.renewal_acceptances, 1);
  assert.equal(countsABefore.renewal_submissions, 1);
  assert.equal(countsABefore.evidence_files, 1);
  assert.equal(countsABefore.push_delivery_ledger, 1);

  await t.test("without the secret header the action is refused 403 internal_only and nothing is deleted", async () => {
    const refused = await api.post(A, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true });
    assert.equal(refused.status, 403, JSON.stringify(refused.body));
    assert.equal(refused.body.code, "internal_only");
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId), countsABefore);
  });

  await t.test("a wrong-length secret is refused the same way", async () => {
    const refused = await api.post(A, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true }, { "x-itrack-internal-secret": "nope" });
    assert.equal(refused.status, 403, JSON.stringify(refused.body));
    assert.equal(refused.body.code, "internal_only");
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId), countsABefore);
  });

  await t.test("an empty payload is refused 400 confirm_required", async () => {
    const refused = await api.post(A, "deleteWorkspace", {}, SECRET_HEADER);
    assert.equal(refused.status, 400, JSON.stringify(refused.body));
    assert.equal(refused.body.code, "confirm_required");
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId), countsABefore);
  });

  await t.test("the demo identity is refused 409 demo_workspace", async () => {
    const response = await api.fetchDemo("/api/workspace", {
      method: "POST",
      headers: { "content-type": "application/json", ...SECRET_HEADER },
      body: JSON.stringify({ action: "deleteWorkspace", payload: { confirm: true } }),
    });
    assert.equal(response.status, 409);
    const body = await response.json();
    assert.equal(body.code, "demo_workspace");
    assert.ok(
      api.db.raw.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM credentials WHERE user_id = (SELECT id FROM users WHERE is_demo = 1)").get().n > 0,
      "the demo workspace is still seeded",
    );
  });

  await t.test("as A with the secret: every user-scoped row and object of A is gone, B is byte-for-byte unchanged, the log line carries the counts", async () => {
    const { result, events } = await captureWorkspaceDeletedLog(() =>
      api.post(A, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true }, SECRET_HEADER),
    );
    assert.equal(result.status, 200, JSON.stringify(result.body));
    assert.deepEqual(result.body, { ok: true, action: "deleteWorkspace", id: seedA.userId });
    const zero = Object.fromEntries([...USER_SCOPED_TABLES, "users"].map((table) => [table, 0]));
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId), zero);
    assert.deepEqual(orphanCounts(api.db), { credential_requirements: 0, activity_allocations: 0 });
    assert.ok(![...api.bucket.objects.keys()].some((key) => key.startsWith(`evidence/${seedA.userId}/`)), "no object under A's prefix");
    assert.ok(api.bucket.deletes.includes(seedA.evidenceKey), "A's object was deleted, not merely forgotten");
    assert.equal(ownerFingerprint(api.db, api.bucket, seedB.userId), fingerprintB, "B is untouched");
    assert.equal(events.length, 1, "exactly one workspace_deleted line");
    assert.equal(events[0].userId, seedA.userId);
    assert.deepEqual(events[0].counts, { ...countsABefore, r2Objects: 1 });
    assert.ok(!JSON.stringify(events[0]).includes(A), "the log line never carries the address");
  });

  await t.test("a second call is a no-op that succeeds: ensureUser's three rows are re-created and deleted again", async () => {
    const { result, events } = await captureWorkspaceDeletedLog(() =>
      api.post(A, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true }, SECRET_HEADER),
    );
    assert.equal(result.status, 200, JSON.stringify(result.body));
    assert.deepEqual(result.body, { ok: true, action: "deleteWorkspace", id: seedA.userId });
    const expected = Object.fromEntries([...USER_SCOPED_TABLES, "users"].map((table) => [table, 0]));
    expected.users = 1;
    expected.profiles = 1;
    expected.reminder_preferences = 1;
    expected.r2Objects = 0;
    assert.deepEqual(events[0].counts, expected, "only the rows ensureUser re-created were there to delete");
    const zero = Object.fromEntries([...USER_SCOPED_TABLES, "users"].map((table) => [table, 0]));
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedA.userId), zero);
    assert.equal(ownerFingerprint(api.db, api.bucket, seedB.userId), fingerprintB, "B is still untouched");
  });

  await t.test("an R2 failure after the D1 batch answers 503 evidence_delete_retry; the retry re-lists the prefix and finishes", async () => {
    const seedC = await seedOwner(api, C, {
      credentialName: "Charlie LPC",
      activityTitle: "Charlie course",
      taskTitle: "Charlie task",
      device: "charlie",
    });
    api.bucket.failNextDelete = true;
    const deferred = await api.post(C, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true }, SECRET_HEADER);
    assert.equal(deferred.status, 503, JSON.stringify(deferred.body));
    assert.equal(deferred.body.code, "evidence_delete_retry");
    const zero = Object.fromEntries([...USER_SCOPED_TABLES, "users"].map((table) => [table, 0]));
    assert.deepEqual(countsFor(api.db, seedC.userId), zero, "D1 was already clean when R2 failed");
    assert.ok(api.bucket.objects.has(seedC.evidenceKey), "the object survived the failed delete");
    const { result, events } = await captureWorkspaceDeletedLog(() =>
      api.post(C, "deleteWorkspace", { confirm: true }, SECRET_HEADER),
    );
    assert.equal(result.status, 200, JSON.stringify(result.body));
    assert.ok(!api.bucket.objects.has(seedC.evidenceKey), "the retry found the object by listing the prefix");
    assert.equal(events[0].counts.r2Objects, 1, "…and counted it");
    assert.equal(events[0].counts.evidence_files, 0, "with no evidence_files row left to name it");
    assert.equal(ownerFingerprint(api.db, api.bucket, seedB.userId), fingerprintB, "B is untouched by C's purge too");
  });
});
```
