- [ ] **Step 5: The worker action — `requireInternalCaller`, the delete order, the prefix delete, `deleteWorkspace`, the dispatch case**

`app/api/workspace/route.ts` — immediately after the closing brace of `deleteCredential` (`  return credentialId;` / `}` at `:7437-7438`) insert:

```ts
// Spec §8 account deletion, worker half. The gateway (deploy/railway/
// account-routes.mjs) calls this action itself, after parking the auth row
// and dropping every session, with the identity headers of the parked row
// plus the process-local secret below. Nothing a browser sends reaches it:
// the gateway strips inbound `x-itrack-internal*` headers before proxying,
// and the dev server sets no secret at all. The compare walks the whole
// secret so a mismatch costs the same time as a match.
function timingSafeEqualText(left: string, right: string) {
  if (left.length !== right.length) return false;
  let difference = 0;
  for (let index = 0; index < left.length; index += 1) {
    difference |= left.charCodeAt(index) ^ right.charCodeAt(index);
  }
  return difference === 0;
}

function requireInternalCaller(request: Request) {
  const secret = env.INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET;
  const supplied = request.headers.get("x-itrack-internal-secret");
  if (
    !secret ||
    !supplied ||
    supplied.length !== secret.length ||
    !timingSafeEqualText(supplied, secret)
  ) {
    throw new RequestError(
      "This action is only available to the account service.",
      403,
      "internal_only",
    );
  }
}

// Every user-scoped table (db/runtime.ts TABLE_STATEMENTS) in an order one
// batch can delete under PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON: the RESTRICT parents
// first (renewal_acceptances → credentials/renewal_submissions,
// credential_cycle_links.previous_credential_id), the push ledger before its
// subscriptions, then credentials — whose cascade removes requirements,
// checkpoints, allocations, matches and checklist tasks and passes the
// BEFORE DELETE guard triggers because SQLite runs foreign-key actions after
// the parent row is gone (the reasoning deleteCredential documents above) —
// then evidence_files, which cascade from neither users nor activities,
// before activities. The sweeps after them are no-ops once the cascades
// ran; profiles and reminder_preferences last, and the users row itself
// outside this list.
const IDENTITY_TABLES_DELETE_ORDER = [
  "renewal_acceptances",
  "credential_cycle_links",
  "renewal_submissions",
  "push_delivery_ledger",
  "push_subscriptions",
  "reminder_states",
  "credentials",
  "activity_requirement_matches",
  "evidence_files",
  "activities",
  "checklist_tasks",
  "dental_checkpoint_states",
  "xp_events",
  "badge_events",
  "weekly_quest_claims",
  "weekly_progression_periods",
  "reminder_preferences",
  "profiles",
] as const;

// R2 lists and deletes at most 1000 keys per call.
const R2_DELETE_BATCH = 1000;

// Unions the keys the rows named with whatever the bucket still lists under
// the owner's prefix — an upload whose INSERT failed, or a retry after the
// rows are already gone — then deletes in R2-sized chunks. A throw is the
// caller's to report: D1 is already clean by then and a retry re-lists.
async function deleteEvidencePrefix(
  bucket: R2Bucket,
  prefix: string,
  known: readonly string[],
) {
  const keys = new Set(known);
  let cursor: string | undefined;
  do {
    const page = await bucket.list({ prefix, cursor, limit: R2_DELETE_BATCH });
    for (const object of page.objects) keys.add(object.key);
    cursor = page.truncated ? page.cursor : undefined;
  } while (cursor);
  const all = [...keys];
  for (let start = 0; start < all.length; start += R2_DELETE_BATCH) {
    await bucket.delete(all.slice(start, start + R2_DELETE_BATCH));
  }
  return all.length;
}

async function deleteWorkspace(
  request: Request,
  database: D1Database,
  bucket: R2Bucket,
  identity: RequestIdentity,
  payload: JsonRecord,
) {
  requireInternalCaller(request);
  if (identity.isDemo) {
    throw new RequestError(
      "The local preview workspace cannot be deleted.",
      409,
      "demo_workspace",
    );
  }
  if (payload.confirm !== true) {
    throw new RequestError("confirm must be true", 400, "confirm_required");
  }
  // Counts come from SELECT COUNT(*) before the batch: D1 reports a DELETE's
  // meta.changes as a total_changes() delta that includes cascaded rows, so
  // the batch's own numbers would not say what was there.
  const counts: Record<string, number> = {};
  for (const table of [...IDENTITY_TABLES_DELETE_ORDER, "users"]) {
    const column = table === "users" ? "id" : "user_id";
    const row = await query(
      database,
      `SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM ${table} WHERE ${column} = ?`,
      [identity.userId],
    ).first<{ n: number }>();
    counts[table] = Number(row?.n ?? 0);
  }
  const knownKeys = (
    await query(
      database,
      `SELECT object_key AS objectKey FROM evidence_files WHERE user_id = ?`,
      [identity.userId],
    ).all<{ objectKey: string }>()
  ).results.map((row) => row.objectKey);
  await database.batch([
    ...IDENTITY_TABLES_DELETE_ORDER.map((table) =>
      query(database, `DELETE FROM ${table} WHERE user_id = ?`, [
        identity.userId,
      ]),
    ),
    query(database, `DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?`, [identity.userId]),
  ]);
  // R2 after D1. The rows are gone either way; a retry lists the prefix
  // again and finishes what a throw here left behind.
  const objects = await deleteEvidencePrefix(
    bucket,
    `evidence/${identity.userId}/`,
    knownKeys,
  ).catch((error: unknown) => {
    console.error("deleteWorkspace: evidence removal deferred", error);
    throw new RequestError(
      "Evidence files are queued for removal. Retry when storage is available.",
      503,
      "evidence_delete_retry",
    );
  });
  // The one record of what went: the hash, never the address.
  console.log(
    JSON.stringify({
      event: "workspace_deleted",
      userId: identity.userId,
      counts: { ...counts, r2Objects: objects },
    }),
  );
  return identity.userId;
}
```

```js
// deleteWorkspace names no id at all and, without INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET on
```

```js
  // Spec §8 account deletion, auth half. Parks the row (idempotent: the
  // first timestamp is kept) and drops every session at once, so the account
  // can neither act nor sign in again while the gateway purges the workspace
  // under the identity this returns; deleteUser finishes it once the worker
  // has answered. `SELECT *` so `identity_email`, the column Task 14 adds,
  // is read here the day it exists without an edit: until then the identity
  // the worker hashes IS the address.
  beginDeletion(userId) {
    this.db
      .prepare("UPDATE users SET deleting_at = COALESCE(deleting_at, ?) WHERE id = ?")
      .run(this.now(), userId);
    this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?").run(userId);
    const row = this.db
      .prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE id = ? AND deleting_at IS NOT NULL")
      .get(userId);
    return row
      ? { userId: row.id, email: row.email, identityEmail: row.identity_email ?? row.email }
      : null;
  }

  // Parked rows the sweep (account-routes.mjs runPendingDeletions) still has
  // to finish, oldest first.
  pendingDeletions() {
    return this.db
      .prepare("SELECT * FROM users WHERE deleting_at IS NOT NULL ORDER BY deleting_at, id")
      .all()
      .map((row) => ({
        userId: row.id,
        email: row.email,
        identityEmail: row.identity_email ?? row.email,
        deletingAt: Number(row.deleting_at),
      }));
  }

  // The last step: tokens and sessions cascade (PRAGMA foreign_keys = ON).
  deleteUser(userId) {
    const removed = this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM users WHERE id = ?").run(userId);
    return Number(removed.changes ?? 0) === 1;
  }
```

- [ ] **Step 10: Write the failing route tests — `tests/account-routes.test.mjs`**

Append at the end of Task 12's file. Every binding is aliased so the block cannot collide with whatever names the tests above it use; ESM hoists the imports wherever they sit. The tripped-bucket case fills the shared account bucket through `/auth/login` failures (varying `x-forwarded-for`, exactly as `tests/auth-routes.test.mjs:586-603` does) and spends at most two `/account/delete` posts, so Task 12's per-user route limiter never enters the picture.

```js
// ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
// Task 13: POST /account/delete — spec §8's gateway sequence (auth row parked
// → the gateway's own deleteWorkspace call → auth row deleted → cleared
// cookie), the three in-request retries and the cron sweep. Self-contained:
// aliased imports and its own request/response fakes, and the worker call is
// a recording stub — the real transport is proven in tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs.
import { test as deletionTest } from "node:test";
import { strict as deletionAssert } from "node:assert";
import { EventEmitter as DeletionEmitter } from "node:events";
import { AuthStore as DeletionAuthStore } from "../deploy/railway/auth.mjs";
import {
  createAuthRoutes as createDeletionAuthRoutes,
  signValue as signDeletionCookie,
  SESSION_COOKIE as DELETION_SESSION_COOKIE,
} from "../deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs";
import { createAccountRoutes as createDeletionAccountRoutes } from "../deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs";

const DELETION_SECRET = "delete-test-secret";
const DELETION_ORIGIN = "https://itrack.test";

// `workerStatuses` is consumed left to right and its last entry repeats;
// "unreachable" makes the stub throw like a refused socket. Every call also
// records the users row as it stood during the call — the ordering proof.
function makeDeleteHarness({ workerStatuses = [200] } = {}) {
  let clock = 1_700_000_000_000;
  const now = () => clock;
  const store = new DeletionAuthStore(":memory:", { now });
  const sleeps = [];
  const sleep = async (ms) => { sleeps.push(ms); };
  const sendEmail = async () => ({ ok: true });
  sendEmail.mailConfigured = true;
  const workerCalls = [];
  const statuses = [...workerStatuses];
  const authRoutes = createDeletionAuthRoutes({ store, secret: DELETION_SECRET, baseUrl: DELETION_ORIGIN, now, sleep, sendEmail });
  const accountRoutes = createDeletionAccountRoutes({
    store, authRoutes, baseUrl: DELETION_ORIGIN, sendEmail, now, sleep,
    callWorker: async (call) => {
      workerCalls.push({ ...call, rowDuringCall: usersRow(store, "gone@e.co") });
      const status = statuses.length > 1 ? statuses.shift() : statuses[0];
      if (status === "unreachable") throw new Error("connect ECONNREFUSED 127.0.0.1:8787");
      return {
        status,
        body: status === 200
          ? { ok: true, action: "deleteWorkspace", id: "usr_test" }
          : { error: "The CEU workspace could not be loaded. Please try again.", code: "internal_error" },
      };
    },
  });
  const { userId } = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "gone@e.co", displayName: "Gone", password: "correct-pass-11" });
  const cookie = `${DELETION_SESSION_COOKIE}=${signDeletionCookie(store.createSession(userId), DELETION_SECRET)}`;
  return { store, authRoutes, accountRoutes, sleeps, workerCalls, statuses, userId, cookie, tick: (ms) => (clock += ms) };
}

function usersRow(store, email) {
  return store.db.prepare("SELECT id, deleting_at AS deletingAt FROM users WHERE email = ?").get(email) ?? null;
}

function deletionRequest({ method = "POST", url, body = "", headers = {} }) {
  const req = new DeletionEmitter();
  req.method = method;
  req.url = url;
  req.headers = {
    host: "itrack.test",
    origin: DELETION_ORIGIN,
    "content-length": String(Buffer.byteLength(body)),
    ...headers,
  };
  req.socket = { remoteAddress: "203.0.113.9" };
  process.nextTick(() => {
    if (body) req.emit("data", Buffer.from(body));
    req.emit("end");
  });
  return req;
}

function deletionResponse() {
  return {
    statusCode: null, headers: {}, body: "",
    writeHead(status, headers) {
      this.statusCode = status;
      for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(headers ?? {})) this.headers[name.toLowerCase()] = value;
    },
    setHeader(name, value) { this.headers[name.toLowerCase()] = value; },
    end(chunk) { this.body += chunk ?? ""; this.ended = true; },
  };
}

async function postDeletion(harness, payload) {
  const body = JSON.stringify(payload);
  const req = deletionRequest({ url: "/account/delete", body, headers: { "content-type": "application/json", cookie: harness.cookie } });
  const res = deletionResponse();
  const handled = await harness.accountRoutes.handle(req, res, "/account/delete");
  return { handled, res, json: res.body ? JSON.parse(res.body) : null };
}

async function loginDeletion(harness, password, ip) {
  const body = new URLSearchParams({ email: "gone@e.co", password }).toString();
  const req = deletionRequest({
    url: "/auth/login", body,
    headers: { "content-type": "application/x-www-form-urlencoded", "x-forwarded-for": ip },
  });
  const res = deletionResponse();
  await harness.authRoutes.handle(req, res, "/auth/login");
  return res;
}

deletionTest("delete: a typed email that is not the account's answers 400 email_mismatch and touches nothing", async () => {
  const h = makeDeleteHarness();
  const { handled, res, json } = await postDeletion(h, { email: "someone-else@e.co", password: "correct-pass-11" });
  deletionAssert.equal(handled, true);
  deletionAssert.equal(res.statusCode, 400);
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(json, { error: "That isn’t the email on this account.", code: "email_mismatch" });
  deletionAssert.equal(res.headers["set-cookie"], undefined, "the session is kept");
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(h.workerCalls, []);
  deletionAssert.equal(usersRow(h.store, "gone@e.co").deletingAt, null, "the row is not parked");
  deletionAssert.ok(h.authRoutes.sessionForRequest({ headers: { cookie: h.cookie } }), "the cookie still resolves");
});

deletionTest("delete: a wrong password answers 403 password_incorrect and counts in the account bucket login shares", async () => {
  const h = makeDeleteHarness();
  // Nine login failures from nine addresses fill the account bucket to one
  // short of its limit; the delete failure below is the tenth.
  for (let attempt = 0; attempt < 9; attempt += 1) {
    const res = await loginDeletion(h, "wrong-pass-11", `10.0.${attempt}.1`);
    deletionAssert.equal(res.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials");
  }
  const tenth = await postDeletion(h, { email: "gone@e.co", password: "wrong-pass-11" });
  deletionAssert.equal(tenth.res.statusCode, 403);
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(tenth.json, { error: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.", code: "password_incorrect" });
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(h.sleeps, [], "no delay while under the limit");
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(h.workerCalls, []);
  deletionAssert.equal(usersRow(h.store, "gone@e.co").deletingAt, null, "the row is not parked");
  let authenticateCalls = 0;
  const original = h.store.authenticate.bind(h.store);
  h.store.authenticate = (...args) => { authenticateCalls += 1; return original(...args); };
  const tripped = await postDeletion(h, { email: "gone@e.co", password: "correct-pass-11" });
  deletionAssert.equal(tripped.res.statusCode, 403, "even the right password is refused while the account is tripped");
  deletionAssert.equal(tripped.json.code, "password_incorrect");
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(h.sleeps, [2000], "the fixed lock delay");
  deletionAssert.equal(authenticateCalls, 0, "no scrypt for a tripped account");
  const login = await loginDeletion(h, "correct-pass-11", "10.9.9.9");
  deletionAssert.equal(login.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials", "login is tripped by the same bucket");
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(h.sleeps, [2000, 2000]);
  deletionAssert.ok(h.authRoutes.sessionForRequest({ headers: { cookie: h.cookie } }), "still signed in: nothing was deleted");
});

deletionTest("delete happy path: the row is parked, the worker is called once with the parked address and no Origin, the row goes last, the cookie is cleared", async () => {
  const h = makeDeleteHarness();
  const { res, json } = await postDeletion(h, { email: "  GONE@E.CO ", password: "correct-pass-11" });
  deletionAssert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  deletionAssert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true });
```

(a) `deploy/railway/gateway.mjs` — after `applySecurityHeaders` (`:71-73`, ending `  for (const [name, value] of Object.entries(SECURITY_HEADERS)) res.setHeader(name, value);\n}`) and before `export function createGateway(` (`:75`) insert:

```js
// The gateway's own call into the worker for the account operations spec §8
// orchestrates (delete account today). It carries the identity headers
// proxy() sets — the parked auth row's address, read before the row goes —
// plus the process-local secret that authorises `deleteWorkspace`, and no
// Origin or sec-fetch-site: the worker's same-origin check on saves rejects
// only a mismatching value. Nothing a browser sends reaches this path — the
// inbound `x-itrack-internal*` headers are stripped in proxy() — and the
// answer is read as JSON once, capped, so a runaway body cannot pin memory.
const WORKER_CALL_MAX_BYTES = 64 * 1024;

export function createWorkerCaller({ upstreamPort, publicHost, internalSecret }) {
  return ({ identityEmail, contactEmail, displayName, action, payload }) =>
    new Promise((resolve, reject) => {
      const body = JSON.stringify({ action, payload });
      const headers = {
        host: publicHost,
        accept: "application/json",
        "content-type": "application/json",
        "content-length": Buffer.byteLength(body),
        "oai-authenticated-user-email": identityEmail,
        "x-itrack-internal-secret": internalSecret,
      };
      if (contactEmail) headers["oai-authenticated-user-contact-email"] = contactEmail;
      if (displayName) {
        headers["oai-authenticated-user-full-name"] = encodeURIComponent(displayName);
        headers["oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding"] = "percent-encoded-utf-8";
      }
      const request = http.request(
        { host: "127.0.0.1", port: upstreamPort, method: "POST", path: "/api/workspace", headers },
        (response) => {
          const chunks = [];
          let size = 0;
          response.on("data", (chunk) => {
            if (size >= WORKER_CALL_MAX_BYTES) return;
            size += chunk.length;
            chunks.push(chunk);
          });
          response.on("end", () => {
            let parsed = null;
            try {
              parsed = JSON.parse(Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8").slice(0, WORKER_CALL_MAX_BYTES));
            } catch {
              parsed = null;
            }
            resolve({ status: response.statusCode ?? 502, body: parsed });
          });
          response.on("error", reject);
        },
      );
      request.on("error", reject);
      request.end(body);
    });
}
```

(`http` is already imported at `gateway.mjs:8`.)

Inside `createAccountRoutes`, before `async function handle(`, add the retry and replace Task 12's stub `runPendingDeletions` (the function returning `{ finished: 0, deferred: 0 }`) with the real one:

```js
  // Spec §8: the workspace purge, retried in-request. Any answer but 200 —
  // a 5xx, a 403 from a secret mismatch, an unreachable worker — defers the
  // finish to the sweep; the row stays parked either way.
  async function purgeWorkspaceWithRetry(marked) {
    const delays = [0, 250, 1000];
    let error = "unknown";
    for (const delay of delays) {
      if (delay) await sleep(delay);
      try {
        const result = await callWorker({
          identityEmail: marked.identityEmail,
          contactEmail: marked.email,
          action: "deleteWorkspace",
          payload: { confirm: true },
        });
        if (result.status === 200) return { ok: true };
        error = `status_${result.status}`;
      } catch {
        error = "unreachable";
      }
    }
    return { ok: false, error };
  }

  const SWEEP_MIN_AGE_MS = 60 * 1000;

  // The cron half of spec §8's idempotent retry (serve.mjs fireCron, every
  // 15 minutes): one attempt per parked row older than a minute — a younger
  // row may still be inside its own request's retries. The worker's purge is
  // idempotent, so a row whose purge succeeded but whose deleteUser never
  // ran is simply purged again (three ensureUser rows) and finished.
  async function runPendingDeletions({ log = console.log } = {}) {
    let finished = 0;
    let deferred = 0;
    for (const row of store.pendingDeletions()) {
      if (now() - row.deletingAt < SWEEP_MIN_AGE_MS) continue;
      let status = null;
      try {
        ({ status } = await callWorker({
          identityEmail: row.identityEmail,
          contactEmail: row.email,
          action: "deleteWorkspace",
          payload: { confirm: true },
        }));
      } catch {
        status = null;
      }
      if (status === 200) {
        store.deleteUser(row.userId);
        finished += 1;
        log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_delete_finished", userId: row.userId }));
      } else {
        deferred += 1;
        log(JSON.stringify({
          event: "account_delete_deferred",
          userId: row.userId,
          error: status === null ? "unreachable" : `status_${status}`,
        }));
      }
    }
    return { finished, deferred };
  }
```

Replace the whole of `startStack` — from `export async function startStack({ upstreamHandler } = {}) {` (`:15`) to the closing `}` before `export const get =` (`:51`), including whatever Task 12 added inside it — with:

```js
export const INTERNAL_SECRET = "gw-internal-secret";

export async function startStack({ upstreamHandler } = {}) {
  let lastUpstream = null;
  // Every request the stub upstream ever saw, in order — a gateway-originated
  // call and a proxied browser request look the same here.
  const upstreamRequests = [];
  const upstream = http.createServer((req, res) => {
    lastUpstream = { url: req.url, method: req.method, headers: { ...req.headers } };
    upstreamRequests.push(lastUpstream);
    if (upstreamHandler) return upstreamHandler(req, res);
    res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "text/plain" });
    res.end("app-response");
  });
  await new Promise((resolve) => upstream.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const upstreamPort = upstream.address().port;

  const clock = { now: 1_800_000_000_000 };
  const now = () => clock.now;
  const store = new AuthStore(":memory:", { now });
  const sent = [];
  const sendEmail = async (message) => { sent.push(message); return { ok: true }; };
  const sleep = async () => {};
  const authRoutes = createAuthRoutes({ store, secret: "gw-secret", baseUrl: BASE_URL, now, sleep, sendEmail });
  const accountRoutes = createAccountRoutes({
    store, authRoutes, baseUrl: BASE_URL, sendEmail, now, sleep,
    callWorker: createWorkerCaller({ upstreamPort, publicHost: "gw.test", internalSecret: INTERNAL_SECRET }),
  });
  const gateway = http.createServer(
    createGateway({ authRoutes, accountRoutes, baseUrl: BASE_URL, pagesDir, upstreamPort, now }),
  );
  await new Promise((resolve) => gateway.listen(0, "127.0.0.1", resolve));
  const base = `http://127.0.0.1:${gateway.address().port}`;

  return {
    base, store, sent, clock, accountRoutes, upstreamRequests,
    upstreamSeen: () => lastUpstream,
    close: async () => {
      await new Promise((resolve) => gateway.close(resolve));
      await new Promise((resolve) => upstream.close(resolve));
    },
  };
}
```

```js
// Spec §8 end to end over the real gateway and the real caller: the stub
// upstream plays the worker, answering deleteWorkspace only when the secret
// is present, and reads the auth row while it is being "called".
test("delete-account: the gateway calls the worker itself with the secret and the identity, then answers 200 with a cleared cookie", async (t) => {
  const seen = [];
  let rowDuringPurge = null;
  // The handler needs the stack's store, which exists only once startStack
  // has resolved; a ref keeps the closure ahead of the assignment.
  const stackRef = { current: null };
  const stack = await startStack({
    upstreamHandler(req, res) {
      const chunks = [];
      req.on("data", (chunk) => chunks.push(chunk));
      req.on("end", () => {
        seen.push({ url: req.url, method: req.method, headers: { ...req.headers }, body: Buffer.concat(chunks).toString("utf8") });
        rowDuringPurge = stackRef.current.store.db.prepare("SELECT deleting_at AS deletingAt FROM users WHERE email = ?").get("gone@e.co") ?? null;
        if (req.url !== "/api/workspace" || req.headers["x-itrack-internal-secret"] !== INTERNAL_SECRET) {
          res.writeHead(403, { "content-type": "application/json" });
          res.end(JSON.stringify({ error: "This action is only available to the account service.", code: "internal_only" }));
          return;
        }
        res.writeHead(200, { "content-type": "application/json" });
        res.end(JSON.stringify({ ok: true, action: "deleteWorkspace", id: "usr_stub" }));
      });
    },
  });
  stackRef.current = stack;
  t.after(() => stack.close());
  const { base } = stack;
  const cookie = await signedInCookie(stack, "gone@e.co", "correct-pass-11");

  const response = await fetch(`${base}/account/delete`, {
    method: "POST",
    redirect: "manual",
    headers: { "content-type": "application/json", origin: BASE_URL, cookie },
    body: JSON.stringify({ email: "gone@e.co", password: "correct-pass-11" }),
  });
  assert.equal(response.status, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(await response.json(), { ok: true });
  assert.match(response.headers.get("set-cookie") ?? "", /^itrack_session=; Path=\/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=0$/);

  assert.equal(seen.length, 1, "exactly one worker call");
  assert.equal(stack.upstreamRequests.length, 1, "…and nothing was proxied for the browser");
  const [call] = seen;
  assert.equal(call.method, "POST");
  assert.equal(call.url, "/api/workspace");
  assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(call.body), { action: "deleteWorkspace", payload: { confirm: true } });
  assert.equal(call.headers["oai-authenticated-user-email"], "gone@e.co", "the parked row's address is the identity");
  assert.equal(call.headers["oai-authenticated-user-contact-email"], "gone@e.co");
  assert.equal(call.headers["x-itrack-internal-secret"], INTERNAL_SECRET);
  assert.equal(call.headers.host, "gw.test", "the canonical host, as proxy() sends it");
  assert.equal(call.headers["content-type"], "application/json");
  assert.equal(call.headers.origin, undefined, "no Origin: the worker's same-origin check passes by absence");
  assert.equal(call.headers["sec-fetch-site"], undefined);
  assert.equal(call.headers.cookie, undefined, "the gateway's own call carries no browser cookie");
  assert.equal(typeof rowDuringPurge?.deletingAt, "number", "the auth row was parked, not gone, while the worker ran");
  assert.equal(stack.store.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users WHERE email = ?").get("gone@e.co").n, 0, "the auth row went last");
  assert.deepEqual(stack.store.authenticate("gone@e.co", "correct-pass-11"), { ok: false, reason: "bad-credentials" });

  const dead = await get(base, "/api/workspace", { accept: "application/json", cookie });
  assert.equal(dead.status, 401, "the old session no longer resolves");
  assert.equal(stack.upstreamRequests.length, 1, "…and reached no worker");

  // A browser cannot buy the purge with the header: proxy() strips it, and
  // the stub answers 403 to what arrives without it.
  const forged = await fetch(`${base}/api/workspace`, {
    method: "POST",
    headers: {
      "content-type": "application/json", origin: BASE_URL,
      cookie: await signedInCookie(stack, "other@e.co"),
      "x-itrack-internal-secret": INTERNAL_SECRET,
    },
    body: JSON.stringify({ action: "deleteWorkspace", payload: { confirm: true } }),
  });
  assert.equal(forged.status, 403);
  assert.equal(seen[seen.length - 1].headers["x-itrack-internal-secret"], undefined, "stripped before the worker saw it");
  assert.equal(stack.store.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users WHERE email = ?").get("other@e.co").n, 1);
});
```

```bash
    -H "origin: $B" -H "cookie: $1" --data "{\"action\":\"$2\",\"payload\":$3}")
  printf '%s %s' "$status" "$(cat "$TMP/body.json")"
}
ws_as()     { curl -s "$B/api/workspace" -H 'accept: application/json' -H "cookie: $1"; }
post_json() { # post_json <cookie> <path> <json> -> "<status> <body>"; the response headers land in $TMP/headers.txt
  local status
  status=$(curl -s -o "$TMP/body.json" -D "$TMP/headers.txt" -w '%{http_code}' -X POST "$B$2" \
    -H 'accept: application/json' -H 'content-type: application/json' \
    -H "origin: $B" -H "cookie: $1" --data "$3")
  printf '%s %s' "$status" "$(cat "$TMP/body.json")"
}

run_login_as_throwaway() {   # the second bootstrap account; Docker only — `account` deletes it for real

    --data-urlencode 'email=wave4-throwaway@example.test' --data-urlencode "password=$THROWAWAY_PASSWORD" \
    | tr -d '\r' > "$TMP/login-throwaway.txt"
  check 'throwaway login 303'                 '^HTTP/[0-9.]+ 303'            "$(cat "$TMP/login-throwaway.txt")"
  check 'throwaway login sets itrack_session' '^set-cookie: itrack_session=' "$(cat "$TMP/login-throwaway.txt")"
  T=$(awk 'tolower($1)=="set-cookie:" && $2 ~ /^itrack_session=/ { sub(/;.*/, "", $2); print $2 }' "$TMP/login-throwaway.txt")
}
```

### Task 14: Email change with re-verification, identity pinned to the sign-up address: users.identity_email, email_changes table, POST /account/email + cancel, /auth/verify email-change branch, oai-authenticated-user-contact-email forwarded, RequestIdentity.identityEmail, ensureUser binds it

**Rationale:** spec §6 lists "email change (re-verify)" among what Account must offer, and §8 makes it, with deletion, one of "the first operations that touch both stores" — the auth store `/data/auth.db` and D1 — "implemented as a gateway-orchestrated sequence … with an idempotent retry". Audit app-ux-M-02 ("No account self-service: display name, email, password and account deletion cannot be changed or requested anywhere in the product") is the finding this task closes for the email. The obstacle is §8's own sentence: "workspace identity remains `sha256(email)` with the `license-lantern:` salt". Read literally, changing the address means re-keying the workspace: `db/identity.ts:48-55` hashes the forwarded address into `users.id` (`usr_<sha256>`), every user-scoped D1 row carries that id (18 `user_id` columns plus `users` itself), every R2 object is stored under `evidence/${identity.userId}/…` (`app/api/evidence/route.ts:213`), three integrity triggers forbid an `UPDATE … SET user_id` outright — `dental_checkpoint_states_identity_guard_v1` (`db/runtime.ts:562`), `dental_checkpoint_credentials_scope_guard_v1` (`:569`), `activity_allocations_identity_guard_v2` (`:831`), `activity_requirement_matches_identity_guard_v2` (`:900`) — `users.id` has foreign-key children with no `ON UPDATE CASCADE`, R2 has no rename, and `ensureUser` (`db/runtime.ts:6027-6061`) runs before every action, so the first request that carried a new address would mint an empty workspace under the new hash before any move finished. This task keeps §8's join ("a `users` row and an auth row are joined by that hash") and reads its sentence as *the address the account signed up with*: the auth store pins it as `users.identity_email` (backfilled from `email` for every existing row — Chris's production row backfills to `christophertskerritt@gmail.com`, the identical hash, nothing migrates), the gateway forwards it as `oai-authenticated-user-email` (the name the worker already hashes) and the contact address beside it as a sibling header `oai-authenticated-user-contact-email`, the worker keeps `userId = stableUserId(identityEmail)` and reports the contact address as `identity.email` (so `getWorkspace().user.email` at `route.ts:5234` and the packet owner block at `packet/route.ts:181` show the address the person uses without either line changing), and `ensureUser` writes the identity address into D1's unique `users.email` so that column never moves either. An email change therefore touches the auth store alone: a mailed link, the account's password, one `UPDATE users SET email`. Chris approves this reading before the task starts — Step 0, in the wording of Task 19 Step 9's `spec-s8.md` — and Task 19 splices the approved wording into the spec as the §8 amendment. The neutral-answer rules are security-04 and infra-M-02 (a taken address gets the same 200 as a free one, and nothing is mailed; the signup guard that keeps a moved-away address from being re-registered answers with the existing neutral "sent" copy, `auth-routes.mjs:322-330`), security-M-03 governs the mail (the link is dispatched and never logged — `dispatch`/`logMailFailure` at `auth-routes.mjs:237-261` are reused, not rewritten), and the password check reuses the one per-account failure bucket login, verify and Task 12's routes share (`accountLimiter`, `auth-routes.mjs:196`).

**Decisions.** (1) **Pinned identity, no re-key.** `users.identity_email` is set at signup, backfilled on upgrade, unique (NOCASE) across accounts, and never updated afterwards; the only D1/R2 consequence of an email change is none. (2) **A consequence, accepted:** an address that is any living account's `identity_email` can never sign up a new account (a new row would hash to that account's workspace); `createUser` throws `AuthError("email-taken")`, which the signup flow already answers with the neutral "sent" page, and `createVerifiedUser` (the boot bootstrap) treats the holder as the existing account (`{ created: false }`, logged as "skipped existing") rather than throwing — a bootstrap collision must never stop the boot (`serve.mjs:170-175` exits 1 on any bootstrap error). (3) **Mail-unconfigured is decided from configuration before any lookup or hash** (the `createAuthRoutes` rule, `auth-routes.mjs:188-191`): production has no `RESEND_API_KEY`/`AUTH_EMAIL_FROM` (Global Constraints), so in production `POST /account/email` answers 503 `mail_unconfigured` until Chris sets them; `GET /account` reports `mailConfigured` so Task 16's sheet shows the support line and disables the primary before any attempt. (4) **The `/verify` page is reused as-is** (keep-list): its form posts `token` + `password` to `/auth/verify`, its copy reads "Confirm your email" / "Confirm my email", and its `retryable` script keeps the confirm view on `error=password` and `error=rate-limited` (`pages/verify.html:66-71, 94-99`); Wave 5 restyles it. (5) **The changed address ends signed in again** on `/profile?notice=email-changed`: `confirmEmailChange` drops every session (the account's password was just proven, a fresh session is issued by the verify branch, every other device is signed out — the change is a credential change), and Task 16's Account screen consumes the notice once. (6) **A separate `email_changes` table**, not a new `tokens.kind`: `tokens.kind` carries `CHECK (kind IN ('verify','reset'))` (`auth.mjs:70`) and SQLite cannot alter a CHECK. (7) **One pending change per account:** a new request replaces the last one — with a link when the address is free, with nothing when it is taken — so a stale link never outlives a newer request and the two branches leave the same shape behind; `GET /account.pendingEmail` reports the real row, so a taken address shows no pending change after a reload (the accepted, documented cost of not saying which addresses have accounts). (8) **The account's own sign-up address may be reclaimed as its contact address** (`(email = ? OR identity_email = ?) AND id <> ?`): nobody else can hold it, and it is the address that keys the workspace — refusing it would strand anyone who changed away and back. (9) **Taken since it was mailed:** if the target address was registered between the mail and the click, `confirmEmailChange` rolls back, consumes the link and returns null; the verify branch sees the link dead and answers `/verify?error=expired` ("invalid, already used, or expired") — never "wrong password", never a hint that the address exists. (10) **Timing:** both the free and the taken branch burn exactly one scrypt (`store.authenticate`); the free branch adds two SQL statements and an un-awaited send. Task 12's JSON routes carry no response floor; the difference is microseconds of SQLite, recorded here as the residual. (11) **Limiters:** Task 12's `opLimiter` (five POSTs per account per quarter hour, counted in `handle`) covers every POST; this route adds `mailLimiter` — three requests per account per hour, free or taken alike, 429 with the shared `rate_limited` sentence; a wrong password counts in the shared `account:${email}` bucket and a tripped bucket answers after the 2 s delay without hashing, exactly as Task 12's password route does. (12) **Log lines by id only:** `{ event: "account_email_change_requested", userId }` (both branches, one line), `{ event: "account_email_change_cancelled", userId }`, `{ event: "account_email_changed", userId }` (the verify branch), and `{ event: "auth_mail_failed", kind: "email-change", error }` from `logMailFailure` — never an address, never the link.

**What is on disk when this task starts (Tasks 12 and 13 have landed):** `deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs` exists with `createAccountRoutes({ store, authRoutes, baseUrl, sendEmail, callWorker, now, sleep, mailConfigured })`, its `json`/`notFound` helpers, `PASSWORD_INCORRECT`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS`, `opLimiter`, `readJsonBody`, the routes `profile`, `password` (Task 12) and `delete` with `purgeWorkspaceWithRetry` and the real `runPendingDeletions` (Task 13), a `POST_ROUTES` map and the `GET /account` block that still answers `identityEmail: session.user.email, pendingEmail: null`. `deploy/railway/auth.mjs` has `updateDisplayName`/`changePassword` (Task 12) and `deleting_at` in `SCHEMA` + `#upgradeSchema`, `#userById`/`authenticate` ignoring parked rows, `beginDeletion`/`pendingDeletions`/`deleteUser` (Task 13; `beginDeletion` and `pendingDeletions` read the row with `SELECT *` and map `identityEmail: row.identity_email ?? row.email`, so the column this task adds reaches them without an edit — Step 3i verifies that). `deploy/railway/auth-routes.mjs` is main @`c6b1fe4` plus Task 12's two edits (`export const CLEAR_COOKIE` at `:146`, the multi-line return at the end of the file) — every anchor below at or above `:434` keeps its `c6b1fe4` line number. `deploy/railway/gateway.mjs` has the `accountRoutes` branch, the `x-itrack-internal*` strip and Task 13's `createWorkerCaller` (which already forwards `oai-authenticated-user-contact-email` when its call carries `contactEmail`); `deploy/railway/serve.mjs` wires `callWorker` and `INTERNAL_ACCOUNT_SECRET`. `db/identity.ts` is main @`c6b1fe4` with `stableUserId` exported (Task 13; its hash expression at `:49` untouched). - [ ] **Step 0: Gate — Chris approves the §8 reading (the task does not start without it)**

Spec §8 (approved) reads "workspace identity remains `sha256(email)`" and lists email change with deletion as a gateway-orchestrated two-store sequence. This task changes that design: the hash is pinned to the sign-up address `users.identity_email`, an email change moves only the contact address (auth.db alone; D1 and R2 are never re-keyed), and a sign-up address can never register a second account while the first lives. Amending §8 is Chris's call, not a build-time decision. - [ ] **Step 1: Write the five failing store tests**

Append to the END of `tests/auth-store.test.mjs` (after the last test Task 13 appended; the file already imports `AuthStore`, `AuthError`, `VERIFY_TTL_MS`, `SESSION_TTL_MS` and builds `require` with `createRequire` at `:13-14`):

```js

test("identity_email is the sign-up address: set by createUser and createVerifiedUser, backfilled with its unique index when an auth.db predates the column, idempotent on a second open", () => {
  const { store } = makeStore();
  const signed = store.createUser({ email: "Signed@E.co", displayName: "S", password: "x".repeat(12) });
  assert.equal(
    store.db.prepare("SELECT identity_email FROM users WHERE id = ?").get(signed.userId).identity_email,
    "signed@e.co",
    "lowercased, like email",
  );
  const booted = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "boot@e.co", displayName: null, password: "x".repeat(12) });
  assert.equal(store.db.prepare("SELECT identity_email FROM users WHERE id = ?").get(booted.userId).identity_email, "boot@e.co");

  // A file from before this task: no identity_email (and no deleting_at). The
  // rows in it signed up with the address they carry, so the backfill is exact.
  const { DatabaseSync } = require("node:sqlite");
  const dbPath = `${process.env.TMPDIR ?? "/tmp"}/auth-upgrade-identity-${process.pid}.db`;
  const legacy = new DatabaseSync(dbPath);
  legacy.exec(`CREATE TABLE users (id TEXT PRIMARY KEY, email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE, display_name TEXT, password_scrypt TEXT NOT NULL, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, verified_at INTEGER);
    CREATE TABLE tokens (token_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, kind TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (kind IN ('verify','reset')), expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, used_at INTEGER);
    CREATE TABLE sessions (session_hash TEXT PRIMARY KEY, user_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE, created_at INTEGER NOT NULL, expires_at INTEGER NOT NULL, last_seen_at INTEGER NOT NULL, cookie_issued_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0);
    INSERT INTO users (id, email, display_name, password_scrypt, created_at, verified_at) VALUES ('acct_old', 'old@e.co', 'Old', 'scrypt:x', 1, 1);`);
  legacy.close();
  const upgraded = new AuthStore(dbPath);
  const columns = upgraded.db.prepare("PRAGMA table_info(users)").all().map((row) => row.name);
  assert.ok(columns.includes("identity_email"));
  assert.ok(columns.includes("deleting_at"), "Task 13's column arrives in the same upgrade");
  assert.equal(upgraded.db.prepare("SELECT identity_email FROM users WHERE id = 'acct_old'").get().identity_email, "old@e.co", "backfilled from email");
  const index = upgraded.db.prepare("PRAGMA index_list(users)").all().find((row) => row.name === "users_identity_email_unique");
  assert.ok(index, "the unique index exists");
  assert.equal(Number(index.unique), 1);
  assert.equal(upgraded.createVerifiedUser({ email: "old@e.co", displayName: null, password: "x".repeat(12) }).created, false, "the upgraded row is the existing account");
  upgraded.close();
  const again = new AuthStore(dbPath);
  assert.equal(again.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users").get().n, 1, "a second open changes nothing");
  again.close();
  require("node:fs").rmSync(dbPath, { force: true });
});

test("signup refuses an address that is another account's identity address — the workspace that address keys is theirs — and bootstrap treats its holder as the existing account", () => {
  const { store } = makeStore();
  const owner = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "first@e.co", displayName: "O", password: "x".repeat(12) });
  const { token } = store.createEmailChange(owner.userId, "second@e.co");
  assert.ok(store.confirmEmailChange(token, "x".repeat(12)));
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("second@e.co", "x".repeat(12)).user.identityEmail, "first@e.co", "moved the contact address only");
  assert.throws(
    () => store.createUser({ email: "First@E.co", displayName: "Squatter", password: "y".repeat(12) }),
    (err) => err instanceof AuthError && err.code === "email-taken",
    "nobody signs up with an address that keys a living workspace",
  );
  assert.throws(
    () => store.createUser({ email: "second@e.co", displayName: "Squatter", password: "y".repeat(12) }),
    (err) => err instanceof AuthError && err.code === "email-taken",
    "…nor with the account's current contact address",
  );
  const boot = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "first@e.co", displayName: null, password: "z".repeat(12) });
  assert.deepEqual(boot, { userId: owner.userId, created: false }, "bootstrap skips it as existing — never a second row, never a thrown boot");
  assert.equal(store.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM users").get().n, 1);
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("first@e.co", "z".repeat(12)).ok, false, "the bootstrap password was not written anywhere");
});

test("createEmailChange refuses the account's own address and any taken one, allows its own sign-up address back, and replaces a prior pending change — with nothing when the new target is taken", () => {
  const { store } = makeStore();
  const a = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "a@e.co", displayName: "A", password: "a".repeat(12) });
  const b = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "b@e.co", displayName: "B", password: "b".repeat(12) });
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, "a@e.co"), null, "its own address");
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, " A@E.CO "), null, "…however spelled");
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, ""), null);
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, undefined), null);
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange("acct_missing", "x@e.co"), null, "unknown account");
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(a.userId), null);
  const first = store.createEmailChange(a.userId, "Fresh@E.co");
  assert.match(first.token, /^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{40,}$/);
  assert.deepEqual(store.pendingEmailChange(a.userId), { newEmail: "fresh@e.co", expiresAt: 1_000_000_000_000 + VERIFY_TTL_MS });
  assert.deepEqual(store.peekEmailChange(first.token), { userId: a.userId, email: "a@e.co", newEmail: "fresh@e.co" });
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, "B@E.CO"), null, "another account's contact address, NOCASE");
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(a.userId), null, "a request for a taken address still replaces the last one — with nothing");
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(first.token), null, "…so the earlier link is dead");
  const second = store.createEmailChange(a.userId, "other@e.co");
  assert.notEqual(second.token, first.token);
  assert.deepEqual(store.pendingEmailChange(a.userId), { newEmail: "other@e.co", expiresAt: 1_000_000_000_000 + VERIFY_TTL_MS });
  assert.ok(store.confirmEmailChange(second.token, "a".repeat(12)));
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("other@e.co", "a".repeat(12)).ok, true);
  assert.ok(store.createEmailChange(a.userId, "a@e.co"), "its own sign-up address may come back: nobody else can hold it");
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(b.userId, "a@e.co"), null, "…and nobody else may take it: it keys A's workspace");
  assert.equal(store.createEmailChange(b.userId, "other@e.co"), null, "A's contact address is taken too");
  assert.ok(store.createEmailChange(b.userId, "free@e.co"));
});

test("peekEmailChange/confirmEmailChange: the current password, single use, expiry after VERIFY_TTL_MS, the contact address moved, every session dropped, identity_email untouched; an address taken since it was mailed kills the link", () => {
  const { store, tick } = makeStore();
  const { userId } = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "move@e.co", displayName: "M", password: "right-pass-123" });
  const laptop = store.createSession(userId);
  const phone = store.createSession(userId);
  const { token } = store.createEmailChange(userId, "moved@e.co");
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(token, "wrong-pass-123"), null, "wrong password is refused");
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(token), null, "no password is refused");
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(token, ""), null, "empty password is refused");
  assert.ok(store.peekEmailChange(token), "the refusals did not consume the link");
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(laptop), "…or touch a session");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("move@e.co", "right-pass-123").ok, true, "…or the address");
  assert.deepEqual(store.confirmEmailChange(token, "right-pass-123"), { userId, email: "moved@e.co", displayName: "M" });
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(laptop), null, "every session is dropped: the change is a credential change");
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(phone), null);
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("move@e.co", "right-pass-123").ok, false, "the old address no longer signs in");
  const auth = store.authenticate("moved@e.co", "right-pass-123");
  assert.equal(auth.ok, true);
  assert.equal(auth.user.identityEmail, "move@e.co", "the workspace identity is the sign-up address still");
  assert.equal(store.db.prepare("SELECT identity_email FROM users WHERE id = ?").get(userId).identity_email, "move@e.co");
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(userId), null, "nothing pending once confirmed");
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(token), null, "consumed");
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(token, "right-pass-123"), null, "single use");
  const late = store.createEmailChange(userId, "late@e.co");
  tick(VERIFY_TTL_MS + 1);
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(late.token), null, "expired");
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(late.token, "right-pass-123"), null);
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(userId), null, "an expired change is not pending");
  // Taken between the mail and the click: the link dies, nothing else moves.
  const desk = store.createSession(userId);
  const raced = store.createEmailChange(userId, "race@e.co");
  store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "race@e.co", displayName: "R", password: "r".repeat(12) });
  assert.equal(store.confirmEmailChange(raced.token, "right-pass-123"), null);
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(raced.token), null, "the link is dead — the verify route reads that as expired, not as a wrong password");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("moved@e.co", "right-pass-123").ok, true, "the account is as it was");
  assert.ok(store.sessionUser(desk), "…sessions included");
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange("nope"), null);
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(undefined), null);
});

test("sessionUser, authenticate, beginDeletion and pendingDeletions carry identityEmail; cancelEmailChange and cleanup remove pending rows", () => {
  const { store, tick } = makeStore();
  const { userId } = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "id@e.co", displayName: "I", password: "i".repeat(12) });
  const before = store.createSession(userId);
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(before).identityEmail, "id@e.co");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("id@e.co", "i".repeat(12)).user.identityEmail, "id@e.co");
  const { token } = store.createEmailChange(userId, "contact@e.co");
  assert.ok(store.confirmEmailChange(token, "i".repeat(12)));
  const after = store.createSession(userId);
  const user = store.sessionUser(after);
  assert.equal(user.email, "contact@e.co");
  assert.equal(user.identityEmail, "id@e.co");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("contact@e.co", "i".repeat(12)).user.identityEmail, "id@e.co");
  const cancelled = store.createEmailChange(userId, "c@e.co");
  assert.ok(store.pendingEmailChange(userId));
  store.cancelEmailChange(userId);
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(userId), null);
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(cancelled.token), null, "a cancelled link is dead");
  store.cancelEmailChange(userId);
  store.cancelEmailChange("acct_missing");
  store.createEmailChange(userId, "d@e.co");
  tick(VERIFY_TTL_MS + 1);
  store.cleanup();
  assert.equal(store.db.prepare("SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM email_changes").get().n, 0, "cleanup sweeps expired changes");
  // Task 13's deletion path carries the identity the worker must purge —
  // the sign-up address, not the contact address the account moved to.
  assert.deepEqual(store.beginDeletion(userId), { userId, email: "contact@e.co", identityEmail: "id@e.co" });
  assert.deepEqual(store.pendingDeletions().map((row) => [row.userId, row.email, row.identityEmail]), [[userId, "contact@e.co", "id@e.co"]]);
});
```

**3a — `SCHEMA`.** Insert `  identity_email TEXT,` on its own line directly after

```sql
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
```

and append the fourth table after the sessions block — i.e. after the line `);` that follows `  cookie_issued_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0` and before the closing backtick of the template literal — so the whole constant reads (Task 13's `deleting_at INTEGER` line is already in the users block):

```js
const SCHEMA = `
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS users (
  id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  email TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE COLLATE NOCASE,
  identity_email TEXT,

);
```

**3b — `#upgradeSchema`.** Replace the whole method — from `  #upgradeSchema() {` through its closing `  }` (at `c6b1fe4` it was `:99-110`; Task 13 added the `users`/`deleting_at` guard inside it) — with:

```js
  // Additive migrations for auth.db files created by earlier builds. Each
  // guard is idempotent so the constructor can run on every boot.
  #upgradeSchema() {
    const sessionColumns = this.db
      .prepare("PRAGMA table_info(sessions)")
      .all()
      .map((row) => row.name);
    if (!sessionColumns.includes("cookie_issued_at")) {
      this.db.exec(
        "ALTER TABLE sessions ADD COLUMN cookie_issued_at INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0",
      );
      this.db.exec("UPDATE sessions SET cookie_issued_at = created_at WHERE cookie_issued_at = 0");
    }
    const userColumns = this.db
      .prepare("PRAGMA table_info(users)")
      .all()
      .map((row) => row.name);
    if (!userColumns.includes("deleting_at")) {
      this.db.exec("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN deleting_at INTEGER");
    }
    // The workspace identity: the address the account signed up with. The
    // worker hashes it into every D1 row id and R2 key (db/identity.ts), so
    // it never changes; an email change moves `email` alone. Every row from
    // before the column signed up with the address it carries, so the
    // backfill is exact — Chris's production row included.
    if (!userColumns.includes("identity_email")) {
      this.db.exec("ALTER TABLE users ADD COLUMN identity_email TEXT");
      this.db.exec("UPDATE users SET identity_email = email WHERE identity_email IS NULL");
    }
    // Idempotent, so it runs on every boot: a fresh SCHEMA has the column
    // but not the index; an upgraded file gets it once.
    this.db.exec(
      "CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS users_identity_email_unique ON users (identity_email COLLATE NOCASE)",
    );
  }
```

**3e — `createVerifiedUser`.** Replace the whole method (`:189-201`) with:

```js
  // Startup bootstrap: creates a VERIFIED account only when no row exists for
  // the address. Existing rows (verified or not) are never modified — and an
  // account that signed up with the address and moved its contact address
  // away counts as existing: never a second row over the same workspace
  // hash, never a thrown error that stops the boot.
  createVerifiedUser({ email, displayName, password }) {
    const normalized = String(email).trim().toLowerCase();
    const existing = this.db.prepare("SELECT id FROM users WHERE email = ?").get(normalized);
    if (existing) return { userId: existing.id, created: false };
    const holder = this.#identityHolder(normalized);
    if (holder) return { userId: holder.id, created: false };
    const userId = `acct_${randomUUID()}`;
    const now = this.now();
    this.db
      .prepare(
        "INSERT INTO users (id, email, identity_email, display_name, password_scrypt, created_at, verified_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?, ?)",

      .run(userId, normalized, normalized, displayName ?? null, hashPassword(password), now, now);
```

**3g — the email-change block.** Insert the following before the comment line `  // Rows whose address is not printable ASCII — created before signup` (`:337` at `c6b1fe4`; Tasks 12–13 inserted their methods above it, which is fine — this block goes directly above that comment):

```js
  // ----- Email change (spec §6 Account; §8 as amended by Wave 4) -----
  // A change moves the CONTACT address only: `email` is what signs in and
  // what the gateway forwards as oai-authenticated-user-contact-email.
  // `identity_email` — the address the account signed up with — never
  // changes, is forwarded as oai-authenticated-user-email, and is what the
  // worker hashes into every D1 row id and R2 key. So a change touches this
  // store alone: no worker action, no R2 move, nothing to retry.

  // The account whose sign-up address this is, if any (NOCASE, like email).
  #identityHolder(address) {
    return this.db
      .prepare("SELECT id FROM users WHERE identity_email = ? COLLATE NOCASE")
      .get(address) ?? null;
  }

  // The live change behind a link, joined to its account, without consuming
  // it. null when the link is unknown, used, expired, or the account is
  // parked for deletion.
  #liveEmailChange(rawToken) {
    const row = this.db
      .prepare(
        `SELECT c.token_hash, c.user_id, c.new_email, c.expires_at, c.used_at,
                u.email, u.display_name, u.password_scrypt, u.deleting_at
           FROM email_changes c JOIN users u ON u.id = c.user_id
          WHERE c.token_hash = ?`,
      )
      .get(sha256Hex(String(rawToken ?? "")));
    if (!row || row.used_at !== null || row.expires_at < this.now() || row.deleting_at !== null) return null;
    return row;
  }

  // Starts a change to `newEmail` and returns the raw token to mail, or null
  // when there is nothing to mail: an unknown or parked account, an empty
  // address, the account's own current address, or an address that signs in
  // another account or keys another account's workspace (its own sign-up
  // address is allowed back — nobody else can hold it). The caller answers
  // the same way either way (security-04, infra-M-02). One pending change
  // per account: a new request replaces the last one — with a link when the
  // address is free, with nothing when it is not — so a stale link never
  // outlives a newer request and both outcomes leave the same shape behind.
  createEmailChange(userId, newEmail) {
    const address = String(newEmail ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
    const me = this.#userById(userId);
    if (!me || !address || address === me.email.toLowerCase()) return null;
    this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM email_changes WHERE user_id = ?").run(userId);
    const taken = this.db
      .prepare("SELECT id FROM users WHERE (email = ? OR identity_email = ? COLLATE NOCASE) AND id <> ?")
      .get(address, address, userId);
    if (taken) return null;
    const token = randomBytes(32).toString("base64url");
    this.db
      .prepare(
        "INSERT INTO email_changes (token_hash, user_id, new_email, expires_at) VALUES (?, ?, ?, ?)",
      )
      .run(sha256Hex(token), userId, address, this.now() + VERIFY_TTL_MS);
    return { token };
  }

  // What GET /account reports: the live change, if any.
  pendingEmailChange(userId) {
    const row = this.db
      .prepare(
        "SELECT new_email, expires_at FROM email_changes WHERE user_id = ? AND used_at IS NULL AND expires_at >= ?",
      )
      .get(userId, this.now());
    return row ? { newEmail: row.new_email, expiresAt: Number(row.expires_at) } : null;
  }

  cancelEmailChange(userId) {
    this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM email_changes WHERE user_id = ?").run(userId);
  }

  // The account and target behind a live link. `email` is the CURRENT
  // address — the verify route keys its per-account limiter on it, the same
  // bucket login guesses against.
  peekEmailChange(rawToken) {
    const row = this.#liveEmailChange(rawToken);
    return row ? { userId: row.user_id, email: row.email, newEmail: row.new_email } : null;
  }

  // Confirms a change — only with the account's current password, for the
  // reason verifyEmail gives: a link proves inbox access, not presence at the
  // account. A wrong password leaves the link live (the caller limits the
  // attempts). On success, in one transaction: the link is consumed, the
  // contact address moves, every session is dropped (the verify route issues
  // a fresh one); identity_email is untouched. If the address was taken
  // between the mail and the click, the transaction rolls back, the link is
  // consumed and null comes back — the caller sees a dead link, never a hint
  // that the address exists.
  confirmEmailChange(rawToken, password) {
    const row = this.#liveEmailChange(rawToken);
    if (!row) return null;
    if (!verifyPassword(String(password ?? ""), row.password_scrypt)) return null;
    const now = this.now();
    const consume = this.db.prepare("UPDATE email_changes SET used_at = ? WHERE token_hash = ?");
    this.db.exec("BEGIN");
    try {
      consume.run(now, row.token_hash);
      this.db.prepare("UPDATE users SET email = ? WHERE id = ?").run(row.new_email, row.user_id);
      this.db.prepare("DELETE FROM sessions WHERE user_id = ?").run(row.user_id);
      this.db.exec("COMMIT");
    } catch (error) {
      this.db.exec("ROLLBACK");
      if (!String(error?.message).includes("UNIQUE")) throw error;
      consume.run(now, row.token_hash);
      return null;
    }
    return { userId: row.user_id, email: row.new_email, displayName: row.display_name };
  }
```

- [ ] **Step 7: The worker — `db/identity.ts` whole, `db/runtime.ts` one binding**

Replace `db/identity.ts` whole. Everything below is main @`c6b1fe4` plus Task 13's `export` on `stableUserId`, with the type, the header constant and `resolveRequestIdentity` changed; the hash expression at `:49` (`new TextEncoder().encode(\`license-lantern:${email}\`)`) is a protected identifier (`tests/protected-identifiers.test.mjs:56-60`) and is byte-identical:

```ts
export type RequestIdentity = {
  userId: string;
  // The contact address: what the app shows and what mail reaches. An email
  // change (the gateway's account routes) moves it.
  email: string;
  // The sign-up address: what userId hashes, forever. The gateway forwards
  // it as oai-authenticated-user-email and the contact address beside it as
  // oai-authenticated-user-contact-email; a request that carries only the
  // first has one address for both.
  identityEmail: string;
  displayName: string;
  isDemo: boolean;
};

const EMAIL_HEADER = "oai-authenticated-user-email";
const CONTACT_EMAIL_HEADER = "oai-authenticated-user-contact-email";
const NAME_HEADER = "oai-authenticated-user-full-name";
const NAME_ENCODING_HEADER = "oai-authenticated-user-full-name-encoding";
const PERCENT_ENCODED_UTF8 = "percent-encoded-utf-8";
// The app's product name is iTrack, but the identifiers below predate the
// product renames and are load-bearing: the demo email and the
// "license-lantern:" hash salt both feed stableUserId, so changing either
// would orphan every existing user's data. Leave them as-is.
const DEMO_EMAIL = "demo@local.license-lantern";

function isLocalHostname(hostname: string): boolean {
  const normalized = hostname.toLowerCase().replace(/^\[|\]$/g, "");
  return (
    normalized === "localhost" ||
    normalized.endsWith(".localhost") ||
    normalized === "127.0.0.1" ||
    normalized === "::1"
  );
}

function safeDecodeName(value: string | null, encoding: string | null) {
  if (!value || encoding !== PERCENT_ENCODED_UTF8) return null;
  try {
    const decoded = decodeURIComponent(value).trim();
    return decoded ? decoded.slice(0, 160) : null;
  } catch {
    return null;
  }
}

function displayNameFromEmail(email: string) {
  const localPart = email.split("@")[0] || "professional";
  const words = localPart
    .replace(/[._+-]+/g, " ")
    .split(/\s+/)
    .filter(Boolean)
    .map((word) => word.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + word.slice(1));
  return words.join(" ") || "Professional";
}

export async function stableUserId(email: string): Promise<string> {
  const bytes = new TextEncoder().encode(`license-lantern:${email}`);
  const digest = await crypto.subtle.digest("SHA-256", bytes);
  const hex = Array.from(new Uint8Array(digest), (byte) =>
    byte.toString(16).padStart(2, "0"),
  ).join("");
  return `usr_${hex}`;
}

export async function resolveRequestIdentity(
  request: Request,
): Promise<RequestIdentity | null> {
  const requestUrl = new URL(request.url);
  const forwardedEmail = request.headers.get(EMAIL_HEADER)?.trim().toLowerCase();

  if (forwardedEmail) {
    const displayName =
      safeDecodeName(
        request.headers.get(NAME_HEADER),
        request.headers.get(NAME_ENCODING_HEADER),
      ) ?? displayNameFromEmail(forwardedEmail);
    // The contact address rides beside the identity; absent, the identity
    // address is the contact address (every pre-change account, every test
    // harness, every request the fixtures send).
    const contactEmail = request.headers.get(CONTACT_EMAIL_HEADER)?.trim().toLowerCase();
    return {
      userId: await stableUserId(forwardedEmail),
      email: (contactEmail || forwardedEmail).slice(0, 320),
      identityEmail: forwardedEmail.slice(0, 320),
      displayName,
      isDemo: false,
    };
  }

  if (!isLocalHostname(requestUrl.hostname)) return null;

  return {
    userId: await stableUserId(DEMO_EMAIL),
    email: DEMO_EMAIL,
    identityEmail: DEMO_EMAIL,
    displayName: "Alex Morgan",
    isDemo: true,
  };
}
```

(`userId` hashes the unsliced `forwardedEmail`, exactly as before; a contact header without an identity header falls through to the anonymous/demo branches — the contact address never keys anything.)

```js
  const { store, routes } = makeRoutes();

  assert.equal(res.headers["set-cookie"], undefined);

test("verify with an email-change link shares the per-account bucket with login, keyed on the CURRENT address: ten wrong passwords lock both", async () => {
  const { store, routes, sleeps } = makeRoutes();
  const { userId } = store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "lock@e.co", displayName: "L", password: "longenough1" });
  const { token } = store.createEmailChange(userId, "locked@e.co");
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) {
    const { res } = await post(routes, "/auth/verify", form({ token, password: "wrong-pass-1" }),
      { "x-forwarded-for": `10.0.${i}.1` });
    assert.equal(res.headers.location, `/verify?error=password&token=${token}`);
  }
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [], "no delay while under the limit");
  let scrypts = 0;
  for (const method of ["confirmEmailChange", "authenticate"]) {
    const original = store[method].bind(store);
    store[method] = (...args) => { scrypts += 1; return original(...args); };
  }
  let { res } = await post(routes, "/auth/verify", form({ token, password: "longenough1" }), { "x-forwarded-for": "10.9.9.9" });
  assert.equal(res.headers.location, `/verify?error=password&token=${token}`, "even the right password is refused while tripped");
  assert.equal(res.headers["set-cookie"], undefined);
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/auth/login", form({ email: "lock@e.co", password: "longenough1" }), { "x-forwarded-for": "10.9.9.8" }));
  assert.equal(res.headers.location, "/login?error=bad-credentials", "login for the current address is locked by the same bucket");
  assert.deepEqual(sleeps, [2000, 2000]);
  assert.equal(scrypts, 0, "scrypt is not burned for a tripped account");
  assert.ok(store.peekEmailChange(token), "the link survives the lockout for a retry after the window");
  // The per-IP login limiter counts here too, and keeps the link.
  const fresh = makeRoutes();
  const other = fresh.store.createVerifiedUser({ email: "ip@e.co", displayName: "I", password: "longenough1" });
  const { token: ipToken } = fresh.store.createEmailChange(other.userId, "ip-moved@e.co");
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i += 1) {
    await post(fresh.routes, "/auth/login", form({ email: `x${i}@e.co`, password: "wrong-pass-1" }));
  }
  ({ res } = await post(fresh.routes, "/auth/verify", form({ token: ipToken, password: "longenough1" })));
  assert.equal(res.headers.location, `/verify?error=rate-limited&token=${ipToken}`);
  assert.equal(res.headers["set-cookie"], undefined);
  assert.ok(fresh.store.peekEmailChange(ipToken));
});
```

```js
test("a session whose IDENTITY address is not a legal header value is refused too, even once its contact address is", async (t) => {
  const stack = await startStack();
  t.after(() => stack.close());
  const logs = [];
  const originalLog = console.log;

  // A row from before EMAIL_RE that later moved its contact address to a
  // legal one: the identity header would still carry U+0101, which

  const { token } = stack.store.createEmailChange(userId, "legal@e.co");

  assert.equal(stack.store.authenticate("legal@e.co", "longenough1").user.identityEmail, "ā@e.co");
  const cookie = `${SESSION_COOKIE}=${signValue(stack.store.createSession(userId), "gw-secret")}`;
  const before = stack.upstreamSeen();
  const json = await get(stack.base, "/api/workspace", { accept: "application/json", cookie });
  assert.equal(json.status, 401);
  assert.equal(stack.upstreamSeen(), before, "nothing reached the worker");
  assert.deepEqual(JSON.parse(logs[0]), { event: "auth_session_refused", reason: "email_not_header_safe", userId });
  assert.doesNotMatch(logs.join("\n"), /@e\.co/, "ids, never addresses");
});
```

```js
      // An email-change link (account-routes.mjs) lands on the same page and
      // posts here, so it is tried first. Same shape as a verify link: the
      // password proves the account, a wrong one keeps the link for a retry,
      // and the attempts are limited per IP and per account — keyed on the
      // CURRENT address, the one login guesses against. Confirming drops
      // every session (confirmEmailChange); the fresh one is issued here.
      const change = store.peekEmailChange(token);
      if (change) {
        const retryChange = (error) => `/verify?error=${error}&token=${encodeURIComponent(token)}`;
        const ipKey = `login:${ip}`;
        if (!loginLimiter.check(ipKey)) return redirect(res, retryChange("rate-limited")), true;
        const accountKey = `account:${change.email}`;
        if (!accountLimiter.check(accountKey)) {
          loginLimiter.allow(ipKey);
          await sleep(ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS);
          return redirect(res, retryChange("password")), true;
        }
        const confirmed = store.confirmEmailChange(token, password);
        if (!confirmed) {
          // The address was taken since the link was mailed: the store
          // consumed the link, and the page's "invalid, already used, or
          // expired" is all anyone learns.
          if (!store.peekEmailChange(token)) return redirect(res, "/verify?error=expired"), true;
          loginLimiter.allow(ipKey);
          accountLimiter.allow(accountKey);
          return redirect(res, retryChange("password")), true;
        }
        console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_email_changed", userId: confirmed.userId }));
        issueSessionCookie(res, confirmed.userId);
        return redirect(res, "/profile?notice=email-changed"), true;
      }
```

```js
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 400);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "That is already your email.", code: "same_email" });
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "new@e.co", password: "wrong-pass-1234" }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403);
  assert.deepEqual(json, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "new@e.co" }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 403, "a missing password is a wrong one");
  assert.deepEqual(json, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(userId), null, "nothing started");
  assert.equal(sent.length, 0, "nothing mailed");
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), true, "two failures are under the limit…");
  for (let i = 0; i < 8; i += 1) authRoutes.recordPasswordFailure(email);
  assert.equal(authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(email), false, "…and they counted: eight more trip the bucket login shares");
});

test("POST /account/email: 503 mail_unconfigured is decided by configuration before any lookup or hash — no store call, no pending change, and GET /account says so up front", async () => {
  const { store, routes, sent } = makeRoutes({ mailConfigured: false });
  const { cookie, userId, password } = signedIn(store);
  let calls = 0;
  for (const method of ["authenticate", "createEmailChange"]) {
    const original = store[method].bind(store);
    store[method] = (...args) => { calls += 1; return original(...args); };
  }
  const { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "new@e.co", password }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 503);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Email delivery is not set up yet; contact support@itrackceu.com", code: "mail_unconfigured" });
  assert.equal(calls, 0, "neither the password nor the address was looked at");
  assert.equal(store.pendingEmailChange(userId), null);
  assert.equal(sent.length, 0);
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.mailConfigured, false, "what the sheet reads before it even tries");
});

test("POST /account/email: a free address mails one link and GET /account shows the pending change; a taken address gets the identical 200 and no mail; cancel clears it; confirming through /auth/verify moves the contact address and keeps identityEmail", async () => {
  const { store, authRoutes, routes, sent, tick } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, raw, password } = signedIn(store, "mover@e.co", "current-pass-12", "Mover");
  signedIn(store, "taken@e.co");
  const expiresAt = 1_700_000_000_000 + VERIFY_TTL_MS;
  assert.deepEqual((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json, {
    email: "mover@e.co", identityEmail: "mover@e.co", displayName: "Mover", pendingEmail: null, mailConfigured: true,
  });
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "Moved@E.co", password }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true, pending: { newEmail: "moved@e.co", expiresAt } });
  assert.equal(sent.length, 1);
  assert.equal(sent[0].to, "moved@e.co");
  assert.equal(sent[0].subject, "Confirm your new iTrack email");
  assert.doesNotMatch(sent[0].text, /Mover|mover@e\.co|moved@e\.co/, "no name, no address in the body");
  const first = sent[0].text.match(/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/)[1];
  assert.deepEqual((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.pendingEmail, { newEmail: "moved@e.co", expiresAt });
  // The taken address: same status, same shape, nothing mailed — and, since
  // a request replaces the last one, nothing pending after a reload.
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "TAKEN@e.co", password }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true, pending: { newEmail: "taken@e.co", expiresAt } });
  assert.equal(sent.length, 1, "nothing mailed for a taken address");
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.pendingEmail, null, "a reload shows no pending change: the documented cost of saying nothing");
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(first), null, "the earlier link is dead either way");
  // Cancel.
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "again@e.co", password }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.equal(sent.length, 2);
  ({ res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email/cancel", {}, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { ok: true });
  assert.equal((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.pendingEmail, null);
  assert.equal(store.peekEmailChange(sent[1].text.match(/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/)[1]), null, "a cancelled link is dead");
  // Confirm one end to end. Four POSTs are spent of five per quarter hour,
  // and three mails of three per hour: wait the hour out.
  tick(60 * 60 * 1000 + 1);
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "final@e.co", password }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200);
  const token = sent[2].text.match(/token=([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)/)[1];
  const verify = await postForm(authRoutes, "/auth/verify", { token, password });
  assert.equal(verify.res.headers.location, "/profile?notice=email-changed");
  assert.equal(store.sessionUser(raw), null, "the session that asked is gone with every other");
  const fresh = verify.res.headers["set-cookie"].split(";")[0];
  assert.deepEqual((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie: fresh })).json, {
    email: "final@e.co", identityEmail: "mover@e.co", displayName: "Mover", pendingEmail: null, mailConfigured: true,
  });
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("mover@e.co", password).ok, false, "the old address no longer signs in");
  assert.equal(store.authenticate("final@e.co", password).user.identityEmail, "mover@e.co", "the workspace identity is the sign-up address still");
});

test("POST /account/email: 429 rate_limited on the fourth request in an hour, per account, free or taken alike; the window resets", async () => {
  const { store, routes, sent, tick } = makeRoutes();
  const { cookie, password } = signedIn(store);
  signedIn(store, "held@e.co");
  for (const [i, address] of ["try1@e.co", "held@e.co", "try3@e.co"].entries()) {
    const { res } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: address, password }, { cookie });
    assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, `request ${i + 1}`);
  }
  assert.equal(sent.length, 2, "the taken one mailed nothing but counted");
  let { res, json } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "try4@e.co", password }, { cookie });
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 429);
  assert.deepEqual(json, { error: "Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again.", code: "rate_limited" });
  assert.deepEqual((await get(routes, "/account", { cookie })).json.pendingEmail.newEmail, "try3@e.co", "the fourth did not replace the third");
  const other = signedIn(store, "other@e.co");
  assert.equal((await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "elsewhere@e.co", password: other.password }, { cookie: other.cookie })).res.statusCode, 200, "per account");
  tick(60 * 60 * 1000 + 1);
  ({ res } = await post(routes, "/account/email", { newEmail: "try5@e.co", password }, { cookie }));
  assert.equal(res.statusCode, 200, "a new hour");
});
```
