**19c — the two routes.** Insert before `  const POST_ROUTES = new Map([`:

```js
  // POST /account/email — starts a change to a new contact address. Neutral
  // by construction (security-04, infra-M-02): once the address is well-
  // formed and not the account's own, mail is configured and the password
  // holds, the answer is the same 200 whether or not the address is free —
  // a free one is mailed a confirmation link (auth-routes.mjs
  // emailChangeEmail, through the same dispatch as signup), a taken one is
  // mailed nothing. The pending change GET /account reports is the real
  // row, so a taken address shows none after a reload: the accepted cost of
  // not saying which addresses have accounts. Both branches burn one scrypt
  // (authenticate); the free branch adds two SQL statements and a send that
  // is never awaited.
  async function email(res, session, body) {
    const address = String(body.newEmail ?? "").trim().toLowerCase();
    if (!EMAIL_RE.test(address)) {
      return json(res, 400, { error: "Enter a valid email address.", code: "invalid_email" });
    }
    if (address === session.user.email.toLowerCase()) {
      return json(res, 400, { error: "That is already your email.", code: "same_email" });
    }
    // Configuration, decided before any lookup or hash (the createAuthRoutes
    // rule): the sheet already shows this line from GET /account.
    if (!mailConfigured) return json(res, 503, MAIL_UNCONFIGURED);
    if (!authRoutes.passwordAttemptAllowed(session.user.email)) {
      // Tripped by this route, the password route or login: fixed delay,
      // generic answer, no scrypt.
      await sleep(ACCOUNT_LOCK_DELAY_MS);
      return json(res, 403, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
    }
    const attempt = store.authenticate(session.user.email, String(body.password ?? ""));
    if (!attempt.ok) {
      authRoutes.recordPasswordFailure(session.user.email);
      return json(res, 403, PASSWORD_INCORRECT);
    }
    if (!mailLimiter.allow(`mail:${session.user.id}`)) return json(res, 429, RATE_LIMITED);
    const created = store.createEmailChange(session.user.id, address);
    if (created) authRoutes.dispatch("email-change", address, emailChangeEmail(baseUrl, created.token));
    // One line either way, by id — never the address, never the link.
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_email_change_requested", userId: session.user.id }));
    return json(res, 200, { ok: true, pending: { newEmail: address, expiresAt: now() + VERIFY_TTL_MS } });
  }

  // POST /account/email/cancel (body {}): the pending change, if any, is
  // gone and its link is dead.
  function cancelEmail(res, session) {
    store.cancelEmailChange(session.user.id);
    console.log(JSON.stringify({ event: "account_email_change_cancelled", userId: session.user.id }));
    return json(res, 200, { ok: true });
  }

```

**Gotchas for this task:** Task 13's `beginDeletion`/`pendingDeletions` read the row with `SELECT *` and map `row.identity_email ?? row.email` — Step 3i only verifies that spelling survived, because a SELECT that named its columns without `identity_email` would make the fallback win forever, and a deletion after an email change would hand `deleteWorkspace` the contact address, purge an empty workspace and orphan the real one; the last store test pins it. `HEADER_VALUE_RE` must hold for both addresses or the session is refused (`auth_session_refused`, by id): a pre-`EMAIL_RE` row that moves to a legal contact address still cannot be proxied, and `serve.mjs:180-185`'s boot count reads `email` only — that warning stays as it is (a Wave 5 ops-floor item, not this task's). The email-change branch runs before `peekVerifyToken` on every `POST /auth/verify`: one extra `SELECT` on `email_changes` per verify, nothing else changes for a plain verify link (`tests/auth-routes.test.mjs:160` and the gateway's "signup -> verify -> session cookie -> app" prove it). `createEmailChange` deletes the prior pending row *before* the taken check on purpose (decision 7): a taken address leaves nothing pending, and `GET /account` says so after a reload — the test documents it, the sheet (Task 16) shows the neutral notice from the 200. The 429 sentence is the copy table's one `rate_limited` line ("Wait 15 minutes") while the email window is an hour; the table has one sentence and this task adds no prose — a fourth request within the hour is refused with it (Task 16 renders it). The signup consequence (decision 2) is permanent while the account lives: an address that was ever a living account's sign-up address cannot be registered anew; Task 13's `deleteUser` removes the row and frees it. `confirmEmailChange` wraps three statements in `BEGIN … COMMIT` on the store's one `DatabaseSync` handle — nothing else in `auth.mjs` opens a transaction, and the gateway is single-threaded, so no other statement can interleave; a UNIQUE failure (`users_email_unique` via `users.email`'s NOCASE constraint) rolls back and then consumes the link outside the transaction. ### Task 15: Full export: GET /api/export/all streams a store-only zip (workspace.json, activities.csv incl. archived, every evidence file, evidence.json) via pure zipStore.ts; activities CSV query shared in _activityCsv.ts; isolation/gateway/live-smoke/run-check coverage

**Rationale:** spec §6 Account — "data export (full JSON + CSV + evidence zip — critic-06)" — and §9 Deploy ("Docker build + run-check locally before every merge; live smoke (curl matrix + Playwright login) after every deploy"), §4's isolation rule ("every workspace action, `/api/evidence` read/write, `/api/export/*`, and the packet route refuse cross-identity ids"). Audit critic-06 (P3, carry_into_redesign): "Data portability is one-directional and partial: CSV export covers non-archived activities only (no credentials, tasks, check-in state, or evidence files)" — its recommendation is "a full export (JSON + evidence files as a zip …); keep the CSV formula-injection guard (csvCell) — it is correct"; architecture-M-03's "no … data export for self-serve users" and app-ux-M-02's missing Account self-service are the same gap seen from the identity and the screen. Today the only exports are `GET /api/export` (`app/api/export/route.ts:27-144` — one query at `:43-84` with `WHERE a.user_id = ?\n          AND a.archived_at IS NULL` at `:79-80`, `csvCell` at `:21-25`, the header/assembly at `:86-112`, the filename date in the stored reminder zone at `:113-123`) and the per-credential HTML packet (`app/api/export/packet/route.ts`, which already imports `getWorkspace` from `@/app/api/workspace/route` at `:11` — the precedent this route copies). Evidence lives in R2 under `evidence/${identity.userId}/${activityId}/${evidenceId}` (`app/api/evidence/route.ts:213`) with its row in `evidence_files` (`db/runtime.ts:254-269`: `object_key`, `original_filename`, `content_type`, `size_bytes`, `sha256`, `status` 'ready'|'deleting', `created_at` `CURRENT_TIMESTAMP`). The worker runtime has no zip library and `package.json` adds no dependency (Global Constraints), so the archive is written by a pure module: store-only, one R2 body in flight at a time, no ZIP64. Task 16's Account screen links `/api/export/all` as a plain `<a … download>` ("Download everything", copy table row 155): the gateway pipes the worker's chunked response end to end (`deploy/railway/gateway.mjs:177-178` `workerResponse.pipe(res)`), `public/sw.js:263` passes non-static requests through, and a signed-out request never reaches the worker — the gateway answers it with `sendJson(req, res, 401, { error: "unauthenticated" })` (`gateway.mjs:347`), which is what `tests/auth-gateway.test.mjs` and the live smoke pin. The zip writer, the CSV module, the two routes and the node suite below were typechecked with the repo's `tsc` (strict, `--module nodenext` for the pure module, the repo's `tsconfig.json` options with `@/` paths for the routes), linted clean with the repo's eslint, and the suite passed 4/4 against the emitted `.test-build/zipStore.js` — including `unzip -tq` "No errors detected" and `unzip -p` round trips on Info-ZIP 6.00; the `run_export` function was `bash -n`'d and dry-run against port 9 (19 checks).

**Decisions (binding):** (1) A zip, streamed, store-only (method 0): evidence files are already-compressed images and PDFs, and a store-only writer is ~200 lines with its tests. General-purpose flags `0x0808` — bit 3 (a data descriptor follows each body, so the local header is written before the CRC and size are known) and bit 11 (UTF-8 names). (2) No ZIP64: the route refuses up front with 413 `export_too_large` when `COUNT(*) + 3 > ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES` (60 000 — the 16-bit entry count) or `SUM(size_bytes) > ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES` (2 GiB — every offset stays under the 32-bit limit) over the account's ready evidence; nothing is buffered — `createZipStream` pulls one entry at a time and the route yields one `bucket.get(...).body` at a time. (3) The CSV route keeps serving its download (isolation + auth-gateway + `csvCell` intact); its query moves to `app/api/export/_activityCsv.ts` as `buildActivitiesCsv(database, userId, { includeArchived, filters })` — the archived clause is a branch INSIDE the module, so `app/api/export/route.ts` no longer contains the literal `WHERE a.user_id = ? … a.archived_at IS NULL`; the source pin over `exportRouteSource` in `tests/rendered-html.test.mjs` therefore FAILS and is deleted whole with its `readFile` binding (pins rule: deleted, never re-pointed) and its behaviour is re-asserted in `tests/isolation.test.mjs` over the built worker (an archived activity is absent from `/api/export` and present in `/api/export/all`). (4) Entry order and names are the contract Task 16 documents and the run-check reads: `workspace.json` (the `getWorkspace` payload minus `catalog` — the rule library is not the account's data), `activities.csv` (archived included, one extra final column "Archived at"), `evidence/<activityId>/<evidenceId>-<fileName>` for every `evidence_files` row with `status = 'ready'` in `activity_id, created_at, id` order (a missing R2 object is skipped and recorded), then `evidence.json` last so the manifest can say which files were included. (5) The zip's 401 is `{ error: "Sign in to continue.", code: "authentication_required" }` (copy table row 17's sentence; Task 3 gives the other five routes the same); its 500 reuses the CSV route's sentence "The activity export could not be created. Please try again." verbatim (copy table row 140 keeps it; no new prose). (6) `run_export` lives in `actions` (it creates and deletes data — never against production) and proves the whole path through the gateway: a credential, an activity, a 72-byte PNG uploaded as evidence, the activity archived, then `/api/export` omits it while the zip lists it, names the evidence file, streams its bytes, and `unzip -tq` accepts the archive; it deletes its credential at the end (the archived activity stays in the ops account, like the `actions` mode's rewritten time zone). In `all`, `run_export` runs right after `run_actions` and BEFORE Task 13's `run_account`, which logs in as the throwaway and replaces the `$C` cookie.

  ```ts
  export type ZipEntry = { name: string; body: Uint8Array | ReadableStream<Uint8Array>; lastModified?: Date };
  export const ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES = 60000;
  export const ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 2 * 1024 ** 3;      // 2147483648
  export function crc32(bytes: Uint8Array, seed = 0): number;   // seed = the crc so far: crc32(concat(a, b)) === crc32(b, crc32(a)), node:zlib's convention
  export function createZipStream(entries: AsyncIterable<ZipEntry>): ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
  //   per entry: local header 0x04034b50 (version 20, flags 0x0808, method 0, DOS time/date from lastModified in UTC or 1980-01-01 for the epoch,
  //   crc/sizes 0, name) → body chunks → data descriptor 0x08074b50 (crc, size, size); then one central header 0x02014b50 per entry
  //   (version 20/20, flags 0x0808, method 0, time/date, crc, size, size, name length, 0, 0, 0, 0, 0, local offset, name) and the end record
  //   0x06054b50 (0, 0, count, count, directory size, directory offset, 0). Little-endian throughout.
  ```

- [ ] **Step 2: Write the failing unit test for the zip writer**

Create `tests/zip-store.test.mjs` (header like `tests/instruments.test.mjs:1-8`; it imports the ESM `npm run build:lib-test` emits, never a source file — architecture-03):

```js
// `app/lib/zipStore.ts` writes the full-export archive (spec §6 Account,
// audit critic-06): CRC-32, store-only entries with data descriptors, the
// central directory and the end record — no library, no ZIP64. It is pure,
// so it is tested here against the ESM that `npm run build:lib-test` emits,
// exactly like tests/instruments.test.mjs. The CRC is cross-checked against
// node:zlib's crc32 (Node ≥ 22.2), the archive is parsed from its end record
// the way every reader does, and — when Info-ZIP unzip is on PATH — the
// bytes are handed to `unzip -tq` and `unzip -p`, the tools the run-check
// uses on the Docker container's download.
import assert from "node:assert/strict";
import { execFileSync } from "node:child_process";
import { mkdtempSync, rmSync, writeFileSync } from "node:fs";
import { tmpdir } from "node:os";
import path from "node:path";
import test from "node:test";
import zlib from "node:zlib";

import {
  ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES,
  ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES,
  crc32,
  createZipStream,
} from "../.test-build/zipStore.js";

const encode = (text) => new TextEncoder().encode(text);

const LOCAL_HEADER = 0x04034b50;
const DATA_DESCRIPTOR = 0x08074b50;
const CENTRAL_HEADER = 0x02014b50;
const END_RECORD = 0x06054b50;

async function zipBytes(entries) {
  return Buffer.from(await new Response(createZipStream(entries)).arrayBuffer());
}

// Reads the archive the way a zip tool does: the end record last, the
// central directory it points at, then each entry's local header and body.
function parseZip(bytes) {
  const end = bytes.length - 22;
  assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(end), END_RECORD, "the file ends with an end-of-central-directory record");
  const count = bytes.readUInt16LE(end + 10);
  const directorySize = bytes.readUInt32LE(end + 12);
  const directoryOffset = bytes.readUInt32LE(end + 16);
  const entries = [];
  let cursor = directoryOffset;
  for (let index = 0; index < count; index += 1) {
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor), CENTRAL_HEADER, `central header ${index}`);
    const flags = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 8);
    const method = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 10);
    const dosTime = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 12);
    const dosDate = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 14);
    const crc = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 16);
    const compressedSize = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 20);
    const size = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 24);
    const nameLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 28);
    const extraLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 30);
    const commentLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 32);
    const offset = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 42);
    const name = bytes.subarray(cursor + 46, cursor + 46 + nameLength).toString("utf8");
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(offset), LOCAL_HEADER, `${name}: local header at ${offset}`);
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt16LE(offset + 6), flags, `${name}: the local header carries the same flags`);
    const localNameLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(offset + 26);
    const localExtraLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(offset + 28);
    assert.equal(bytes.subarray(offset + 30, offset + 30 + localNameLength).toString("utf8"), name);
    const bodyStart = offset + 30 + localNameLength + localExtraLength;
    const body = bytes.subarray(bodyStart, bodyStart + size);
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(bodyStart + size), DATA_DESCRIPTOR, `${name}: a data descriptor follows the body`);
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(bodyStart + size + 4), crc, `${name}: the descriptor's crc`);
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(bodyStart + size + 8), size, `${name}: the descriptor's size`);
    entries.push({ name, flags, method, dosTime, dosDate, crc, compressedSize, size, offset, body });
    cursor += 46 + nameLength + extraLength + commentLength;
  }
  assert.equal(cursor - directoryOffset, directorySize, "the end record's directory size");
  return { count, entries };
}

function unzipAvailable() {
  try {
    execFileSync("unzip", ["-v"], { stdio: "pipe" });
    return true;
  } catch {
    return false;
  }
}

test("crc32 matches the reference value and node:zlib, including the running-seed form", () => {
  assert.equal(crc32(encode("The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog")), 0x414fa339);
  assert.equal(crc32(new Uint8Array(0)), 0);
  for (let round = 0; round < 25; round += 1) {
    const a = Buffer.from(Array.from({ length: 1 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 300) }, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 256)));
    const b = Buffer.from(Array.from({ length: 1 + Math.floor(Math.random() * 300) }, () => Math.floor(Math.random() * 256)));
    assert.equal(crc32(new Uint8Array(a)), zlib.crc32(a));
    // A body hashed chunk by chunk: the seed is the crc so far.
    assert.equal(crc32(new Uint8Array(b), crc32(new Uint8Array(a))), zlib.crc32(Buffer.concat([a, b])));
  }
});

test("the limits are the classic format's: 60 000 entries, 2 GiB", () => {
  assert.equal(ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES, 60000);
  assert.equal(ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES, 2147483648);
});

test("createZipStream writes a store-only archive: local headers, streamed bodies, data descriptors, central directory, end record", async (t) => {
  const json = encode(JSON.stringify({ user: { email: "b@example.test" }, credentials: [] }, null, 2));
  const chunks = [encode("Activity,Provider\r\n"), encode("\"Ethics course\",\"NASW\"\r\n"), encode("\"Trauma seminar\",\"\"\r\n")];
  const streamed = new ReadableStream({
    start(controller) {
      for (const chunk of chunks) controller.enqueue(chunk);
      controller.close();
    },
  });
  async function* entries() {
    yield { name: "workspace.json", body: json, lastModified: new Date("2026-09-16T14:05:09Z") };
    yield { name: "activities.csv", body: streamed };
    yield { name: "evidence/activity-1/evidence-1-café.png", body: new Uint8Array(0) };
  }
  const bytes = await zipBytes(entries());
  const { count, entries: parsed } = parseZip(bytes);
  assert.equal(count, 3);
  assert.deepEqual(
    parsed.map((entry) => entry.name),
    ["workspace.json", "activities.csv", "evidence/activity-1/evidence-1-café.png"],
  );
  for (const entry of parsed) {
    assert.equal(entry.flags, 0x0808, `${entry.name}: data descriptor + UTF-8 name flags`);
    assert.equal(entry.method, 0, `${entry.name}: stored, not deflated`);
    assert.equal(entry.compressedSize, entry.size);
    assert.equal(entry.crc, zlib.crc32(entry.body), `${entry.name}: crc of the body`);
  }
  // The first entry starts the file; each local header sits where the
  // directory says; the streamed body arrived whole.
  assert.equal(parsed[0].offset, 0);
  assert.deepEqual(parsed[0].body, Buffer.from(json));
  assert.deepEqual(parsed[1].body, Buffer.concat(chunks.map((chunk) => Buffer.from(chunk))));
  assert.equal(parsed[2].size, 0);
  assert.equal(parsed[2].crc, 0);
  // DOS stamps: 2026-09-16 14:05:09 UTC, and the epoch clamped to 1980-01-01.
  assert.equal(parsed[0].dosDate, ((2026 - 1980) << 9) | (9 << 5) | 16);
  assert.equal(parsed[0].dosTime, (14 << 11) | (5 << 5) | (9 >> 1));
  assert.equal(parsed[1].dosDate, (1 << 5) | 1);
  assert.equal(parsed[1].dosTime, 0);

  if (!unzipAvailable()) {
    t.diagnostic("unzip is not on PATH; the Info-ZIP round trip was not run");
    return;
  }
  const directory = mkdtempSync(path.join(tmpdir(), "itrack-zip-"));
  try {
    const file = path.join(directory, "export.zip");
    writeFileSync(file, bytes);
    assert.match(execFileSync("unzip", ["-tq", file]).toString(), /No errors detected/);
    assert.equal(execFileSync("unzip", ["-p", file, "workspace.json"]).toString(), Buffer.from(json).toString());
    assert.equal(
      execFileSync("unzip", ["-p", file, "activities.csv"]).toString(),
      Buffer.concat(chunks.map((chunk) => Buffer.from(chunk))).toString(),
    );
  } finally {
    rmSync(directory, { recursive: true, force: true });
  }
});

test("an empty iterable is a valid archive with zero entries", async () => {
  const bytes = await zipBytes((async function* () {})());
  assert.equal(bytes.length, 22);
  const { count } = parseZip(bytes);
  assert.equal(count, 0);
  assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(12), 0, "directory size");
  assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(16), 0, "directory offset");
});
```

(`unzip -p` is asked for the two ASCII names on purpose: Apple's Info-ZIP build mangles a non-ASCII name given on its command line, while the archive itself — `unzip -tq` on all three entries, including the `café` one — is accepted. An empty archive is deliberately not handed to `unzip -tq`: Info-ZIP answers "zipfile is empty" with exit 1, a warning, not a defect.)

Create `app/lib/zipStore.ts` (no imports at all — nothing React, DOM-only-through-lib, or D1; `ReadableStream`, `DataView` and `TextEncoder` come from the default lib the standalone `tsc` uses):

```ts
// A store-only ZIP writer for the full data export (spec §6 Account, audit
// critic-06). The worker runtime has no zip library and package.json adds no
// dependency, so the archive is written here: method 0 (stored, no
// compression — the evidence files are already compressed images and PDFs),
// general-purpose flags 0x0808 (bit 3: a data descriptor follows each body,
// so the local header is written before the CRC and size are known and one
// R2 object streams through at a time; bit 11: UTF-8 names), then the
// central directory and the end record. No ZIP64: the route refuses an
// export above ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES or ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES up front (413).
//
// Pure: no React, DOM-only-through-lib or D1 import — `npm run build:lib-test`
// compiles it standalone for tests/zip-store.test.mjs.

export type ZipEntry = {
  name: string;
  body: Uint8Array | ReadableStream<Uint8Array>;
  lastModified?: Date;
};

// Two hard limits of the classic (non-ZIP64) format: 32-bit sizes/offsets and
// a 16-bit entry count. 2 GiB keeps every offset well under 4 GiB, and 60 000
// entries stays under 65 535 with the three fixed entries.
export const ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES = 60000;
export const ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES = 2 * 1024 ** 3;

const CRC_TABLE = (() => {
  const table = new Uint32Array(256);
  for (let n = 0; n < 256; n += 1) {
    let c = n;
    for (let k = 0; k < 8; k += 1) {
      c = c & 1 ? 0xedb88320 ^ (c >>> 1) : c >>> 1;
    }
    table[n] = c >>> 0;
  }
  return table;
})();

// CRC-32 (IEEE 802.3, the ZIP polynomial). `seed` is the CRC of the bytes
// already processed, so a body can be hashed chunk by chunk:
// crc32(concat(a, b)) === crc32(b, crc32(a)) — the same convention as
// node:zlib's crc32(data, value).
export function crc32(bytes: Uint8Array, seed = 0): number {
  let c = (seed ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
  for (let i = 0; i < bytes.length; i += 1) {
    c = CRC_TABLE[(c ^ bytes[i]) & 0xff] ^ (c >>> 8);
  }
  return (c ^ 0xffffffff) >>> 0;
}

const LOCAL_HEADER_SIGNATURE = 0x04034b50;
const DATA_DESCRIPTOR_SIGNATURE = 0x08074b50;
const CENTRAL_HEADER_SIGNATURE = 0x02014b50;
const END_RECORD_SIGNATURE = 0x06054b50;
const GENERAL_PURPOSE_FLAGS = 0x0808;
const VERSION_2_0 = 20;
const METHOD_STORED = 0;

type DosStamp = { dosDate: number; dosTime: number };

type EntryRecord = DosStamp & {
  name: Uint8Array;
  crc: number;
  size: number;
  offset: number;
};

const encoder = new TextEncoder();

// MS-DOS date/time (UTC): years before 1980 clamp to 1980-01-01 00:00:00 (the
// format cannot represent the epoch), years after 2107 clamp likewise.
function dosStamp(date: Date | undefined): DosStamp {
  const value = date ?? new Date(0);
  const year = value.getUTCFullYear();
  if (year < 1980 || year > 2107 || Number.isNaN(year)) {
    const clampedYear = year > 2107 ? 2107 : 1980;
    return { dosDate: ((clampedYear - 1980) << 9) | (1 << 5) | 1, dosTime: 0 };
  }
  return {
    dosDate:
      ((year - 1980) << 9) | ((value.getUTCMonth() + 1) << 5) | value.getUTCDate(),
    dosTime:
      (value.getUTCHours() << 11) |
      (value.getUTCMinutes() << 5) |
      (value.getUTCSeconds() >> 1),
  };
}

function localHeader(name: Uint8Array, stamp: DosStamp): Uint8Array {
  const buffer = new Uint8Array(30 + name.length);
  const view = new DataView(buffer.buffer);
  view.setUint32(0, LOCAL_HEADER_SIGNATURE, true);
  view.setUint16(4, VERSION_2_0, true);
  view.setUint16(6, GENERAL_PURPOSE_FLAGS, true);
  view.setUint16(8, METHOD_STORED, true);
  view.setUint16(10, stamp.dosTime, true);
  view.setUint16(12, stamp.dosDate, true);
  view.setUint32(14, 0, true); // crc — in the data descriptor
  view.setUint32(18, 0, true); // compressed size — in the data descriptor
  view.setUint32(22, 0, true); // uncompressed size — in the data descriptor
  view.setUint16(26, name.length, true);
  view.setUint16(28, 0, true); // extra field length
  buffer.set(name, 30);
  return buffer;
}

function dataDescriptor(crc: number, size: number): Uint8Array {
  const buffer = new Uint8Array(16);
  const view = new DataView(buffer.buffer);
  view.setUint32(0, DATA_DESCRIPTOR_SIGNATURE, true);
  view.setUint32(4, crc, true);
  view.setUint32(8, size, true);
  view.setUint32(12, size, true);
  return buffer;
}

function centralHeader(record: EntryRecord): Uint8Array {
  const buffer = new Uint8Array(46 + record.name.length);
  const view = new DataView(buffer.buffer);
  view.setUint32(0, CENTRAL_HEADER_SIGNATURE, true);
  view.setUint16(4, VERSION_2_0, true); // version made by
  view.setUint16(6, VERSION_2_0, true); // version needed to extract
  view.setUint16(8, GENERAL_PURPOSE_FLAGS, true);
  view.setUint16(10, METHOD_STORED, true);
  view.setUint16(12, record.dosTime, true);
  view.setUint16(14, record.dosDate, true);
  view.setUint32(16, record.crc, true);
  view.setUint32(20, record.size, true);
  view.setUint32(24, record.size, true);
  view.setUint16(28, record.name.length, true);
  view.setUint16(30, 0, true); // extra field length
  view.setUint16(32, 0, true); // comment length
  view.setUint16(34, 0, true); // disk number start
  view.setUint16(36, 0, true); // internal attributes
  view.setUint32(38, 0, true); // external attributes
  view.setUint32(42, record.offset, true);
  buffer.set(record.name, 46);
  return buffer;
}

function endRecord(count: number, directorySize: number, directoryOffset: number): Uint8Array {
  const buffer = new Uint8Array(22);
  const view = new DataView(buffer.buffer);
  view.setUint32(0, END_RECORD_SIGNATURE, true);
  view.setUint16(4, 0, true); // this disk
  view.setUint16(6, 0, true); // disk with the central directory
  view.setUint16(8, count, true);
  view.setUint16(10, count, true);
  view.setUint32(12, directorySize, true);
  view.setUint32(16, directoryOffset, true);
  view.setUint16(20, 0, true); // comment length
  return buffer;
}

// One body as a sequence of non-empty chunks; a stream is read with a reader
// (not `for await`) so the same code runs under workerd, node and the DOM lib.
async function* bodyChunks(
  body: Uint8Array | ReadableStream<Uint8Array>,
): AsyncGenerator<Uint8Array> {
  if (body instanceof Uint8Array) {
    if (body.length > 0) yield body;
    return;
  }
  const reader = body.getReader();
  try {
    for (;;) {
      const { done, value } = await reader.read();
      if (done) return;
      if (value && value.length > 0) yield value;
    }
  } finally {
    reader.releaseLock();
  }
}

async function* zipChunks(entries: AsyncIterable<ZipEntry>): AsyncGenerator<Uint8Array> {
  const records: EntryRecord[] = [];
  let offset = 0;
  const emit = (chunk: Uint8Array) => {
    offset += chunk.length;
    return chunk;
  };
  for await (const entry of entries) {
    const name = encoder.encode(entry.name);
    const stamp = dosStamp(entry.lastModified);
    const start = offset;
    yield emit(localHeader(name, stamp));
    let crc = 0;
    let size = 0;
    for await (const chunk of bodyChunks(entry.body)) {
      crc = crc32(chunk, crc);
      size += chunk.length;
      yield emit(chunk);
    }
    yield emit(dataDescriptor(crc, size));
    records.push({ name, crc, size, offset: start, ...stamp });
  }
  const directoryOffset = offset;
  let directorySize = 0;
  for (const record of records) {
    const header = centralHeader(record);
    directorySize += header.length;
    yield emit(header);
  }
  yield emit(endRecord(records.length, directorySize, directoryOffset));
}

// The archive as a byte stream: entries are pulled one at a time, so at most
// one body is in flight and nothing is buffered beyond the current chunk.
export function createZipStream(entries: AsyncIterable<ZipEntry>): ReadableStream<Uint8Array> {
  const chunks = zipChunks(entries);
  return new ReadableStream<Uint8Array>({
    async pull(controller) {
      try {
        const { done, value } = await chunks.next();
        if (done) controller.close();
        else controller.enqueue(value);
      } catch (error) {
        controller.error(error);
      }
    },
    async cancel() {
      await chunks.return(undefined);
    },
  });
}
```

The underscore file beside the route follows `app/api/evidence/_shared.ts` (a module, never a route). It holds `csvCell` (c6b1fe4 `app/api/export/route.ts:21-25`), the query (`:43-84`) and the assembly (`:86-112`) as Task 4 left them — Task 4 appended the four filter clauses after `AND a.archived_at IS NULL`, the `a.format`/`a.notes` columns, the "Format"/"Notes" header cells and a `FORMAT_LABELS` map inside `route.ts` — with two additions of this task's own: `includeArchived` (drops the archived clause and appends an "Archived at" column) and the `filters` parameter (the clauses are applied only when a filter is set, so `/api/export` without a query stays byte-identical to Task 4's file). Create the file with exactly this content — if Task 4's clause text in `route.ts` differs from the four `where +=` fragments below in anything but whitespace, keep Task 4's text (this is a move; the behaviour its four isolation subtests pin is the contract):

```ts
// The activities CSV, shared by GET /api/export (the download: current
// activities, optionally filtered by credential, date range and tag) and
// GET /api/export/all (the zip: archived activities included, with an
// "Archived at" column). The query, `csvCell` and the assembly moved here
// from app/api/export/route.ts in Wave 4 Task 15; the filters and the
// Format/Notes columns are Task 4's. `csvCell`'s formula-injection guard is
// the one the audit called correct (critic-06) — keep it.

export type ActivityCsvFilters = {
  credentialId: string | null;
  from: string | null;
  to: string | null;
  tag: string | null;
};

export const NO_ACTIVITY_CSV_FILTERS: ActivityCsvFilters = {
  credentialId: null,
  from: null,
  to: null,
  tag: null,
};

// The stored `activities.format` values and the words the CSV prints for
// them (the Log activity sheet's Format options, copy table row 111).
export const FORMAT_LABELS: Record<string, string> = {
  live_course: "Live course",
  live_webinar: "Live webinar",
  self_study: "On-demand or self-study",
  conference: "Conference",
  other: "Other",
};

type ActivityCsvRow = {
  title: string;
  provider: string;
  completionDate: string;
  totalUnits: number;
  evidenceStatus: string;
  evidenceReference: string | null;
  credentialName: string | null;
  jurisdiction: string | null;
  requirementNames: string | null;
  allocatedUnits: number;
  format: string | null;
  notes: string | null;
  archivedAt: string | null;
};

export function csvCell(value: unknown): string {
  let text = value === null || value === undefined ? "" : String(value);
  if (/^[=+\-@\t\r]/.test(text)) text = `'${text}`;
  return `"${text.replace(/"/g, '""')}"`;
}

const CSV_HEADER = [
  "Activity",
  "Provider",
  "Completion date",
  "Activity units",
  "Evidence status",
  "Evidence reference",
  "Credential",
  "Jurisdiction",
  "Requirement tags",
  "Allocated units",
  "Format",
  "Notes",
];

// One row per allocation (LEFT JOIN activity_allocations): an activity applied
// to two credentials is listed twice. Every filter therefore gates the
// ACTIVITY (an EXISTS over its allocations), never the joined row, so the
// file still lists every allocation of a matching activity.
export async function buildActivitiesCsv(
  database: D1Database,
  userId: string,
  options: { includeArchived: boolean; filters?: ActivityCsvFilters },
): Promise<string> {
  const filters = options.filters ?? NO_ACTIVITY_CSV_FILTERS;
  const bindings: unknown[] = [userId];
  let where = "WHERE a.user_id = ?";
  if (!options.includeArchived) where += "\n          AND a.archived_at IS NULL";
  if (filters.from) {
    where += "\n          AND a.completion_date >= ?";
    bindings.push(filters.from);
  }
  if (filters.to) {
    where += "\n          AND a.completion_date <= ?";
    bindings.push(filters.to);
  }
  if (filters.credentialId) {
    where += `
          AND EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM activity_allocations filtered
            JOIN credentials filtered_credential
              ON filtered_credential.id = filtered.credential_id
              AND filtered_credential.user_id = a.user_id
            WHERE filtered.activity_id = a.id
              AND filtered_credential.id = ?
          )`;
    bindings.push(filters.credentialId);
  }
  if (filters.tag) {
    where += `
          AND EXISTS (
            SELECT 1
            FROM activity_allocations tagged_allocation
            LEFT JOIN activity_requirement_matches tagged_match
              ON tagged_match.allocation_id = tagged_allocation.id
            LEFT JOIN credential_requirements tagged_requirement
              ON tagged_requirement.id = COALESCE(tagged_match.requirement_id, tagged_allocation.requirement_id)
            WHERE tagged_allocation.activity_id = a.id
              AND tagged_requirement.name = ?
          )`;
    bindings.push(filters.tag);
  }

  const result = await database
    .prepare(
      `SELECT
          a.title,
          a.provider,
          a.completion_date AS completionDate,
          a.total_units AS totalUnits,
          a.evidence_status AS evidenceStatus,
          a.evidence_reference AS evidenceReference,
          c.credential_name AS credentialName,
          c.jurisdiction,
          COALESCE(
            (
              SELECT GROUP_CONCAT(tagged.name, ' | ')
              FROM (
                SELECT DISTINCT matched_requirement.name
                FROM activity_requirement_matches match
                JOIN credential_requirements matched_requirement
                  ON matched_requirement.id = match.requirement_id
                  AND matched_requirement.credential_id = alloc.credential_id
                WHERE match.allocation_id = alloc.id
                ORDER BY matched_requirement.sort_order, matched_requirement.name
              ) tagged
            ),
            req.name
          ) AS requirementNames,
          CASE
            WHEN c.id IS NULL THEN 0
            ELSE COALESCE(alloc.allocated_units, 0)
          END AS allocatedUnits,
          a.format,
          a.notes,
          a.archived_at AS archivedAt
        FROM activities a
        LEFT JOIN activity_allocations alloc ON alloc.activity_id = a.id
        LEFT JOIN credentials c
          ON c.id = alloc.credential_id AND c.user_id = a.user_id
        LEFT JOIN credential_requirements req
          ON req.id = alloc.requirement_id AND req.credential_id = c.id
        ${where}
        ORDER BY a.completion_date DESC, a.created_at DESC`,
    )
    .bind(...bindings)
    .all<ActivityCsvRow>();

  const header = options.includeArchived
    ? [...CSV_HEADER, "Archived at"]
    : CSV_HEADER;
  const rows = result.results.map((row) => {
    const cells: unknown[] = [
      row.title,
      row.provider,
      row.completionDate,
      Number(row.totalUnits),
      row.evidenceStatus,
      row.evidenceReference,
      row.credentialName,
      row.jurisdiction,
      row.requirementNames,
      Number(row.allocatedUnits),
      row.format ? (FORMAT_LABELS[row.format] ?? row.format) : "",
      row.notes,
    ];
    if (options.includeArchived) cells.push(row.archivedAt);
    return cells;
  });
  return `\uFEFF${[header, ...rows]
    .map((row) => row.map(csvCell).join(","))
    .join("\r\n")}\r\n`;
}
```

`app/api/export/route.ts` at c6b1fe4 is 144 lines: imports `:1-4`, `type ExportRow` `:8-19`, `csvCell` `:21-25`, and `GET` `:27-144` with the query `:43-84`, the header/rows/`csv` assembly `:86-112`, the zone lookup `:113-123`, the CSV response `:125-132` and the 500 `:133-143`. Task 4 grew it (the query-string parsing with the 400 `invalid_date`, the four clauses, the two columns, `FORMAT_LABELS`) and Task 3 rewrote its 401 sentence to "Sign in to continue.". Replace the whole file with the following — the same 401/400/500 bodies, the same filename logic, the query and the CSV assembly gone (they are the module's now); keep Task 4's query-string parsing exactly as it reads in the file if its `filtersFromRequest` differs from this one in a detail such as the `slice` caps (the contract is the same: each parameter optional, a malformed `from`/`to` is the one 400):

```ts
import { getD1 } from "@/db";
import { resolveRequestIdentity } from "@/db/identity";
import { ensureUser, initializeDatabase } from "@/db/runtime";
import { ISO_DATE_PATTERN, isValidTimeZone, todayLocal } from "../../lib/dates";
import { type ActivityCsvFilters, buildActivitiesCsv } from "./_activityCsv";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

// ?credentialId=&from=&to=&tag= — each optional (Task 4). A malformed date is
// the one refusal; the ids and names are bounded to the columns' widths.
function filtersFromRequest(request: Request): ActivityCsvFilters | null {
  const query = new URL(request.url).searchParams;
  const from = query.get("from") || null;
  const to = query.get("to") || null;
  if ((from && !ISO_DATE_PATTERN.test(from)) || (to && !ISO_DATE_PATTERN.test(to))) {
    return null;
  }
  return {
    credentialId: query.get("credentialId")?.slice(0, 160) || null,
    from,
    to,
    tag: query.get("tag")?.slice(0, 180) || null,
  };
}

export async function GET(request: Request) {
  try {
    const identity = await resolveRequestIdentity(request);
    if (!identity) {
      return Response.json(
        {
          error: "Sign in to continue.",
          code: "authentication_required",
        },
        { status: 401, headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
      );
    }

    const filters = filtersFromRequest(request);
    if (!filters) {
      return Response.json(
        { error: "Choose the dates as YYYY-MM-DD.", code: "invalid_date" },
        { status: 400, headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
      );
    }

    const database = getD1();
    await initializeDatabase(database);
    await ensureUser(database, identity);
    const csv = await buildActivitiesCsv(database, identity.userId, {
      includeArchived: false,
      filters,
    });
    // The download's date is the user's date, not the worker's UTC date.
    const preference = await database
      .prepare(
        `SELECT time_zone AS timeZone
         FROM reminder_preferences
         WHERE user_id = ?`,
      )
      .bind(identity.userId)
      .first<{ timeZone: string }>();
    const zone = preference?.timeZone ?? "UTC";
    const today = todayLocal(isValidTimeZone(zone) ? zone : "UTC");

    return new Response(csv, {
      headers: {
        "Cache-Control": "no-store",
        "Content-Disposition": `attachment; filename="ceu-activities-${today}.csv"`,
        "Content-Type": "text/csv; charset=utf-8",
        "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
      },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unexpected error";
    console.error("CEU export error", message);
    return Response.json(
      {
        error: "The activity export could not be created. Please try again.",
        code: "internal_error",
      },
      { status: 500, headers: { "Cache-Control": "no-store" } },
    );
  }
}
```

```ts
import { getD1, getEvidenceBucket } from "@/db";
import { resolveRequestIdentity } from "@/db/identity";
import { ensureUser, initializeDatabase } from "@/db/runtime";
import { getWorkspace } from "@/app/api/workspace/route";
import { type DetectedFile, sanitizeFilename } from "@/app/api/evidence/_shared";
import {
  type ZipEntry,
  ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES,
  ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES,
  createZipStream,
} from "@/app/lib/zipStore";
import { isValidTimeZone, todayLocal } from "../../../lib/dates";
import { buildActivitiesCsv } from "../_activityCsv";

export const dynamic = "force-dynamic";

// GET /api/export/all — everything iTrack holds for the account as one
// streamed, store-only zip (spec §6 Account "data export", audit critic-06):
//   workspace.json    the GET /api/workspace payload minus the rule catalog
//   activities.csv    every activity, archived included ("Archived at" column)
//   evidence/<activityId>/<evidenceId>-<fileName>   every ready evidence file,
//                     streamed from R2 one object at a time
//   evidence.json     the manifest, last, so it can say which files were found
// Signed-out requests never reach this route in production — the gateway
// answers them with its JSON 401 first (deploy/railway/gateway.mjs); the 401
// below is what tests see. Nothing is buffered: the zip writer pulls one
// entry at a time, so a 2 GiB export costs the worker one chunk of memory.

const FIXED_ENTRIES = 3; // workspace.json, activities.csv, evidence.json
const NO_STORE = { "Cache-Control": "no-store" };

type EvidenceExportRow = {
  id: string;
  activityId: string;
  activityTitle: string;
  objectKey: string;
  fileName: string;
  contentType: string;
  sizeBytes: number;
  sha256: string;
  createdAt: string;
};

type EvidenceManifestEntry = {
  id: string;
  activityId: string;
  activityTitle: string;
  fileName: string;
  contentType: string;
  sizeBytes: number;
  sha256: string;
  createdAt: string;
  path: string;
  included: boolean;
};

// Every stored content type passed detectFileType at upload, so the map is
// total in practice; the fallback keeps an unexpected value from breaking the
// download (the leaf of the stored name, path separators removed).
const DETECTED_BY_TYPE: Record<DetectedFile["contentType"], DetectedFile> = {
  "application/pdf": { contentType: "application/pdf", extension: "pdf" },
  "image/jpeg": { contentType: "image/jpeg", extension: "jpg" },
  "image/png": { contentType: "image/png", extension: "png" },
  "image/webp": { contentType: "image/webp", extension: "webp" },
};

function isDetectedType(value: string): value is DetectedFile["contentType"] {
  return value in DETECTED_BY_TYPE;
}

function entryFileName(fileName: string, contentType: string): string {
  if (isDetectedType(contentType)) {
    return sanitizeFilename(fileName, DETECTED_BY_TYPE[contentType]);
  }
  return fileName.split(/[\\/]/).pop()?.trim() || "evidence";
}

// SQLite's CURRENT_TIMESTAMP is "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" in UTC; an ISO string
// parses as-is. An unparseable value leaves the entry on the DOS epoch.
function parseStoredTimestamp(value: string): Date | undefined {
  const iso = /^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} \d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2}$/.test(value)
    ? `${value.replace(" ", "T")}Z`
    : value;
  const parsed = Date.parse(iso);
  return Number.isNaN(parsed) ? undefined : new Date(parsed);
}

function jsonError(error: string, code: string, status: number) {
  return Response.json({ error, code }, { status, headers: NO_STORE });
}

export async function GET(request: Request) {
  try {
    const identity = await resolveRequestIdentity(request);
    if (!identity) {
      return jsonError("Sign in to continue.", "authentication_required", 401);
    }

    const database = getD1();
    const bucket = getEvidenceBucket();
    await initializeDatabase(database);
    await ensureUser(database, identity);

    // The classic zip format stops at 32-bit sizes and a 16-bit entry count;
    // refuse up front rather than emit an archive no tool can open.
    const totals = await database
      .prepare(
        `SELECT COUNT(*) AS files, COALESCE(SUM(size_bytes), 0) AS bytes
         FROM evidence_files
         WHERE user_id = ? AND status = 'ready'`,
      )
      .bind(identity.userId)
      .first<{ files: number; bytes: number }>();
    const fileCount = Number(totals?.files ?? 0);
    const totalBytes = Number(totals?.bytes ?? 0);
    if (fileCount + FIXED_ENTRIES > ZIP_MAX_ENTRIES || totalBytes > ZIP_MAX_TOTAL_BYTES) {
      return jsonError(
        "This export is too large to build in one file. Delete evidence files you no longer need, or contact support@itrackceu.com.",
        "export_too_large",
        413,
      );
    }

    const workspace = await getWorkspace(database, identity);
    const csv = await buildActivitiesCsv(database, identity.userId, {
      includeArchived: true,
    });
    const evidenceRows = (
      await database
        .prepare(
          `SELECT
             e.id,
             e.activity_id AS activityId,
             a.title AS activityTitle,
             e.object_key AS objectKey,
             e.original_filename AS fileName,
             e.content_type AS contentType,
             e.size_bytes AS sizeBytes,
             e.sha256,
             e.created_at AS createdAt
           FROM evidence_files e
           JOIN activities a ON a.id = e.activity_id AND a.user_id = e.user_id
           WHERE e.user_id = ? AND e.status = 'ready'
           ORDER BY e.activity_id, e.created_at, e.id`,
        )
        .bind(identity.userId)
        .all<EvidenceExportRow>()
    ).results;

    // The download's date is the user's date (the stored reminder zone), not
    // the worker's UTC date — the same rule as the CSV's filename.
    const zone = workspace.reminderPreferences.timeZone;
    const today = todayLocal(isValidTimeZone(zone) ? zone : "UTC");

    // The catalog is the rule library, not the account's data; an undefined
    // property is dropped by JSON.stringify.
    const workspaceExport = { ...workspace, catalog: undefined };
    const encoder = new TextEncoder();
    const manifest: EvidenceManifestEntry[] = [];

    async function* entries(): AsyncGenerator<ZipEntry> {
      yield {
        name: "workspace.json",
        body: encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(workspaceExport, null, 2)),
      };
      yield { name: "activities.csv", body: encoder.encode(csv) };
      try {
        for (const row of evidenceRows) {
          const object = await bucket.get(row.objectKey);
          const path = `evidence/${row.activityId}/${row.id}-${entryFileName(row.fileName, row.contentType)}`;
          manifest.push({
            id: row.id,
            activityId: row.activityId,
            activityTitle: row.activityTitle,
            fileName: row.fileName,
            contentType: row.contentType,
            sizeBytes: Number(row.sizeBytes),
            sha256: row.sha256,
            createdAt: row.createdAt,
            path,
            included: Boolean(object),
          });
          if (object) {
            yield {
              name: path,
              body: object.body,
              lastModified: parseStoredTimestamp(row.createdAt),
            };
          }
        }
      } catch (error) {
        // After the first byte the response cannot change status; the stream
        // errors, the browser reports a failed download, and the log says why.
        const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unexpected error";
        console.error("Full export stream error", message);
        throw error;
      }
      yield {
        name: "evidence.json",
        body: encoder.encode(JSON.stringify(manifest, null, 2)),
      };
    }

    return new Response(createZipStream(entries()), {
      headers: {
        "Cache-Control": "no-store",
        "Content-Disposition": `attachment; filename="itrack-export-${today}.zip"`,
        "Content-Type": "application/zip",
        "Cross-Origin-Resource-Policy": "same-origin",
        "X-Content-Type-Options": "nosniff",
      },
    });
  } catch (error) {
    const message = error instanceof Error ? error.message : "Unexpected error";
    console.error("Full export error", message);
    return jsonError(
      "The activity export could not be created. Please try again.",
      "internal_error",
      500,
    );
  }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 10: The two isolation subtests over the built worker (`tests/isolation.test.mjs`)**

The zip is the one export that carries EVERYTHING an identity owns, so it is the export most worth the two-identity tripwire (spec §4: `/api/export/*` refuses cross-identity data). First a reader, added at module scope directly after `function base64url(bytes) { … }` (c6b1fe4 `:232-234`) — the same central-directory walk `tests/zip-store.test.mjs` proves, reduced to a name → body map:

```js
// Reads a store-only archive from its end record: entry name → body, in
// directory order. tests/zip-store.test.mjs proves the writer; this proves
// what the route put in.
function zipEntries(bytes) {
  const end = bytes.length - 22;
  assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(end), 0x06054b50, "end-of-central-directory record");
  const count = bytes.readUInt16LE(end + 10);
  let cursor = bytes.readUInt32LE(end + 16);
  const entries = new Map();
  for (let index = 0; index < count; index += 1) {
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor), 0x02014b50, `central header ${index}`);
    const size = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 24);
    const nameLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 28);
    const extraLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 30);
    const commentLength = bytes.readUInt16LE(cursor + 32);
    const offset = bytes.readUInt32LE(cursor + 42);
    const name = bytes.subarray(cursor + 46, cursor + 46 + nameLength).toString("utf8");
    assert.equal(bytes.readUInt32LE(offset), 0x04034b50, `${name}: local header`);
    const bodyStart = offset + 30 + bytes.readUInt16LE(offset + 26) + bytes.readUInt16LE(offset + 28);
    entries.set(name, bytes.subarray(bodyStart, bodyStart + size));
    cursor += 46 + nameLength + extraLength + commentLength;
  }
  return entries;
}
```

```bash
run_export() { # Wave 4 Task 15: GET /api/export/all streams the account's zip through the gateway
  local r AID EID REV
  r=$(post createCredential '{"credentialName":"Wave 4 export","profession":"Counseling","jurisdiction":"Rhode Island","issuer":"E2E board","totalRequired":10,"unitLabel":"hours","cycleStart":"2026-01-01","deadline":"2027-12-31","categories":[{"name":"General","requiredUnits":10}]}')
  check 'export: createCredential 200' '^200 \{"ok":true,"action":"createCredential","id":"' "$r"

  r=$(post addActivity "{\"title\":\"Wave 4 export course\",\"provider\":\"E2E provider\",\"completionDate\":\"2026-06-02\",\"totalUnits\":1,\"allocatedUnits\":1,\"credentialId\":\"$ID\"}")
  check 'export: addActivity 200' '^200 \{"ok":true,"action":"addActivity","id":"' "$r"

  printf '\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n' > "$TMP/check.png"; head -c 64 /dev/zero >> "$TMP/check.png"

  check 'export: archiveActivity 200' '^200 \{"ok":true,"action":"archiveActivity"' "$r"
```

### Task 16: Account screen: Profile + name form, Email/Password/Danger-zone sheets on the routes, Reminders inline (zone offer, time zone, lead days, phone alerts, check-in time, quiet hours; reminders modal deleted), Install, Your data, Momentum collapsed, boundary line, Sign out; account.css rewritten; account.spec + account-data-ops.spec

**Rationale:** spec §6 Account names nine things the screen must carry — display name, email change (re-verify), password change, reminders (time zone auto-detected, quiet hours), install instructions, data export, Momentum, delete account, sign out — and four findings point at the screen that exists today: app-ux-M-02 (no account self-service anywhere: `AuthStore` has no rename/change-password/delete and the only account control is the logout form at `app/ITrackApp.tsx:9456-9460`), app-ux-13 (gamification split across Home's `section.coach-card.progression-card` at `:7024-7200` and Account's "Meaningful momentum" / "Weekly rhythm" cards at `:9463-9605` — it moves to one collapsed Momentum section here, and Task 8 already deleted the Home block), app-ux-14 (the reminders modal at `:5772-5917` and the Account card at `:9606-9637` still say "on Today" — `:5786`, `:9618`), app-ux-15 (`pushDeviceState === "unconfigured"` prints "Phone alerts are being prepared." at `:9366` / `:9380` — the whole push control set is hidden in that state instead) and critic-06 (the only export is the activities CSV; Task 15's `GET /api/export/all` gets its link here). Today the screen is `AccountView` at `app/ITrackApp.tsx:9341-9804` (fifteen props, six legacy cards in `.account-grid`, the header "A renewal system that stays yours." at `:9438-9442`), the reminder preferences live in a root-level `Modal title="Due-date check-ins"` (`:5772-5917`, posted by `handleReminderPreferences` `:3291-3311` through the global `error` string), the Wave 2 zone offer is root state (`:1418-1440`, `adoptDeviceTimeZone`/`dismissZoneOffer` `:3320-3349`, rendered as `.zone-banner` above every tab at `:3969-3994`), and `app/styles/account.css` (510 lines) is entirely on legacy aliases (22 alias names — `--tint-bright`, `--ink-tint`, `--font-ui`, `--wash-tint`, `--edge-tint`, `--white`, `--ring-accent`, `--accent-control` …) and one of the seven files `tests/contrast-audit.test.mjs:25-33` still allows to reference them. Task 5 moved the modal into `app/screens/modals/RemindersModal.tsx` (a gated `{workspace && remindersOpen ? (` site in `ModalsHost`), the zone offer into `app/screens/parts/Banners.tsx`, the push machine into `app/screens/hooks/usePushDevice.ts` and the calendar hand-off into `useCalendarActions.ts`; Task 4 added `quietHoursStart`/`quietHoursEnd` to `reminderPreferences` and to `updateReminderPreferences`; Tasks 12–15 landed the gateway routes (`GET /account`, `POST /account/profile|password|email|email/cancel|delete`) and the zip export. This task is the screen: `app/screens/Account.tsx` on the primitives, `account.css` on first-class tokens, the reminders modal deleted, and `profile.spec.ts` replaced by `account.spec.ts` (demo read-only + a fresh identity) and `account-data-ops.spec.ts` (every `/account/*` request intercepted — the dev server has no gateway).

**Decisions.** (1) The gateway routes are JSON (Tasks 12–14): the sheets and the name form fetch them through `useAccountApi`, which maps the gateway's codes to the copy table's sentences and never renders `error`; a 401 ends the session exactly as `/api/workspace` does, through a `sessionEnded()` this task adds to the store's public value (the memoised `handleSessionEnded`, spelling untouched). Sign-out stays a POST form (`<form method="post" action="/auth/logout">`, `method` before `action` — `tests/app-source-guards.test.mjs:100-107`). (2) The reminders modal is deleted; Reminders is an inline `<form>` under `id="reminders"` with its own `ErrorSummary` "Reminders were not saved". The store's `run()` hands back `copy` + `code`; the section switches on `code` for the field id and the copy-table sentence only (`invalid_time_zone` → Time zone, `invalid_push_hour` → Check-in time, `push_subscription_required` → Send phone alerts, `invalid_quiet_hours` → Quiet from), and any other code shows `copy.next`. (3) The zone offer renders inline in Reminders with the copy table's strings — the button label "Use {zone}" is the one `local-dates.spec.ts` clicks on Home — and its state moves from `Banners.tsx` into the store (`zoneSuggestion`, `dismissZoneOffer`); `Banners` keeps rendering the legacy `.zone-banner` on every tab except `profile`, so the label never appears twice on one page. (4) The dev server has no VAPID keys, so on the desktop projects `pushDeviceState` resolves to `"unconfigured"`; the copy table's Reminders row therefore splits into two groups: the schedule fields (Time zone, lead days, Show check-ins on Home, Check-in time, Quiet from / Quiet until) always render — they are stored preferences the scheduler honours wherever push is configured — and the phone-alert controls (the "Send phone alerts" switch, the device block, its buttons and the connected-device count) are hidden whole while `pushDeviceState === "unconfigured"` (app-ux-15). A save then sends the stored `pushEnabled`, never a `true` the server would 409. (5) The install-help sheet stays a `ModalsHost` site (`{installHelpOpen ? (`); the Install section's button calls `usePushDevice().install()`, which prompts natively or opens that sheet. `usePushDevice(store)` is called once, in `Account`, and handed to `ReminderSettings` as a prop — two instances would register two `beforeinstallprompt` listeners. (6) Momentum is `<details className="account-momentum" id="account-momentum">`, closed by default, nothing persisted; the level bar and every quest bar are `CreditBar`s (`role="progressbar"`, the one sanctioned fill moment; an uncapped bar reads complete at 100 %) — the legacy `.level-track`/`.quest-track` rule with its 180 ms literal dies with them. (7) The display-name form posts `/account/profile` (Task 12); on success the store `reload()`s so `workspace.user.displayName` — mirrored by `ensureUser` on that request — updates. (8) `?notice=email-changed` (Task 14's 303 after `/verify`) is read once by the provider in a deferred mount effect, stored as `accountNotice`, scrubbed with `nav.scrubQuery()`; `Account` shows the toast "Your email is now {email}." from a deferred mount effect and clears it. (9) After a successful delete the sheet calls `window.location.assign("/")` (the response already cleared the cookie; `location.assign` is not a history write — the guard bans `pushState`/`replaceState`/`history.back`/`history.go`). (10) Copy: every string below is copy-table section G verbatim; the Reminders device block keeps the heading/body sentences of `app/ITrackApp.tsx:9393-9428` minus the "unconfigured" pair, and "Send test alert" becomes "Send a test". The old status strip ("Private by default", "This device is connected", "Updating this device…") and the "A careful boundary" list are not carried — the boundary is one footer line. (11) "Resend" re-opens the Change-email sheet prefilled with the pending address (the route needs the password again — Task 14: resend is the same POST); "Cancel change" posts `/account/email/cancel` and toasts "The email change was cancelled.". (12) Every `getByLabel` in the specs passes `{ exact: true }`: "Time zone" would otherwise also match the Select's search input "Search time zones", and "New password" would match "Confirm new password".

```ts
// Replaces tests/e2e/profile.spec.ts. spec §6 Account: one functional H1,

test("Account has its sections in order and Momentum is collapsed", async ({ page, app }) => {
  await app.goto("/profile");
  await expect(page).toHaveTitle("Account · iTrack");
  await expect(app.tab("Account")).toHaveAttribute("aria-current", "page");
  await expect(page.getByRole("heading", { level: 1, name: "Your account" })).toBeVisible();
  await expect(page.getByRole("main").getByRole("heading", { level: 2 })).toHaveText([

    "Reminders",
    "Install",

  ]);

  await expect(momentum).toHaveCount(1);
  await expect(momentum).not.toHaveAttribute("open", /.*/);

  // Your data: the two export links point at the Task 15 routes — read-only

  await expect(data.getByRole("link", { name: "Activities (CSV)" })).toHaveAttribute("href", "/api/export");

});
```

Create `tests/e2e/account-data-ops.spec.ts`:

```ts
import type { Page, Route } from "@playwright/test";
import { expect, freshIdentity, test } from "./fixtures";

// The account routes belong to the gateway, which `npm run dev` does not
// run: every /account/* request here is intercepted (the pattern of
// tests/e2e/session-ended-mid-save.spec.ts) and answered with the JSON the
// gateway sends (Tasks 12–14), so what is proven is the client half — the
// JSON each form posts, the sentence each code maps to, and where focus and
// the page go afterwards. The gateway half is tests/account-routes.test.mjs
// and the Docker run-check. A fresh identity: the demo has no self-service.

test.use({ identity: freshIdentity() });

type Json = Record<string, unknown>;
type Answer = { status: number; contentType: string; headers: Record<string, string>; body: string };

const json = (status: number, body: Json): Answer => ({
  status,
  contentType: "application/json; charset=utf-8",
  headers: { "cache-control": "no-store" },
  body: JSON.stringify(body),
});

const isAccountRoute = (url: URL) => url.pathname === "/account" || url.pathname.startsWith("/account/");

const DEFERRED =
  "Your account is marked for deletion; we’ll finish clearing it automatically. You’ve been signed out.";

// Answers /account/* by "<METHOD> <pathname>" — the object is read on every
// request, so a test may swap an entry between steps — and records each
// call so a test can assert what was (or was not) posted.
async function stubAccount(page: Page, answers: Record<string, (body: Json | null) => Answer>) {
  const calls: Array<{ key: string; body: Json | null }> = [];
  await page.route(isAccountRoute, async (route: Route) => {
    const request = route.request();
    const key = `${request.method()} ${new URL(request.url()).pathname}`;
    const body = request.method() === "POST" ? (request.postDataJSON() as Json) : null;
    calls.push({ key, body });
    const answer = answers[key];
    await route.fulfill(answer ? answer(body) : json(404, { error: "Not Found", code: "not_found" }));
  });
  return calls;
}

const infoFor = (me: { email: string; displayName: string }, mailConfigured: boolean) =>
  json(200, {
    email: me.email,
    identityEmail: me.email,
    displayName: me.displayName,
    pendingEmail: null,
    mailConfigured,
  });

test("the name form posts JSON and confirms the save", async ({ page, app }) => {
  const me = await app.account();
  const calls = await stubAccount(page, {
    "GET /account": () => infoFor(me, true),
    "POST /account/profile": (body) => json(200, { ok: true, displayName: String(body?.name ?? "") }),
  });
  await app.goto("/profile");
  const name = page.getByLabel("Display name", { exact: true });
  await name.fill("Renamed Person");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Save name" }).click();
  await expect(page.locator(".toast-region").getByText("Your name is saved.")).toBeVisible();
  expect(calls.filter((call) => call.key === "POST /account/profile").map((call) => call.body)).toEqual([
    { name: "Renamed Person" },
  ]);
  await expect(name).toHaveValue("Renamed Person");
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("the password sheet validates before posting and maps a wrong current password", async ({ page, app }) => {
  const me = await app.account();
  const answers: Record<string, (body: Json | null) => Answer> = {
    "GET /account": () => infoFor(me, true),
    "POST /account/password": () =>
      json(403, { error: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.", code: "password_incorrect" }),
  };
  const calls = await stubAccount(page, answers);
  await app.goto("/profile");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }).click();
  const sheet = app.dialog("Change password");
  await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
  await sheet.getByLabel("Current password", { exact: true }).fill("old-password-1");
  await sheet.getByLabel("New password", { exact: true }).fill("short");
  await sheet.getByLabel("Confirm new password", { exact: true }).fill("different");
  await sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }).click();
  const summary = sheet.getByRole("alert");
  await expect(summary).toContainText("Use at least 12 characters.");
  await expect(summary).toContainText("These don’t match.");
  expect(calls.filter((call) => call.key === "POST /account/password")).toEqual([]);

  await sheet.getByLabel("New password", { exact: true }).fill("a-longer-password-12");
  await sheet.getByLabel("Confirm new password", { exact: true }).fill("a-longer-password-12");
  await sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }).click();
  await expect(summary).toContainText("That password doesn’t match. Try again.");
  expect(calls.filter((call) => call.key === "POST /account/password").map((call) => call.body)).toEqual([
    { currentPassword: "old-password-1", newPassword: "a-longer-password-12" },
  ]);

  answers["POST /account/password"] = () => json(200, { ok: true });
  await sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Change password" }).click();
  await expect(sheet).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(
    page.locator(".toast-region").getByText("Password changed. Other devices were signed out."),
  ).toBeVisible();
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("the email sheet is disabled when mail is unconfigured and posts otherwise", async ({ page, app }) => {
  const me = await app.account();
  let mailConfigured = false;
  const calls = await stubAccount(page, {
    "GET /account": () => infoFor(me, mailConfigured),
    "POST /account/email": (body) =>
      json(200, { ok: true, pending: { newEmail: String(body?.newEmail ?? ""), expiresAt: 1_800_000_000_000 } }),
  });
  await app.goto("/profile");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Change email" }).click();
  let sheet = app.dialog("Change email");
  await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
  await expect(sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Send confirmation link" })).toBeDisabled();
  await expect(sheet.getByText("Email delivery is not set up yet; contact support@itrackceu.com")).toBeVisible();
  await page.keyboard.press("Escape");
  await expect(sheet).toHaveCount(0);

  mailConfigured = true;
  await app.goto("/profile");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Change email" }).click();
  sheet = app.dialog("Change email");
  await expect(sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Send confirmation link" })).toBeEnabled();
  await sheet.getByLabel("New email", { exact: true }).fill("new-address@example.test");
  await sheet.getByLabel("Current password", { exact: true }).fill("old-password-1");
  await sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Send confirmation link" }).click();
  await expect(sheet).toHaveCount(0);
  await expect(page.locator(".toast-region").getByText("Check the new address for a confirmation link.")).toBeVisible();
  const email = page.locator("#account-email");
  await expect(email).toContainText(
    `Check new-address@example.test for a confirmation link. Until you confirm, ${me.email} stays your sign-in.`,
  );

  await expect(email.getByRole("button", { name: "Cancel change" })).toBeVisible();
  expect(calls.filter((call) => call.key === "POST /account/email").map((call) => call.body)).toEqual([
    { newEmail: "new-address@example.test", password: "old-password-1" },
  ]);
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("delete stays disabled until the email matches, then posts and leaves", async ({ page, app }) => {
  const me = await app.account();
  const calls = await stubAccount(page, {
    "GET /account": () => infoFor(me, true),
    "POST /account/delete": () => json(200, { ok: true }),
  });
  await app.goto("/profile");
  await page.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete account…" }).click();
  const sheet = app.dialog("Delete this account");
  await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
  const confirm = sheet.getByRole("button", { name: "Delete my account" });
  await expect(confirm).toBeDisabled();
  const typed = sheet.getByLabel("Type your email to confirm", { exact: true });
  await typed.fill("someone-else@example.test");
  await expect(confirm).toBeDisabled();
  // Case-insensitive: the gateway lowercases before comparing.
  await typed.fill(me.email.toUpperCase());
  await expect(confirm).toBeEnabled();
  await sheet.getByLabel("Your password", { exact: true }).fill("old-password-1");
  await confirm.click();
  // The cookie is already cleared by the answer; the sheet leaves for the
  // landing page, which the dev server serves at "/".
  await page.waitForURL((url) => url.pathname === "/");
  expect(calls.filter((call) => call.key === "POST /account/delete").map((call) => call.body)).toEqual([
    { email: me.email.toUpperCase(), password: "old-password-1" },
  ]);
  app.expectNoErrors();
});

test("a deferred delete shows its sentence", async ({ page, app }) => {
  const me = await app.account();
  await stubAccount(page, {
    "GET /account": () => infoFor(me, true),

  await expect(sheet.getByRole("alert")).toContainText(DEFERRED);
  await expect(sheet).toBeVisible();
  app.expectNoErrors();
});
```

```tsx
  // The one-tap offer: only while the stored zone is the literal 'UTC' and the
  // device reports a real, different zone, and not after a "Not now" — in this
  // session (state) or on an earlier visit on this device (localStorage, read
  // at render time rather than synced from an effect — react-hooks/
  // set-state-in-effect; the read is idempotent, keyed on the account, and
  // never runs during SSR because `workspace` is fetched on the client).
  const [zoneOfferDismissed, setZoneOfferDismissed] = useState(false);
  const draftStorageNamespace = workspace?.user.draftStorageNamespace;
  const zoneOfferDismissedEarlier = useMemo(() => {
    if (!draftStorageNamespace) return false;
    try {
      return (
        window.localStorage.getItem(zoneOfferStorageKey(draftStorageNamespace)) ===
        deviceTimeZone()
      );
    } catch {
      return false;
    }
  }, [draftStorageNamespace]);
  const storedZone = workspace?.reminderPreferences.timeZone ?? null;
  const zoneSuggestion = useMemo(() => {
    if (storedZone === null || zoneOfferDismissed || zoneOfferDismissedEarlier) return null;
    return deviceZoneSuggestion(storedZone, deviceTimeZone());
  }, [storedZone, zoneOfferDismissed, zoneOfferDismissedEarlier]);
  const dismissZoneOffer = useCallback(() => {
    if (draftStorageNamespace) {
      try {
        window.localStorage.setItem(
          zoneOfferStorageKey(draftStorageNamespace),
          deviceTimeZone(),
        );
      } catch {
        // Private mode or a full store: the offer simply returns next load.
      }
    }
    setZoneOfferDismissed(true);
  }, [draftStorageNamespace]);

  // `?notice=` is the gateway's one-word answer after an email change is
  // confirmed on /verify (Task 14: 303 /profile?notice=email-changed). Read
  // once after mount, deferred like every launch effect, then scrubbed so a
  // reload never repeats the toast. `?delivery=` (useReminderLaunch) never
  // shares a URL with it, so scrubbing here cannot lose a push launch.
  const [accountNotice, setAccountNotice] = useState<AccountNotice | null>(null);
  const clearAccountNotice = useCallback(() => setAccountNotice(null), []);
  const scrubQuery = nav.scrubQuery;
  useEffect(() => {
    const timer = window.setTimeout(() => {
      const notice = new URLSearchParams(window.location.search).get("notice");
      if (notice !== "email-changed") return;
      setAccountNotice("email-changed");
      scrubQuery();
    }, 0);
```

- [ ] **Step 4: `app/screens/account/useAccountApi.ts` — the gateway client with its own code → copy map**

```ts
"use client";

import { useMemo } from "react";
import { readApiResponse } from "../../lib/apiResponse";
import { useWorkspace } from "../../lib/workspaceStore";

// The Account screen's client for the gateway's JSON routes (Tasks 12–14).
// They are not workspace actions — no revision, no refetch, no undo — and
// their codes are the gateway's, so the code → copy map lives here rather
// than in app/lib/copy.ts (whose ERROR_COPY is proven against the worker's
// codes). Nothing here reads Response.json(): readApiResponse is the one
// reader, and its "session-ended" is the same 401 path /api/workspace takes.
// A sheet renders `message`, never `error` — a gateway sentence is never
// the visible one (spec §6).

export type AccountResult<T> =
  | { ok: true; data: T }
  | { ok: false; code: string; message: string };

export type PendingEmail = { newEmail: string; expiresAt: number };

export type AccountInfo = {
  email: string;
  identityEmail: string;
  displayName: string;
  pendingEmail: PendingEmail | null;
  mailConfigured: boolean;
};

export type AccountOk = { ok: true };

export const ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE = "That didn’t save. Try again.";

// Copy table section G. Keys are the codes deploy/railway/account-routes.mjs
// answers with; anything else falls back to ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE.
export const ACCOUNT_ERROR_COPY: Readonly<Record<string, string>> = {
  email_mismatch: "That isn’t the email on this account.",
  password_incorrect: "That password doesn’t match. Try again.",
  password_policy: "Use at least 12 characters.",
  name_invalid: "Use 1 to 80 characters for your name.",
  invalid_email: "Enter a valid email address.",
  same_email: "That is already your email.",
  mail_unconfigured: "Email delivery is not set up yet; contact support@itrackceu.com",
  rate_limited: "Too many attempts. Wait 15 minutes and try again.",
  delete_deferred:
    "Your account is marked for deletion; we’ll finish clearing it automatically. You’ve been signed out.",
};

export function accountErrorMessage(code: string | null | undefined): string {
  return (code && ACCOUNT_ERROR_COPY[code]) || ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE;
}

type Envelope = { ok?: boolean; error?: string; code?: string };

type Call =
  | { method: "GET" }
  | { method: "POST"; body: Record<string, unknown> };

export function useAccountApi() {
  const { sessionEnded } = useWorkspace();
  return useMemo(() => {
    async function call<T>(path: string, init: Call): Promise<AccountResult<T>> {
      let response: Response;
      try {
        response = await fetch(path, {
          method: init.method,
          credentials: "same-origin",
          headers:
            init.method === "POST"
              ? { accept: "application/json", "content-type": "application/json" }
              : { accept: "application/json" },
          body: init.method === "POST" ? JSON.stringify(init.body) : undefined,
        });
      } catch {
        return { ok: false, code: "offline", message: ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE };
      }
      const parsed = await readApiResponse<T & Envelope>(response);
      if (parsed.kind === "session-ended") {
        sessionEnded();
        return { ok: false, code: "authentication_required", message: ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE };
      }
      if (parsed.kind === "unexpected") {
        return { ok: false, code: "unexpected", message: ACCOUNT_FALLBACK_MESSAGE };
      }
      if (!parsed.ok) {
        const code = parsed.data.code ?? null;
        return { ok: false, code: code ?? "unknown", message: accountErrorMessage(code) };
      }
      return { ok: true, data: parsed.data };
    }

    return {
      load: () => call<AccountInfo>("/account", { method: "GET" }),
      profile: (name: string) =>
        call<{ displayName: string }>("/account/profile", { method: "POST", body: { name } }),
      password: (currentPassword: string, newPassword: string) =>
        call<AccountOk>("/account/password", { method: "POST", body: { currentPassword, newPassword } }),
      email: (newEmail: string, password: string) =>
        call<{ pending: PendingEmail }>("/account/email", { method: "POST", body: { newEmail, password } }),
      cancelEmail: () => call<AccountOk>("/account/email/cancel", { method: "POST", body: {} }),
      remove: (email: string, password: string) =>
        call<AccountOk>("/account/delete", { method: "POST", body: { email, password } }),
    };
  }, [sessionEnded]);
}

export type AccountApi = ReturnType<typeof useAccountApi>;
```
